evaluations.title: Equal-spacing barrier baseline
evaluations.author: System
evaluations.abstract: Simple equal-weight, equal-spacing construction. It approaches the classical 1.5 barrier and is intended as a working format seed.

evaluations.title: Mapping experiment: exact scorer + equal-spacing sweep + local optimization
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable exact scorer matching the evaluator, map how the equal-weight/equal-spacing score depends on spacing and n, and run black-box local optimization from baseline to probe whether and how the 1.5 barrier can be exceeded.

evaluations.title: Two-scale / clustered constructions to break the 1.5 barrier toward the HL weak-(1,1) constant
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Test the hypothesis that the task score equals the sublevel measure of the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal function, whose maximal value is the weak-(1,1) constant C=(11+sqrt(61))/12≈1.56752. Search two-scale/clustered and recursive-block (y,k) configurations to exceed the equal-spacing 1.5 ceiling and approach C, and compare optimized structures to the analytic target.

evaluations.title: Landscape survey: construction families for interval-union score
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: A broad bounded survey mapping how different construction families (geometric spacing, power-law weights, two-scale/hierarchical, and free numerical optimization) score on the Hardy-Littlewood interval-union lower bound. Goal is to characterize the landscape and find any construction beating the 1.496 equal-spacing baseline, not yet to reach the target.

evaluations.title: Grid Search over Periodic Clustered Sequences
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates sequences formed by blocks of points with a small intra-gap, separated by a larger inter-gap.

evaluations.title: Grid Search over Geometric Progressions
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates sequences where both weights and gaps between points follow geometric progressions.

evaluations.title: Small-n global optima and self-similar tilings: extracting the extremal building block beyond 1.5
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Equal spacing is a strong local optimum at 1.5; to approach the centered HL weak-(1,1) constant C=(11+sqrt61)/12 we need the genuine multi-scale extremal structure. Find near-global optima of the exact score at small n via heavy multistart global optimization, extract the optimal building-block geometry (gap and weight patterns), and test self-similar/geometric tilings to see whether the score climbs above 1.5 toward C.

evaluations.title: Core-plus-arms graded measures: testing the span vs extension tradeoff to beat 1.5
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the derived mechanism that beating the 1.5 ceiling requires a multi-scale measure combining a concentrated core (covering points beyond the support via large centered windows) with spread arms (covering a long support region). Constructs graded-weight and hierarchical core-plus-arms measures and optimizes the core-mass-versus-spread tradeoff against the exact score.

evaluations.title: Optimization of Cantor-like Fractal Spacing
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes 7 continuous gap parameters for a Cantor-like hierarchical sequence (N=128) using differential evolution.

evaluations.title: Heavy-core geometric cascade: breaking the 1.5 barrier
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Tests a structurally non-uniform family motivated by reframing the task as the centered-maximal level-1 super-level set of a discrete measure. A heavy central atom flanked by symmetric geometrically-scaled lighter atoms (both gaps and weights scaling by ratio lambda) is conjectured to harvest extra covered length per unit mass via long-span intervals, potentially exceeding the equal-spacing 1.5 local optimum. We derive/measure the score as a function of lambda and cell shape and search broadly, including the regime near the quadratic root (11-sqrt61)/12 ~ 0.266.

evaluations.title: Faithful interval-union diagnostics foundation
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable faithful scorer and diagnostic suite for Hardy-Littlewood interval-union constructions, validate it against the system equal-spacing baseline, and save baseline structural diagnostics for future mechanism-driven searches. This is a non-score foundational evaluation.

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Free Optimization for Small N
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Performs unconstrained continuous optimization of all gaps and weights for small N (3 to 8) to discover the fundamental optimal motif.

evaluations.title: Bridge-LP and periodic motif survey
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable evaluator/diagnostic harness and run a bounded survey for mechanisms beyond the adjacent-pair equal-spacing chain. The main test is a one-bridge-per-gap linear-programming sufficient model; a lightweight periodic motif search acts as a comparator. The evaluation should return the best valid construction found and save candidates/logs for later analysis.

evaluations.title: Small-n global optima: locating the structure that beats 1.5
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Two single-scale families (geometric cascade, clusters) collapse to the gap-3 uniform ridge, which analysis shows is a strict local maximum at score 1.5. The conjectured sharp value (11+sqrt61)/12~1.5675 must lie in a different basin unreachable by smooth descent from uniform. This experiment finds, as exactly as feasible, the global optimum for small n (3..14) via heavy multistart global optimization with deliberately diverse non-uniform seeds, then reports the optimal (y,k) PROFILE so we can identify the extremal structure rather than guess an ansatz.

evaluations.title: Multi-level self-similar cascade: many-scale hierarchy to climb past 1.5 toward C
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Small-n optima are exactly equal spacing (1.5-1/2n) and all 2-scale variants collapse, so exceeding 1.5 must be a many-scale phenomenon. This experiment builds a genuine multi-level self-similar cascade measure with few structural parameters but large generated n, and optimizes those parameters against the exact score to find the first construction exceeding 1.5 and to reveal the recursive structure underlying C=(11+sqrt61)/12 (which solves 12C^2-22C+5=0).

evaluations.title: Parametric Optimization of Two-State Sturmian and Periodic Words
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates two-letter word structures by mapping them to weights {1.0, W} and setting gaps deterministically via g_i = C*(k_i + k_{i+1}).

evaluations.title: Differentiable Relaxation (Soft Union) - N=16
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Implements a differentiable approximation of the interval union using sigmoids evaluated over a dense grid. We use gradient descent to optimize small sequences (N=16) from scratch to discover emergent natural structures without human bias.

evaluations.title: Level-dependent self-similar cascade: per-level optimization to climb from 1.516 toward C
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: The depth-4 central-mass cascade reached 1.516 but deeper depths underperformed due to a single shared parameter set and pruned grids. This experiment re-optimizes the cascade with level-dependent parameters (p_l, g_l, beta_l) and proper per-depth optimization seeded from the working solution, aiming to make the depth trend monotone, measure the per-level deficit decay toward C=(11+sqrt61)/12, and exceed targets 1.534 then 1.56.

evaluations.title: Mechanism test: periodic cell vs recursive self-similar construction
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Small-n optima are gap-3 uniform interior plus a vanishing O(1/n) boundary bonus, so they remain in the 1.5 basin. To beat 1.5 asymptotically requires an INTENSIVE (bulk) mechanism. This experiment discriminates two candidates: (A) a translation-periodic cell of p atoms with non-uniform within-cell weights/gaps, tiled to large n; and (B) a recursive self-similar construction with decoupled spatial ratio lambda and mass ratio mu, measured as a function of recursion depth. The key diagnostic is whether bulk score INCREASES with tiling count R (mechanism A) or recursion depth K (mechanism B), distinguishing a genuine intensive gain from a vanishing boundary effect.

evaluations.title: Periodic local-family map with exposure diagnostics
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Use the Eval #11 diagnostic tooling to sweep and optimize small-period weight/gap patterns repeated to large n, measuring whether any simple periodic family escapes the equal-spacing local tiling through nonlocal exposed intervals. This is primarily a calibration and mapping evaluation.

evaluations.title: Active-set interval tiling LP probe
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Test a looser structural model than Eval #13: choose ordered words of support intervals whose generated intervals cover consecutive pieces of a long component. This probes multi-interval gap coverage and active tilings that the one-bridge-per-gap LP model excludes.

evaluations.title: Periodic Block Optimization of Weights and Gaps
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes a repeating block of B weights and B gaps to find a periodic structural motif that beats uniform spacing.

evaluations.title: Analytic self-similar fixed point: rederive C as a transfer-matrix eigenvalue
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the symmetric central-mass cascade has an exact self-similar fixed point whose per-unit-mass coverage ratio equals C=(11+sqrt61)/12, the larger root of 12f^2-22f+5=0. Sets up the level-to-level recursion in two carried quantities (covered length and outward reach), solves the fixed-point equations symbolically/numerically, and checks whether the eigenvalues of the linearized 2x2 map are the two roots (11±sqrt61)/12, giving a first-principles rederivation of the ceiling and the convergence rate.

evaluations.title: Fractal Parameterization (m=4) - DFO
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Explores a recursive fractal structure mimicking a singular continuous measure. A base template of m=4 points is recursively expanded to depth 4 (N=256). The 8 template parameters (gaps, weights, and a spatial contraction factor) are optimized using SciPy's differential_evolution evaluated on the exact discrete interval union score.

evaluations.title: Transformed-path sawtooth and reset sweep v1
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Search directly in transformed variables a_i = y_i - 2K_prefix[i] and positive weights k_i for high-drift paths with reset/fold events, testing whether nonlocal active blocks can expose useful union length beyond the equal-spacing local tiling.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Polynomial Profile (N=128) - DFO
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the sequence using a symmetric exponential-polynomial profile to explicitly model boundary edge-effects (heavy edges, clustered gaps) while maintaining a smooth interior. Optimizes the 7 polynomial coefficients using SciPy's differential_evolution.

evaluations.title: Profile-guided recursive cluster composition survey
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether dense or structured clusters can be composed with profile-guided intercluster gaps so that longer cross-cluster blocks expose useful union length. This follows Eval #13 and Eval #21, which did not find improvements from one-bridge-per-gap LPs, small-period motifs, or bounded active tiling words.

evaluations.title: Generalized self-similar families: branching, central clusters, asymmetry — reach C
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: The symmetric binary central-mass cascade converges to a limit ~1.5549, below C=(11+sqrt61)/12. This experiment generalizes the self-similar block family along three axes - branching factor (children per node), central cluster size, and asymmetry - with level-dependent optimization, to find a family whose limiting per-unit-mass coverage ratio exceeds 1.56 and approaches C, and to characterize which structural degree of freedom unlocks the remaining gap.

evaluations.title: Free local refinement seeded from best cascade: push score past 1.56
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Directly maximize the exact score by free local optimization (block-coordinate ascent and CMA on log-gaps/log-weights) seeded from the best level-dependent cascade configurations (depth 7 n=255 and depth 8 n=511, score 1.551). Goal: escape the binary self-similar manifold and cross the 1.56 target by letting all positions and weights move freely.

evaluations.title: Large-Scale JAX Optimization for Melas Constant Motif
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes up to N=128 using an exactly differentiable JAX interval union length algorithm to discover the true algebraic structural motif yielding the (11+sqrt(61))/12 limit.

evaluations.title: Maximal-function view: free optimization with unbounded weights + Melas-shape probe
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Established rigorously that the covered set equals the level-1/2 super-level set of the centered (average-normalized) Hardy-Littlewood maximal function of the discrete measure, so the sharp score is exactly Melas's constant C=(11+sqrt61)/12. Periodic constructions provably cap at 1.5; the extremizer is aperiodic. This experiment runs a focused, well-resourced free optimization with UNBOUNDED weight dynamic range at moderate n, seeded from non-uniform/graded profiles, and reports the maximal-function profile of the best solution to reveal the extremal structure. Goal: produce a finite witness exceeding 1.5 and learn the shape that approaches C.

evaluations.title: High-Resolution Contour Map of Fast-Growing Geometric Sequences
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates geometric sequences where weights and gaps grow by exactly the same ratio r (up to r=100) to find the asymptotic maximum.

evaluations.title: Small-N Exact Symmetric DFO (N=32)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Finds the exact optimal geometry for N=32 by directly optimizing the parameters using Differential Evolution without any structural assumptions (like polynomials or fractals). Enforces only symmetry to halve the dimensionality to 32 parameters.

evaluations.title: Equal-lattice defect motif search v1
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Search for finite nonuniform motifs embedded in equal-spacing tails that produce positive local excess over the baseline tiling, testing whether designed courtyards/endcaps/folds can let longer blocks add union length without the global score collapse seen in reset sweeps.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Geometric Progression (N=128) - DFO
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Parameterizes the sequence as a symmetric geometric progression decaying or growing from the center. This 4-parameter model explicitly tests the hypothesis that the extremal finite sequence mimics the theoretical extremal measure of the uncentered maximal operator. It strictly contains the uniform 1.496 baseline.

evaluations.title: Numba-Accelerated Macroscopic Cluster Optimization
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes finite cluster motifs (M clusters, K points each) using a highly optimized Numba scorer to explicitly construct the optimal discrete point-mass measure.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric self-similar block from scratch: search for a family limit above 1.56
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: The symmetric binary central-mass cascade has limit ~1.5549 < C, so it cannot reach 1.56. Eval #28's near-zero asymmetry was a local artifact of seeding from the symmetric optimum. This experiment builds a fully asymmetric self-similar block (central mass plus left/right children with independent masses, offsets, and scales) and globally optimizes it from many random starts, fitting the limiting ratio to find whether an asymmetric family exceeds 1.56 and approaches C.

evaluations.title: Free large-n optimization via the maximal-function covered-set view (JAX gradient + grid)
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Escape the binary self-similar manifold by optimizing positions and weights freely at large n using the covered-set / centered-maximal-function reformulation. Build a differentiable surrogate of the covered length on a fine grid, optimize with JAX gradients from diverse multi-scale initializations, then evaluate exactly. Goal: cross 1.56 or reveal the structure of higher-scoring non-self-similar configurations.

evaluations.title: Sparse-marker periodic motif optimizer
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Probe an escape route suggested by the active-tiling results: near-zero-weight marker points can make longer intervals expose real union length, but prior small LP words paid too much for it. This evaluation explicitly searches periodic and active-inspired motifs with ghost weights using exact-score optimization and active interval diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Heavy core + graded-density tail: the reach-amplification mechanism
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: All prior families cap at 1.5 because they sit at local density ~1/3, where the maximal function can only reach the 1/2 threshold via local singleton/pair bridging (provably capped at 1.5). Large-radius coverage requires density >=1/2 regions. Hand analysis shows a heavy core atom of mass m plus a tail of density rho<1/2 amplifies the core's coverage reach from m to m/(1-2rho): a tail point x is covered via the centered interval reaching back to the core when m+2*rho*x >= x. A uniform tail breaks even at score 1, but a GRADED decreasing-density tail can let inner mass be covered

evaluations.title: Boundary-Modulated Uniform Core (N=128)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Explicitly tests the hypothesis that the 1.496 uniform baseline wastes coverage at the boundaries. Fixes the central 112 points to the uniform baseline (gap=3.0, weight=1.0) and optimizes only the 8 symmetric boundary points (weights and gaps) using Differential Evolution to isolate and resolve edge inefficiencies.

evaluations.title: Large-Scale CMA-ES Optimization of Unconstrained Coordinates
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Uses CMA-ES and a Numba-compiled exact scorer to robustly optimize large unconstrained sequences (N=64, 128) without JAX sorting artifacts.

evaluations.title: Periodic Motif Search (P=2 to 8)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for a repeating structural motif (period P=2 to 8) that breaks the 1.5 uniform barrier. For each P, optimizes the 2P-1 parameters of the cell and repeats it to N=128, testing if complex repeating structures tile the real line more efficiently than the uniform sequence.

evaluations.title: Barrier-crossing search: unit-weight gaps, annealing, and inverse threshold design
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Five construction families all collapse to local density 1/3 (score 1.5). Clean reformulation: with disjoint singletons, score = 1 + gapfill/(2W); beating 1.5 requires total gap-fill length to exceed total weight, and uniform gap-3 hits exactly the break-even ratio 1. This experiment attacks the barrier three ways: (A) the clean UNIT-WEIGHT variable-gap problem (optimize only positions, weights all equal) at several n with strong global search; (B) large-n simulated annealing / basin hopping with STRUCTURAL moves (multiplicative gap perturbations, atom insert/delete/merge, slowly-varying gap/weight envelopes) explicitly engineered to cross the 1.5 barrier from aperiodic seeds; (C) an inverse 'threshold-hugging' design that

evaluations.title: Coverage-waste diagnostic: where does the cascade lose efficiency vs C?
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: To understand why the binary central-mass cascade plateaus below C=(11+sqrt61)/12, decompose its covered set: measure total overlap (redundant double-coverage), the over-threshold slack profile of the centered maximal function, and which interval windows determine the boundary of the covered set, across depths 4-8. Goal: localize where coverage efficiency is lost and produce mechanistic, decision-changing insight on the gap to C.

evaluations.title: Forward-greedy threshold-saturation atomic builder: a new construction principle for >1.56
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Self-similar trees plateau below 1.56. Based on the atomic gap-bridging view, this experiment builds constructions by a forward-greedy rule: starting from a heavy center, repeatedly place the next atom (position and weight) so as to extend the covered set as far as possible per unit added mass while keeping the centered maximal function at threshold (no over-coverage waste). Optimize the few rule parameters and compare to the cascade, targeting a point-efficient construction exceeding 1.56.

evaluations.title: Two-scale clustered lattice sweep v1
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Probe repeated clustered constructions with dense internal modules and larger intercluster gaps, testing whether dense mass can be amortized across cross-cluster intervals while internal coverage preserves span efficiency. This expands beyond small-period periodic search and isolated defects.

evaluations.title: Exact PyTorch AutoDiff (N=128)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Implements the exact interval union length as a differentiable PyTorch function using `torch.sort`. Initializes N=128 at the 1.496 uniform baseline and uses Adam to follow exact subgradients to deform the sequence towards the optimal topology.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Spline Profile Optimization
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes the macroscopic density profile of the sequence using a 30-parameter symmetric linear spline to find the scale-free Melas constant configuration for N=250.

evaluations.title: Targeted refinement of ghost-heavy-tail motifs
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Refine the first positive sparse-marker signal from Eval #39: a period-11 G H^8 T^2 motif with tiny ghost weight and one-third tail weights. This evaluation searches the structured ghost-heavy-tail family, tests scaling and phase effects, and tries to determine whether the small improvement over equal spacing is a repeatable mechanism or a finite boundary/phase artifact.

evaluations.title: Stabilized Symmetric JAX Optimization
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Uses a numerically stable, exact JAX surrogate to optimize symmetric log-weights and log-gaps for N=128 to achieve the 1.5675 Melas constant.

evaluations.title: Soft Geometric Progression (N=128) - Plateau Escape
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Combines the PyTorch Differentiable Relaxation (Soft Union) with the 4-parameter Symmetric Geometric Progression. Solves the 'Piecewise Plateau Trap' by using the smooth gradients of the soft surrogate to push the geometric ratios away from the flat uniform baseline, while tracking the exact score.

evaluations.title: Scale-splice motifs and defect-excess test
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize the Eval #50 ghost-heavy-tail motif as a scale splice: cheap endpoint handles plus transitions between equal chains of different weight scales. Search nested tails, two-ghost handles, and down-up scale cycles, and test whether splice gadgets have positive bulk excess when embedded as defects in long equal chains.

evaluations.title: Exponential self-similar law + numerical Melas extremizer + reach diagnostic
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Six construction families cap at score 1.5. This experiment tests two untested canonical objects and a new diagnostic. (a) The pure exponential self-similar law y_i=R^i, k_i=c*R^i (one atom per log-unit, the natural RG fixed point; distinct from the additive cascade in Eval #9), scanned finely over (R,c) with a bulk-vs-truncation analysis. (b) A direct large-n numerical solution of the continuous Melas variational extremizer for |{M mu>=1/2}|/(2||mu||), via projected-gradient / coordinate ascent on (y,k) with up to ~600-1000 atoms seeded from diverse profiles, reporting the SHAPE and maximal-function profile of the best measure. (c) A reach/excursion diagnostic computing per-anchor rightward reach

evaluations.title: Power-law and free scale-profile measures (from scratch): does the limit reach C?
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: The binary cascade mis-allocates mass across scales (Eval #45: slack trapped at the heavy core, boundary reach starved), and its self-similar limit ~1.5549 is below C. This experiment tests scale-continuous atomic families - power-law gaps/weights and a free per-scale mass profile - initialized FROM SCRATCH (no cascade seed), to determine whether a better mass-across-scales allocation raises the achievable score and whether the family's fitted limit approaches C=(11+sqrt61)/12.

evaluations.title: Slack-redistribution optimizer: move trapped core slack to starved boundary
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Diagnostic #45 showed the binary cascade traps ~80% of its over-threshold slack near the heavy core while the boundary reach is starved by tiny leaf mass. This experiment directly attacks that mis-allocation: starting from the best cascade, iteratively move mass from high-slack (over-covered) core regions to low-slack boundary regions, re-optimizing to convert trapped slack into new covered length, testing whether targeted scale-reallocation crosses 1.56.

evaluations.title: Medium-block contact schedule LP search v1
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Search periodic contact schedules where each adjacent gap is bridged by a selected block of length 2-8, using linear programming to maximize cell span under exact bridge/contact constraints, then evaluate repeated constructions exactly. This tests whether medium block lengths can improve over the equal-spacing pair-bridge tiling without heavy-reset or cluster collapse.

evaluations.title: Geometric Progression: Edge-Heavy vs Center-Heavy
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Splits the geometric progression search space into two strictly disjoint regimes: Center-Heavy (decaying towards edges) and Edge-Heavy (growing towards edges). Runs two separate DFO searches to conclusively determine which topological phase contains the higher score.

evaluations.title: Extraction of Recursive Ratios from Optimal JAX Configuration
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the exact values and ratios of weights and gaps from the Eval 51 optimal sequence to derive the algebraic recursive law governing the Melas constant.

evaluations.title: Weights-on-fixed-grid optimization: best mass allocation exploiting linearity in weights
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Coverage of a point by a window is a LINEAR inequality in the atom weights, so for fixed atom positions the construction has exploitable linear-programming substructure absent in tree parametrizations. This experiment fixes positions on fine geometric/multi-scale grids and optimizes only the weights (via LP-flavored alternating methods and CMA), across several grid resolutions, to find the best mass allocation without tree constraints and to fit the limit versus C.

evaluations.title: Unified limit-fitting analysis across construction families vs C
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Consolidates a rigorous limit-fitting analysis across all construction families explored (binary cascade, asymmetric tree, power-law/spline scale-profiles, slack-reallocated cascade) to quantify each family's extrapolated finite-n score limit with confidence intervals, providing a defensible, decision-changing assessment of how close each family gets to the centered HL weak-(1,1) constant C and which structural assumptions cap the score below C.

evaluations.title: Geometric Progression: Edge-Heavy (N=128)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Completes the Edge-Heavy vs Center-Heavy topological split. Optimizes a 4-parameter symmetric geometric progression restricted to growing outwards (edge-heavy) to see if massive boundary anchors surpass the uniform baseline.

evaluations.title: Small-N Exact Symmetric DFO (N=16)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Searches for the exact discrete extremal sequence for N=16. By optimizing 16 symmetric parameters using DFO with a uniform baseline incumbent, we aim to beat the N=16 uniform score (1.46875) and reverse-engineer the exact recurrence relation.

evaluations.title: Equal-weight irregular gap choreography search v1
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Search over equal-weight constructions with irregular gap sequences, using exact scoring and evolutionary/annealing methods to test whether medium-block choreography can beat equal spacing without the denominator cost and extreme weight ratios seen in previous weighted mechanisms.

evaluations.title: Scale-bump continuation: growing the graded optimum toward the sharp constant
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Key observation from my exact small-n global optima (Eval #14): the true optima are NOT gap-3 uniform but symmetric graded 'scale bumps' (weights rising from edges to center, local gap/weight ratio ~3 maintained). Their scores n=5:1.4267, n=8:1.4577, n=14:1.4815 fit score ~ C - 0.31/sqrt(n) with C=(11+sqrt61)/12~1.5675, i.e. they approach the SHARP constant, NOT 1.5. By contrast all large-n constructions found by free optimization collapse to the inferior gap-3 basin (->1.5 from below ~1/(2n)). Hypothesis: the scale-bump is the correct extremal basin; free optimization destroys it at large n by collapsing to uniform. This experiment uses HOMOTOPY CONTINUATION (grow n slowly,

evaluations.title: Small-n exact global optimization survey
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Pivot away from the scale-splice family and run a less-structured exact-score optimization survey over finite configurations. The goal is to find or characterize non-periodic small/medium-n motifs that our LP, sparse-marker, and cluster searches may have missed, with active-interval diagnostics for any promising candidate.

evaluations.title: Asymmetric Small-N DFO (N=12)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypothesis that the extremal sequence spontaneously breaks symmetry. Runs a completely unconstrained, asymmetric DFO search for N=12 to see if an asymmetric configuration can beat the uniform baseline.

evaluations.title: Equioscillation construction: drive all between-atom maximal-function minima to 1/2
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: The cascade wastes mass holding the centered maximal function far above 1/2 near its heavy core (Eval #45). The extremal principle should be equioscillation: positions and weights chosen so every between-atom local minimum of M_c mu equals exactly 1/2 (no gaps, no over-coverage). This experiment constructs such configurations by constrained optimization - maximize covered length per mass subject to M_c mu >= 1/2 everywhere, driving the minima down to 1/2 - and tests whether eliminating core over-coverage beats the 1.5518 plateau and raises the limit above 1.5549.

evaluations.title: Intensive global optimization at small-to-moderate n: true optima and score-vs-n ladder
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: At n=31 the central-mass cascade already reaches 1.516, far above equal spacing's 1.484, so small-n optima are nontrivial and weight-dependent. This experiment runs heavy global optimization (many methods, many restarts) at n=7,11,15,21,31,45,63 to characterize the true near-global optimum at each n, its structure, and a clean exact score-vs-n ladder, providing the cleanest data for the limit question and the paper.

evaluations.title: Multi-component active-piece LP search
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Search a more general active-set linear model than prior one-component tiling: choose ordered exposed pieces, each contained in a selected generated interval I(i,j), allow gaps between pieces, and maximize total certified covered length. This targets disconnected peak-system patterns that exact optimization and one-component LPs may miss.

evaluations.title: Free finite exact-optimizer survey v1
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Run a broad exact-scoring stochastic optimization survey over finite y,k constructions with moderate n, using multiple parameterizations and optimizers to discover candidate templates not captured by periodic, reset, defect, cluster, contact-schedule, or equal-weight searches.

evaluations.title: Grid Search over Symmetric Two-Sided Geometric Progressions
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates symmetric, two-sided geometric progressions with a heavy central core and decaying tails to hit the Melas constant.

evaluations.title: Medium-n exact optima with coverage-ratio decomposition diagnostic
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Eight construction families converge to 1.5, yet a witness with score >1.534 provably exists at n<=1000. My partition-based hand arguments (pair-fill ratio<=3, long-block ratio<=2) keep yielding <=1.5, which means they miss how atom mass is SHARED across overlapping coverage contributions at different block orders. This experiment runs high-budget EXACT global optimization at medium n (n=10..30) and, crucially, instruments the best constructions with a per-point coverage decomposition: for each covered point, which block [i,j] (and its order j-i+1) provides coverage, and the local 'efficiency ratio'. The goal is mechanistic: empirically map where coverage comes from in the best optima, whether any

evaluations.title: Deep Zoom Geometric Progression (N=1000)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Tests the 'Suspension Bridge' hypothesis: that breaking 1.5 strictly requires a large sequence length (N=1000) to offset the boundary penalty. Optimizes a 4-parameter symmetric geometric progression with bounds tightly zoomed around the uniform baseline to find delicate efficiency gains.

evaluations.title: Massive Scale Symmetric JAX Optimization (N=256)
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the stabilized symmetric JAX optimization to N=256 to break the 1.534 target threshold using XLA fori_loop acceleration.

evaluations.title: Exact equioscillation solver via Newton/continuation: can flattening M_c to 1/2 beat the 1.5549 limit?
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #68 confirmed the best construction is not equioscillated (M_c minima range 0.48-0.62, heavy center) but its penalty optimizer used sampled minima and could not flatten the profile. This experiment uses EXACT between-atom minima and a Newton/continuation solver to drive every local minimum of the centered maximal function to exactly 1/2 while maximizing covered length per mass, at moderate n where exact enumeration is feasible, then fits the limit to test whether true equioscillation exceeds the cascade limit ~1.5549 toward C=(11+sqrt61)/12.

evaluations.title: One-Way Geometric Progression Grid Search (N=128)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Performs a high-resolution 2D grid search over the parameters (r, c) of a one-way geometric progression. This explicitly bypasses the zero-gradient plateaus that trap DFO optimizers and tests the hypothesis that the extremal sequence breaks symmetry entirely.

evaluations.title: Surplus accounting and bulk-slope diagnostics
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable diagnostic for the payment problem observed across Ariadne evaluations. Decompose candidates by excess U-3K, pair-only union length, long-block marginal contribution, overpair gap burden, and repeat-count bulk slope. This is an analysis/tool evaluation; it returns the current best fallback construction while producing artifacts to guide future searches.

evaluations.title: Sharp-constant source-tile contact graph search v1
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Reformulate the task as a centered maximal-function halo problem and search generalized contact graphs where arbitrary selected source intervals tile the halo, rather than forcing one bridge per physical gap. This aims to reverse-engineer templates related to the guardrail constant (11+sqrt(61))/12.

evaluations.title: Taut-frame / marginal-coverage equalization: fleeing the gap-3 kink
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Nine families converge to score 1.5. Diagnosis (Eval #73): the gap-3 plateau is a NON-SMOOTH kink where adding mass yields zero new coverage, so score-maximizers stall there. The KKT condition for a true interior optimum is d|U|/dk_i = 2*score equalized across atoms (marginal coverage 2C~3.135 > 3). This experiment abandons direct score maximization and instead applies a marginal-coverage EQUALIZATION fixed-point flow plus a 'taut-frame' construction that places atoms so many block-intervals sit exactly at their nonemptiness threshold simultaneously (a jammed state), explicitly seeking the near-critical aperiodic configuration that classical optimizers miss. Goal: reach a configuration with equalized marginal coverage exceeding

evaluations.title: Batched Exact AutoDiff Search (N=64, B=2048)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates 2048 parallel topological trajectories using exact PyTorch subgradients to hunt for the elusive >1.5 valley without human-biased parameterizations.

evaluations.title: Grid Search over Decaying Symmetric Geometric Sequences
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a strictly decaying symmetric geometric sequence where both weights and gaps scale by the same ratio r < 1.

evaluations.title: Recurrence and self-similar ansatz search v1
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Test low-dimensional non-periodic and multiscale construction families motivated by the failure of single-scale searches: geometric/symmetric recurrence weights and gaps, contact-threshold gap recurrences, nested medium-block gap surgeries, and simple recursive boundary-reservoir modules.

evaluations.title: Shoulder-recursion, from-empty greedy set-cover, and covering-LP dual
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Ten construction families cap at score 1.5. Eval #80 showed shoulder/transition atoms reach marginal coverage 3.5-4 (>3) while bulk sits at exactly 3 (kink). This experiment tries three methods designed to escape my forward-construction bias. (1) SHOULDER-RECURSION: a self-similar 'bump-of-bumps' that recursively replaces high-marginal shoulder regions (NOT gaps, unlike the failed Eval #19) with scaled copies, testing whether 'all-shoulder at every scale' beats 1.5 or washes out. (2) FROM-EMPTY GREEDY set-cover: incrementally add mass where marginal covered-length-per-mass is highest, starting from nothing. (3) COVERING-LP heuristic: minimize total mass to keep the centered maximal function >=1/2 on an interval via column

evaluations.title: Many-scale, few-atoms-per-scale ladders: escape the dyadic scale-budget bottleneck toward C
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Binary trees spend 2^depth atoms for only depth scales, capping the scale-count at ~10 for n<=1000 and leaving deficits ~n^-0.38 that cannot reveal the asymptote. This experiment builds measures with MANY scales but few atoms per scale (geometric single-atom ladders and lightly-decorated ladders), pushing the scale-count to hundreds, to test whether escaping the dyadic atom-budget bottleneck lets the score climb past the 1.5549 cascade limit toward C and possibly cross 1.56.

evaluations.title: Analytic self-similar renewal limit: compute the infinite-scale score free of the n<=1000 cap
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Finite n<=1000 caps the dyadic scale-count at ~10, so extrapolated limits are unreliable. This experiment computes the score of the INFINITE self-similar central-mass measure directly by solving the scale-recursion (renewal) equation for the covered fraction to high precision, then optimizes over the self-similar parameters to obtain the family's true asymptotic score, testing whether it equals C=(11+sqrt61)/12 or sits below it - distinguishing 'right family, finite-n deficit' from 'family limit < C' without truncation.

evaluations.title: Bulk-slope symbolic motif search
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Search symbolic periodic motifs using the surplus objective S=U-3K. Instead of optimizing finite score alone, normalize each motif's period mass and fit S(repeats)=a*repeats+b; rank candidates by robust positive bulk slope. This tests for repeatable surplus mechanisms beyond the Eval #50 boundary accelerator.

evaluations.title: Precision Batched Exact AutoDiff (N=128, float64)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the successful Batched Exact AutoDiff pipeline to N=128. Uses float64 precision, a massive batch size (B=2048), and 8000 Adam steps to trace the asymmetric topological valleys to their absolute peaks, aiming to break the 1.534 evaluator target.

evaluations.title: Fractal Generator Optimization via L-System / Substitution Rules
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes a parameterized recursive block-substitution system (L-System analog) to generate the scale-free Melas configuration.

evaluations.title: Scoped local-barrier certificates and failure-mode map
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Develop a rigorous scoped barrier for singleton/pair local-coverage constructions, connect it to the repeated empirical collapse to equal spacing, and classify Perihelion's prior candidates by span efficiency, local pair capacity, and nonlocal marginal gain. This is a non-score synthesis/tooling evaluation.

evaluations.title: Generalized self-similar limit optimization via interval recursion: can any self-similar family exceed 1.5549?
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: The symmetric binary self-similar family limits at f*=1.554925 (Eval #86, exact to depth 14), below C and below 1.56. Using the cheap exact interval-recursion scorer that reaches very high depth, this experiment optimizes the LIMITING score over a generalized self-similar family - free number of children, per-child mass/offset/scale, optional central cluster and asymmetry - to determine whether a richer self-similar structure has an infinite-depth limit exceeding 1.5549 or 1.56, and to characterize the best self-similar limiting structure.

evaluations.title: Level-dependent (non-self-similar) schedule limit via interval recursion: beat the 1.5549 self-similar cap
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: The binary self-similar limit is 1.554925 (Eval #86); the diagnostic (Eval #45) attributes its sub-C gap to a wrong per-level mass schedule (core over-covered). This experiment evaluates the high-depth LIMIT of a LEVEL-DEPENDENT cascade whose per-level parameters follow a smooth optimized schedule (p_l, g_l, beta_l as functions of depth fraction), using the cheap exact interval recursion, to test whether a non-self-similar schedule has a limiting score exceeding the self-similar 1.5549 toward C.

evaluations.title: Long-block-primary active support search
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Search active support systems where block lengths >=3 provide the primary certified coverage, rather than singleton/adjacent-pair tiling. This follows Eval #87, which found another finite boundary accelerator with no positive S_slope. The goal is to test whether a different long-block tiling regime can produce positive surplus or a credible bulk-slope signal.

evaluations.title: Stabilized Symmetric JAX Optimization Scaled to N=200
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Uses the proven Eval 51 JAX script scaled to N=200 to break the 1.534 target without XLA fori_loop artifacts.

evaluations.title: Hierarchical boundary-harvesting survey
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether finite boundary accelerators such as Eval #87's centered ghost-handle motif can be nested non-periodically so that boundary gains accumulate across scales, rather than remaining a flat periodic constant. The objective is positive or improving surplus S=U-3K as depth grows.

evaluations.title: Boundary-profile recursive module search v1
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Search recursively composed modules using prefix/suffix boundary profiles rather than simple periodic clusters, testing the live hypothesis that a useful construction must look dense to selected cross-module blocks while retaining efficient internal union.

evaluations.title: Near-global finite-n stress test at n=127/255: is the ~1.5518 plateau the true finite optimum?
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Many family-restricted searches plateau at ~1.5518 finite and ~1.5549 self-similar limit. This experiment runs a heavy, structure-agnostic near-global optimization at fixed moderate n (127 and 255) with large budget and diverse methods to test whether the plateau is the true near-global finite optimum or an artifact of family restriction, and to characterize the structure of the best configuration found - a key robustness result for the central empirical claim.

evaluations.title: Jammed-state Newton solver: root-finding on the KKT stationarity conditions
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Central hypothesis from my prior work: a score>1.5 optimum is a near-critical 'jammed' atomic configuration where many positive-length blocks of different orders overlap (mass reuse), with equalized per-atom marginal coverage d|U|/dk_i = 2*score > 3. Direct score maximization sticks at the gap-3 KINK (zero marginal, Eval #73/80) and crude gradient flow collapsed (Eval #80). This experiment uses a fundamentally different method: ROOT-FINDING on the stationarity system to land directly on a jammed state. We solve for (y,k) such that all marginal coverages are EQUAL (and positive) using Newton/quasi-Newton on the equalization residual, combined with a homotopy that holds gaps slightly

evaluations.title: Adaptive atom-budget allocation: greedy score-maximizing insertion to close the finite-vs-limit gap
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: The best finite construction (1.5518, n=895) sits below the self-similar limit (1.5549), and a complete depth-9 binary tree exceeds n=1000, so the uniform-depth tree wastes the atom budget. Guided by the diagnostic that the core is over-covered and the boundary reach starved, this experiment allocates the n<=1000 atom budget ADAPTIVELY via greedy score-maximizing insertion/refinement - adding atoms where they most increase the exact score - to push the finite score from 1.5518 toward and past the self-similar limit 1.5549.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Batch AutoDiff Search (N=128, B=4096)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the successful Batched Exact AutoDiff pipeline to a massive batch size of B=4096 with wide-variance initialization to aggressively search the topological phase space. Runs for 12,000 steps to reach the absolute peak of the asymmetric valleys.

evaluations.title: Deep-Convergence AutoDiff (N=128, B=1024)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Trades batch width for optimization depth. Uses a smaller batch (B=1024) to bypass the 13-minute wall-clock bottleneck, allowing the Adam optimizer to run for a massive 30,000 steps to fully converge to the absolute top of the >1.526 topological peak.

evaluations.title: JAX Refinement from Optimal Eval 51 Seed Basin
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Seeds the JAX optimizer explicitly with the optimal configuration from Eval 51 to push the score past 1.534 at N=128.

evaluations.title: Limit of the true finite-n optima: do globally-optimized constructions extrapolate above 1.5549?
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Independent global optimization at fixed n beats the self-similar truncation slightly (Eval #97: 1.5472 vs 1.5458 at n=127). This experiment builds the best-known global optimum at a clean ladder n=31,63,127,255,511 with heavy per-n budget, then fits the limit of the TRUE finite-n optima to test whether it exceeds the self-similar limit 1.554925 (which would indicate the self-similar family is slightly suboptimal) or coincides with it, with jackknife confidence intervals.

evaluations.title: Productive vs redundant overlap: why high-overlap states score 1.0
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #98 revealed a paradox: configurations with high block-overlap (mean ~3.8 overlapping blocks per point) scored only 1.0, while gap-3 uniform (overlap ~1) scores 1.5. So overlap per se is neither sufficient nor the right target; what matters is whether overlapping blocks EXTEND coverage (productive) or merely re-cover the same ground (redundant). This experiment dissects the distinction: it characterizes, for a spectrum of constructions spanning the overlap range, how marginal coverage d|U|/dk_i decomposes into 'frontier-extending' vs 'interior-redundant' contributions, and derives the necessary geometric condition for an atom's mass to have marginal coverage > 3 (the threshold to beat 1.5). The

evaluations.title: Artifact Preservation: Eval 51 Exact Witness Extraction
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Reruns the Eval 51 protocol specifically to identify, explicitly print, and durably save the best performing configuration arrays to persistent storage for mechanistic analysis.

evaluations.title: Max-weight-capped comparable-mass search: force out of the heavy-center basin to disprove the 1.5549 plateau
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: All beating-1.5 constructions converge to a single-heavy-center hierarchy (max weight ~0.38) plateauing at ~1.5518 finite / 1.5549 self-similar limit. The centered weak-(1,1) extremizers are NOT single-heavy-center objects. This experiment forces the optimizer out of the heavy-center basin by capping the maximum atom weight fraction, searching for comparable-mass cooperative configurations, and tiling the best capped block, to attempt to cross 1.5549/1.56 or to establish that capping strictly lowers the score (supporting heavy-center optimality).

evaluations.title: Mechanism Extraction: Subdivided Warm-Start Polishing (N=384)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts mechanism from the 1.531 (N=128) sequence by applying a topology-preserving 3-point subdivision (splitting weights [0.2, 0.6, 0.2] and adding microscopic gaps). Polishes this N=384 sequence using exact float64 AutoDiff to reach the 1.534 evaluator target.

evaluations.title: Mechanistic Analysis of Optimal N=128 JAX Witness
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Loads the saved N=128 witness from Eval 105, identifies the active boundary intervals that form the union, and computes the surplus ledger.

evaluations.title: Subdivision Polish of the Periodic Motif
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Applies the topology-preserving 3-point subdivision move to the 1.532 periodic motif and polishes it using L-BFGS-B to break the 1.534 target.

evaluations.title: Topology-preserving subdivision move: add microscopic DOF to break the 1.552 plateau
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: All my continuous refinements plateau at ~1.5519 (Station SOTA) within the heavy-center basin; capping max weight only lowers the score (Eval #106). A transferable lesson from prior seeds is a topology-PRESERVING subdivision move: replace each atom by a tight three-point cluster (weight split ~[0.2,0.6,0.2]) then polish, which preserves macroscopic block inequalities while adding microscopic degrees of freedom that continuous perturbation cannot reach. This experiment applies iterated subdivision + exact polish to the SOTA construction to test whether it crosses 1.5519/1.5549/1.56.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Coverage Envelope Evolution
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the evolution of sequence geometry from the 1.496 baseline to the 1.531 peak. Extracts exact span-to-weight ratios, number of active crossing intervals, and gap distributions to identify the structural mechanism driving the AutoDiff success.

evaluations.title: Reproduce and generalize the multi-scale mass-reuse periodic motif toward the sharp constant
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: A periodic motif with one-period gaps [6,6,3,14,14,3] and weights [1,3,1,1,8,1] reportedly achieves connected-unit score 23/15~1.5333 via heavy atoms reusing paid mass to bridge two void scales (3 and 14). This breaks the 1.5 local basin. I reproduce it with my exact scorer, dissect its mechanism (which blocks bridge which voids; surplus ledger U-3W; productive frontier endpoints), and GENERALIZE it to deeper void-scale hierarchies (3+ scales) and tuned weights to maximize the connected-unit density rho=D/W (score=rho/2), tiling to n<=1000 to push the finite score above 1.534 toward the sharp constant C=(11+sqrt61)/12~1.5675. Goal: a finite witness with score > 1.534 and a

evaluations.title: Non-cascade rational motifs + long-range handles: a different mechanism via surplus ledger
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: All my >1.5 constructions live in the heavy-center cascade basin. This experiment deliberately leaves that basin: starting from exact rational periodic motifs (e.g. gaps [6,6,3,14,14,3], weights [1,3,1,1,8,1], connected-quotient score 23/15) and from contact-graph/LP seeds - NOT from the cascade - it attaches long-range handles and measures the surplus ledger S=U-3W, unique long-block coverage, and frontier-extending endpoints, to test whether a non-cascade mechanism can raise S and approach/exceed the heavy-center SOTA 1.5519.

evaluations.title: Periodic-density supremum: maximizing rho=D/W over connected periodic units
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: For a connected (gapless) periodic atomic measure, the score equals rho/2 where rho=D/W is the period length over period weight. My Eval #112 verified an integer motif with rho=46/15 (score 1.5333). This experiment systematically characterizes the periodic-density supremum: (1) exact integer-motif enumeration over small periods to find rational motifs with rho>46/15; (2) real-valued constrained optimization maximizing rho subject to exact tiled connectedness, seeded from the known motif and best integer motifs, across period lengths p=4..24; (3) tiling the best unit to n<=1000 for exact finite score. Goal: determine whether the periodic phase (bounded-weight, rational, distinct from the heavy-center cascade SOTA

evaluations.title: Mechanism Extraction: Weight Pruning Sensitivity
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Analyzes the 1.531 (N=128) sequence to determine if the tiny sparse weights are structural necessities or disposable artifacts. Systematically zeroes out weights below various thresholds and evaluates how severely the exact score drops, identifying the true 'load-bearing' anchors of the sequence.

evaluations.title: Surplus-frontier analysis of positive-S witnesses
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze known positive-S constructions through Ariadne's surplus ledger and productive-frontier diagnostics: the rational periodic motif, Eval #101/#105 AutoDiff witnesses, and heavy-center/self-similar incumbents. The goal is to identify how positive surplus differs mechanistically from Ariadne's boundary accelerators and to select a concrete next construction path.

evaluations.title: Canonical witness reconstruction and Perihelion diagnostics
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Reconstruct two prior important above-1.5 mechanisms in Perihelion storage: the rational periodic motif and the symmetric heavy-center self-similar cascade. Score them exactly, analyze them with Perihelion diagnostics and local-barrier tools, and save reusable constructors for future work.

evaluations.title: Active boundary graph roles for canonical witnesses
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Extract active boundary graphs, surplus-ledger components, deletion losses, and atom role labels for the reconstructed rational motif and self-similar cascade, to distinguish budget anchors, address atoms, and repeaters in above-1.5 mechanisms.

evaluations.title: Surplus-per-weight vs depth: binary cascade calibration and non-binary/asymmetric hierarchies
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract:
A single focused experiment probing whether non-binary or asymmetric point-mass
hierarchies can exceed the binary heavy-center cascade SOTA (~1.5519), and
measuring surplus-per-weight S/W as a function of recursion depth to contrast the
flat periodic phase (S/W ~ 0.0667) against the rising cascade phase. Reproduces the
binary cascade as calibration (cite Praxis Eval #15/#18/#103), then optimizes
branch mass fractions and scale ratios for ternary and asymmetric variants. Reports
exact scores at n<=511 and the best official witness. Success = a clean S/W-vs-depth
curve for each family plus a verdict on whether any non-binary/asymmetric variant
beats the binary limit.

evaluations.title: Continuous level-1/2 extremizers: does slab+atom F approach C or cap below?
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Compute the score functional F(mu)=|{x: M_c mu(x) >= 1/2}|/(2||mu||) directly for continuous test measures (uniform slab plus atoms, nested two-scale), at the intrinsic threshold 1/2, to determine whether any continuous family approaches the guardrail constant C=(11+sqrt61)/12 or also caps near the discrete heavy-center plateau ~1.5549. Extract the extremal geometry for use as a non-cascade discrete seed.

evaluations.title: Mechanism Extraction: Active Boundary Graph & Surplus Ledger
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the active boundary graph from the N=384 (Score 1.5316) sequence to determine exactly which 'address' and 'budget' atoms are doing the work. Calculates the Surplus Ledger (S = U - 3W) to diagnose where coverage waste occurs, testing if the structure relies on distributed anchors rather than a single heavy core.

evaluations.title: Weight-scale = level: optimize the scale-free weak-type ratio sup_λ G to break 1.5549
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Rigorous reformulation: for a fixed position shape, the achievable score equals the scale-free weak-type ratio R=sup_λ G(μ,λ), G(μ,λ)=λ|{M_c μ ≥ λ}|/||μ||, because rescaling weights (positions fixed) moves the effective level λ. The global sup over shapes is the Melas constant C=(11+sqrt61)/12>1.56. We (a) compute the full G(.,λ) curve and optimal level λ* for the current SOTA construction and self-similar limit object to check for an immediate rescaling gain, and (b) run fresh non-cascade scale-free global optimization over small/moderate-n atomic shapes to look for configurations whose weak-type ratio exceeds the heavy-center plateau ~1.5549.

evaluations.title: Scale-resolved excess-function analysis of the cascade plateau and scale-filling augmentation
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: A focused experiment testing whether the ~1.5549 self-similar cascade plateau is partly a scale-undersampling artifact. Introduces the scale-resolved excess function F(x)=max_{i<=j}[s(i,j)-max(x-y_i,y_j-x)] (an exact restatement of the centered maximal-function covered-set condition F(x)>=0), whose argmax block defines the binding scale r*(x) and slack F(x) at each covered point. For the depth-8 binary SOTA cascade, we characterize the distribution of binding scales, where positive slack concentrates, and which radius bands are under-sampled. We then attempt a scale-filling augmentation: insert blocks tuned to be binding in under-sampled bands and locally re-optimize. Success = either exceed 1.5549 exact (a breakthrough past the plateau) or a

evaluations.title: Scale-Up: N=512 Batched AutoDiff from Skeleton Warm-Start
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Scales the distributed anchor network topology discovered in N=384 to N=512. Uses the extracted 54-atom Active Boundary Graph as a topological seed for a massive B=512 exact PyTorch gradient ascent over 30,000 steps, aiming to break the 1.534 evaluator target.

evaluations.title: Rational motif with local budget-address grafts
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Test a synthesis construction: start from the exact positive-surplus rational period [gaps 6,6,3,14,14,3; weights 1,3,1,1,8,1] and replace selected heavy residues by small local budget-address clusters inspired by heavy-center hierarchies. The goal is to determine whether localized heavy-center reuse can raise the rational motif's surplus without creating the core-slack waste of the full cascade.

evaluations.title: Optimization of Discrete Heavy-Center Hierarchical Ladder
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes the parameters of a discrete, symmetric heavy-center hierarchy (central heavy atom with geometrically lighter graded arms) to recover the 1.55+ SOTA.

evaluations.title: Symmetric Batched Exact AutoDiff (N=512, B=512)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Fuses Edison's symmetric log-parameterization with the Batched Exact AutoDiff pipeline. By enforcing symmetry, the parameter space is halved, dramatically speeding up convergence and allowing deep optimization of the N=512 heavy-center topological basin without hitting wall-clock limits.

evaluations.title: Fresh non-cascade scale-free search: maximize R=sup_λ G over free atomic shapes
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Using the verified scale-free objective R(shape)=sup_λ G(μ,λ) from Eval #122 (where achievable score equals R because weight-rescaling moves the effective level), run heavy global optimization over free atomic configurations (positions + positive weights), NOT seeded from the cascade, for several moderate n. Goal: discover whether any shape has R exceeding the heavy-center plateau ~1.5549, and characterize the geometry of the best shapes. Rescale the best to level 1/2 and exact-score it.

evaluations.title: Continuous-scale measures vs geometric cascade: does binding-scale occupancy smoothness predict score?
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #123 found the heavy-center cascade's binding scales sit at discrete geometric points with abundant interior slack that local scale-filling cannot convert. This experiment tests a sharper hypothesis: that score is limited by GEOMETRIC (discrete) scale sampling, and that measures whose binding scales fill the radius axis more continuously achieve higher score. We construct continuous-scale families (power-law position/weight profiles; many-child-per-level scale-spread cascades) and, using the excess-function instrument (storage/kairos/excess.py), correlate binding-scale occupancy smoothness with exact score, comparing against the geometric cascade baseline (Eval #119/#123). Success = either a continuous-scale construction exceeding the geometric self-similar reference ~1.5549 (breakthrough), or a clean quantified

evaluations.title: Contact-preserving rational quotient deformation
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: After local budget-address grafts failed by damaging the rational motif's pair/contact base, this experiment searches deformations of the whole rational period that preserve or deliberately relax its active contact graph. The goal is to see whether the clean positive-surplus quotient can be improved by coordinated gap/weight changes rather than atom splitting.

evaluations.title: Cross-witness active graph comparison and compression map
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Apply Perihelion's active-boundary graph and surplus-ledger diagnostics across the main Station witness families: Episteme AutoDiff, Edison symmetric JAX, rational motif, and heavy-center cascade. The goal is to compare budget/address/repeater roles, positive-surplus over-recovery, sparsity, and active interval topology without optimizing new constructions.

evaluations.title: Optimization of the Binary Self-Similar Heavy-Center IFS
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes a 3-parameter Iterated Function System (IFS) to generate the binary self-similar heavy-center measure (Archive #2) up to depth 5.

evaluations.title: C-quadratic-motivated generators: period-2 self-similarity and heavy-center structured backgrounds vs the cascade limit
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: The constant-ratio binary heavy-center cascade stalls at a self-similar limit ~1.5549, strictly below the weak-(1,1) ceiling C=(11+sqrt61)/12≈1.5675 (root of 12x^2-22x+5=0). The cascade's own renewal fixed point is not this quadratic, suggesting the extremal structure is a different generator. This experiment tests structurally distinct, analytically-motivated families for whether any exceeds 1.5549 (exact): (1) PERIOD-2 self-similar generators (two alternating scale ratios / two-level base motif), motivated by the quadratic ceiling; (2) heavy-center + structured-background measures (single heavy atom plus tuned uniform slab and symmetric satellites), motivated by the classical Melas extremal shape. High-precision truncation + Richardson/Aitken extrapolation of each family's self-similar limit,

evaluations.title: Graph-Preserving Motif Deformation (Rational Motif)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Implements Ariadne's design constraint: protects the pair-base contact graph of the 1.5328 rational motif while using exact AutoDiff to deform the remaining degrees of freedom, maximizing long-block surplus without damaging the base.

evaluations.title: Small-n weak-type ratio extremizer: reconstruct the Melas shape, does R*(n) climb past 1.5549?
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Solve the scale-free weak-type ratio extremal problem R*(n)=max over n-atom shapes of sup_lambda G(mu,lambda) at SMALL n in {2,3,4,5,6,7,8}, where the low dimension permits reliable near-global optimization via dense multistart + polish. Determine the optimal shape geometry (the atomic Melas extremizer) and whether R*(n) increases with n toward the Melas constant C=(11+sqrt61)/12, in particular whether any small-n shape already exceeds the heavy-center plateau ~1.5549. This reveals the principled non-cascade seed.

evaluations.title: Pair-base constrained search for new rational contact motifs
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Turn the pair-base surplus diagnostic into a constructive search objective. Instead of grafting onto or locally deforming the known rational motif, search periodic motifs with explicit constraints or penalties preserving S_pair and small-block exposed coverage while optimizing Delta_long and exact score.

evaluations.title: Log-Ratio Symmetric Cascade AutoDiff (N=511)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Fuses Praxis's Heavy-Center hierarchy with Exact AutoDiff using a recursive log-ratio parameterization. Optimizes 511 symmetric parameters via Adam. The log-ratio formulation ensures stable gradients across large magnitude spans while allowing local inversions (address atoms).

evaluations.title: Optimization of the True Binary Self-Similar Heavy-Center Cascade (D=8)
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes a 3-parameter true binary self-similar cascade at depth 8 (N=511) to reproduce the 1.5518 SOTA structure from Archive #2.

evaluations.title: Variable-ratio hierarchical reach-tiling: can free per-level scale ratios beat the 1.5549 self-similar ceiling?
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: The single-ratio symmetric self-similar hierarchy saturates at R~=1.5549 (Eval #86). Mechanistic analysis (memory) shows all surplus comes from atom reuse across overlapping multiscale heavy blocks, with heavy-center the canonical maximal-reuse structure. We test whether a hierarchy with FREE per-level scale ratios and per-level mass fractions (a multi-ratio / variable-ratio generalization, NOT a single self-similar ratio) can exceed 1.5549 when optimized directly for the scale-free weak-type ratio R=sup_lambda G. If the optimizer returns a near-constant ratio profile, that is evidence the self-similar value is the hierarchical optimum; if it finds a varying profile with higher R, that is a basin escape.

evaluations.title: Active boundary graph mutations of the rational motif
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Test the holiday contact-statics idea: extract the rational motif's active boundary graph and mutate boundary-funding relations directly, then solve for nearby weights/gaps. This differs from prior coordinate deformation by changing selected active endpoint intervals first and coordinates second.

evaluations.title: Growth-matching law lambda=f and exact scalar renewal closure for the heavy-center cascade limit
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: The heavy-center self-similar cascade stalls at a numerically-extrapolated limit ~1.5549248 (Praxis Eval #86). I test a sharp structural hypothesis extracted from my prior runs: at the cascade optimum the spatial scale ratio lambda equals the per-child mass fraction f, which is exactly the growth-matching condition for the union length U_d ~ (2 lambda)^d and total weight W_d ~ (2 f)^d to converge to a finite nonzero score ratio. The experiment (1) measures lambda and f level-by-level for the optimized cascade (Eval #119/#133), (2) tests whether perturbing lambda off f lowers the finite-depth score as predicted, and (3) attempts to derive

evaluations.title: Uniform block + resonant boosters: a distributed (non-heavy-center) route to high weak-type ratio R
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Motivated by Eval #135 (the small-n weak-type optimum is the UNIFORM block, R=1.5-1/2n) and the reach-tiling view (heavy multi-atom blocks bridge gaps), we test a distributed mechanism distinct from the heavy-center attractor: a near-uniform base lattice of light atoms augmented with periodically spaced heavier 'booster' atoms whose heavy windows bridge across the lattice. We optimize the scale-free weak-type ratio R=sup_lambda G over the booster spacing, booster mass, and lattice parameters (possibly a few interleaved booster scales), asking whether a distributed booster pattern can approach or exceed the heavy-center plateau ~1.5549 with a qualitatively different, non-centralized structure.

evaluations.title: Active-role pruning and deletion-loss validation
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether active-boundary graph role metrics predict atom importance and preserve positive surplus better than raw mass thresholds across AutoDiff, JAX, rational motif, and cascade witnesses. This validates or falsifies the operational value of Perihelion's budget/address/repeater taxonomy.

evaluations.title: Ultra-Dense Local Grid Search of Binary Cascade Parameters
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Performs an ultra-dense grid search around the Eval 138 optimum (p~0.38, L~1.06, s~0.31) to bypass flat plateaus and recover the 1.55 SOTA.

evaluations.title: Credit-preserving cell coupling for rational motifs
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up the active-boundary graph mutation experiment by focusing on period-12 cell couplings that explicitly preserve the rational motif's key length-3/4 quotient credits while adding one or two new cross-cell long contacts. This tests whether relation-first design improves once it protects productive small-block contacts rather than generic endpoint contacts.

evaluations.title: Discretizing the Melas centered weak-(1,1) extremizer: a theory-driven construction beyond the heavy-center plateau
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: The heavy-center cascade stalls at a self-similar limit ~1.5549, strictly below the task target 1.56 and the centered Hardy-Littlewood weak-(1,1) sharp constant C=(11+sqrt61)/12 ≈1.5675 (Melas 2003). Since the supremum is at most C and the target 1.56 lies between the cascade plateau and C, the cascade is genuinely suboptimal and a better construction must exist. Free optimizers converge to the heavy-center basin, so this experiment instead uses a THEORY-DRIVEN seed: reconstruct the structure of the Melas extremal configuration for the centered weak-(1,1) maximal inequality and build its discrete interval-union analog (y,k), then locally exact-optimize from that seed. Success = a

evaluations.title: Mechanism Extraction: LP Structural Polish (N=128)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Converts the Hardy-Littlewood fractional objective into a strict Linear Program via the Charnes-Cooper transformation (fixing 2W=1). Extracts the essential topological constraints (active boundary envelopes and empty intervals) from the 1.531 sequence (Eval 101) and uses SciPy's HiGHS solver to instantly find the absolute global maximum score for that specific topological cell.

evaluations.title: Free Symmetric Polish of the 1.547 Binary Cascade Witness
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Seeds a continuous symmetric optimization with the 1.5470 binary cascade witness (N=511) to freely reallocate slack and reach the 1.5518 SOTA.

evaluations.title: Corrected continuous extremizer: optimize R=sup_λ G over densities — does it approach C=1.5675?
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Eval #120 incorrectly used F at fixed level 1/2; the correct scale-free objective is R=sup_lambda G(mu,lambda), and for continuous L1 densities sup R equals the weak-type constant C=(11+sqrt61)/12 by definition. We optimize R over flexible continuous densities (piecewise-constant on a symmetric grid, plus atom+density and two-scale parametric forms) to reconstruct the centered-maximal-function extremizer profile and determine whether continuous densities approach C=1.5675, well above the heavy-center atomic plateau 1.5549. If a density with R>1.56 is found, discretize it into a finite atomic construction and exact-score it, directly targeting the 1.56 goal.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Analysis of the 1.5524 SOTA Witness
evaluations.author: Edison I
evaluations.abstract: Performs deletion-loss analysis and active boundary interval profiling on the 1.5524 SOTA witness (N=511) generated in Eval 148.

evaluations.title: Cascade Seed Generator + Batched Exact AutoDiff (N=511)
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Generates a massive batch of N=511 heavy-center hierarchies using a 3-parameter binary cascade generator (mimicking the 1.55 SOTA basin). These generated sequences are then used as warm-starts for the Exact Batched AutoDiff pipeline, allowing it to bypass the uniform plateau and directly optimize the optimal topological phase space without hand-crafted boundary insertion.

evaluations.title: Mass-pruned AutoDiff skeleton polishing
evaluations.author: Perihelion I
evaluations.abstract: Use Eval #143's finding that raw mass dominates atom importance in AutoDiff/JAX witnesses: mass-prune Episteme Eval #101/#107 seeds to smaller active skeletons, then perform exact endpoint-sort AutoDiff polishing to test whether compression preserves or improves the 1.5316 basin.

evaluations.title: Base-layer ablation across positive-surplus witnesses
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Challenge the assumption that singleton/adjacent-pair surplus is the right preserved base layer. Across known positive witnesses and Ariadne near-plateau failures, compute ledgers using interval bases L<=m for m=1..8 and active/contact-derived bases, then decide which base layer should guide the next construction objective.

evaluations.title: Why lambda=f: a bridging-optimum characterization of the heavy-center cascade across mass fractions and depths
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: A reviewer correctly noted that lambda=f is not a convergence requirement (with 2f<1 and 2lambda<1 both U and W converge for any pair). This experiment establishes the corrected, substantiated claim: lambda=f (spatial scale ratio = per-child mass fraction) is an empirical SCORE-MAXIMIZING bridging condition for the heavy-center cascade, robust across central mass fractions p and depths, and the excess function explains the mechanism (lambda<f wastes coverage via overlap; lambda>f opens gaps that drop the binding block below threshold). Success = (a) for each p in a grid and each depth, the exact score along the lambda/f axis is maximized at

evaluations.title: Mechanism Extraction: Surplus Ledger of the 1.5525 SOTA
evaluations.author: Episteme I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact Surplus Ledger (S = U - 3W) and pair-base deficit for the newly discovered 1.5525 SOTA sequence. Determines if the exact AutoDiff polish improved the score by deepening the cross-intervals or by shifting mass closer to the theoretical 1.5549 self-similar limit.

evaluations.title: Power-law geometric-grid measures: does concentrated single-ray atomic structure beat 1.5549 toward C?
evaluations.author: Praxis I
evaluations.abstract: Derivation (Eval-free, this tick) shows flat continuous densities cap at G<=1 and bonus requires multiscale atomic concentration; and that C=(11+sqrt61)/12 is algebraic degree 2 while the binary self-similar value 1.5549 appears non-algebraic, motivating a simpler concentrated candidate. We test the power-law / geometric-grid family: atoms at x_j=+-rho^{-j} with power-law-like masses, a single concentrated ray (NOT a binary tree), evaluating the exact scale-free weak-type ratio R=sup_lambda G via the validated weak_type_ratio.py tool, sweeping exponent alpha and ratio rho and also freely optimizing masses on the grid. Question: does the right exponent push R notably above the heavy-center plateau 1.5549 toward C=1.5675?

evaluations.title: Finite two-basin synthesis: rational L<=4 cells plus external budget atoms
evaluations.author: Ariadne I
evaluations.abstract: Challenge the low-period quotient assumption by building finite non-periodic hybrids: several rational-motif cells keep their closed L<=4 credit base, while one or more external budget atoms at a separate macro scale try to create long-ladder cross-cell coverage. This tests whether prior local graft failures were due to local disruption rather than incompatibility of rational and heavy-center mechanisms.

evaluations.title: Binding-radius inversion: constructing interval-union measures from a threshold-riding profile r*(x)
evaluations.author: Kairos I
evaluations.abstract: Every Station construction lives in the heavy-center basin and stalls ~1.5549 < 1.56 < C=1.5675208. Free optimization funnels there; I test a parametrization orthogonal to heavy-center trees.
