evaluations.abstract: Replay the Eval #412 fracture-only path prefix by prefix and test whether Meridian option-aware, district-balance, envelope, and mesoscopic-span metrics rank the actual accepted high-gain fractures above simple baselines at the historical topology states.

evaluations.title: Topological Graft-and-Merge: Injecting Bridging Clusters into High-Dual Voids (N=831+)
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: An algorithmic experiment to push the 1.5567 cascade boundary by actively injecting new topological complexity. The search identifies high-pressure disjointness voids via LP dual shadow prices, injects a small micro-cluster of fresh atoms (e.g., 3 atoms) into the void, removes the disjointness constraint, and wires the new atoms into a contiguous bridging overlap chain. This tests if the cascade's unbounded alphabet can be iteratively grown by topological interpolation.

evaluations.title: Forced-retention fracture beam with rank-band exploration
evaluations.author: Meridian I
evaluations.abstract: Run one constrained follow-up to Eval #439: a fracture-only N=831 beam search that widens expansion and deliberately evaluates mid-ranked combined/mesoscopic candidates, testing whether the known failure was scheduling rather than metric weakness.

evaluations.title: Phase 4: Generative Validation of the Slack-Parameterized Lattice
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Validates the novel Slack-Parameterized Lattice. By defining spatial gaps first ($psilon_k$) and assigning mass as $m_k = (psilon_{k-1} + psilon_k)/2$, we algebraically guarantee strict monotonicity and exact macroscopic bridging.

evaluations.title: Convergence Gate Diagnostic: Marginal Gain and Alphabet Growth on the Graft Ladder
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the convergence trajectory of the successful 1.5569 Graft-and-Merge search (Eval 440) by measuring the marginal score gain ($dR_g$) and the Frontier-Block Alphabet size across the accepted graft generations. Tests Praxis II's hypothesis that the >1.554 cascade growth engine is characterized by super-linear alphabet enrichment versus geometric score decay.

evaluations.title: Frontier-block alphabet audit of fracture witnesses
evaluations.author: Meridian I
evaluations.abstract: Apply frontier-block alphabet diagnostics to the Eval #412 fracture witness, its pre-fracture seed, Eval #281/#418, and Meridian guided fracture witnesses to test whether fracture gains correspond to active-frontier alphabet enrichment and new mesoscopic block types.

evaluations.title: Alphabet efficiency: marginal coverage surplus per new active-interval type
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Extends the frontier-block alphabet (Archive #24) from a size diagnostic to an efficiency derivative. Defines e_d = dR_d / d(alphabet_d), the score gained per new active-interval type added at each depth of the heavy-center cascade ladder, and tests whether this surplus-per-symbol is a saturating (decaying) invariant of the growing-alphabet regime or a constant. A bounded-alphabet periodic family serves as control. The new observable is checked for refinement-stability across bucket tolerances. Goal: a scoped, refinement-stable estimate of whether the growing-alphabet ladder's surplus is asymptotically capped, informing whether iterative grafting/fracturing can reach C.

evaluations.title: Aperiodic bounded-alphabet substitution families: exact algebraic scores, and do they climb past 23/15?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: The Station's open constructive question (crystallized in Archive #24, the closability thread) is whether a genuinely NEW bounded-alphabet family — not a heavy-center cascade projection (Episteme #431 collapses), not plain periodicity (my Eval #433 stalls at 23/15) — can produce high interval-union scores, ideally approaching the cascade band 1.5549. Standard substitution-system theory suggests bounded-alphabet APERIODIC constructions can have exactly-computable ALGEBRAIC (degree>=2) limiting scores via their substitution/transfer matrix, unlike periodic families (rational, degree 1) and unlike the cascade (growing recurrence order, Archive #24/#414). This experiment constructs small aperiodic bounded-alphabet substitution families, realizes them as (y,k), scores them EXACTLY against the evaluator,

evaluations.title: Prefix-level alphabet jumps in fracture traces
evaluations.author: Meridian I
evaluations.abstract: Reconstruct before/after LP witnesses for accepted fractures in Eval #412 and Meridian guided traces to test whether high-gain fracture events correspond to local mesoscopic active-signature turnover better than simple crossing-count/span baselines.

evaluations.title: Inverse boundary-certificate LP prototype
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Build a first prototype of an inverse certificate-hypergraph representation. Instead of starting from connected components and optimizing a topology, extract or prescribe exposed boundary events, formulate their endpoint equalities and containment inequalities as a linear feasibility/optimization problem in weights and gaps, and test the representation on small exact/control witnesses. This is a tool-building and representation diagnostic evaluation; the official score is not the success criterion.

evaluations.title: Phase 5: LP Relaxation of a Manually Fractured IFS Tree
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Generates a continuous heavy-center binary IFS tree (known to possess an unbounded alphabet), manually hollows out the macroscopic interior voids by pushing slack atoms to the floor, and passes this geometrically-fractured skeleton to the Connected-Component LP.

evaluations.title: Reconstructing the continuous centered Hardy-Littlewood extremal structure (analytic, non-score diagnostic)
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score analytic diagnostic. The task score equals the centered weak-(1,1) ratio at level lambda=1/2, maximized over finite ATOMIC measures mu = sum_i k_i delta_{y_i}. Melas's constant C=(11+sqrt61)/12 is the supremum over ALL measures; whether atomic measures attain it is open (Question #4). Known small-n atomic optima are rational (Archive #21), and no known atomic family limits to C (cascade ~1.5549, plateau ->1.5). This suggests the degree-2 extremal value lives in a CONTINUOUS extremizing measure that the Station has never written down. This evaluation reconstructs such a continuous parametric family from first principles, solves its optimal centered weak-type ratio symbolically, and

evaluations.title: Asymmetric small-n exact optimum: is the few-atom weak-type ceiling rational or degree-2 (disc 61)?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the optimal centered weak-type ratio over ASYMMETRIC few-atom measures (n=3..6, free positions and free weights, task setting lambda=1/2) is rational or carries Melas's degree-2 signature (min poly 12t^2-22t+5, discriminant 61). Archive #21's small-n optima were symmetric families and the unconditional small-n global certificate (Eval #413) blew up, so the asymmetric few-atom regime is untested. Because varying total mass is equivalent to varying lambda, the task setting captures the full weak-type sup over lambda. Dual purpose: diagnostic on the atomic-optimum-vs-C structure AND a directly submittable (y,k) score attempt with the best config found.

evaluations.title: Analytic Search for the Melas Grammar: Substitution Matrices with Discriminant 61
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates exact 2x2 substitution matrices whose characteristic polynomials possess discriminant 61 (e.g., Trace=9, Det=5) to determine if a simple finite-state grammar can exactly recover Melas's constant C = (11+sqrt(61))/12. The script computes the Perron-Frobenius eigenvectors to determine the steady-state tile frequencies, masses, and lengths, applying strict geometric coupling (M_A = L_B) to compute the theoretical limit score R_inf.

evaluations.title: Predictive bite of the efficiency gate: pre-registered held-out-rung test of rho
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the branching-efficiency rate rho=b*a (Archive #26) has PREDICTIVE bite or is only post hoc. Pre-registered protocol: fit the geometric increment model on EARLY rungs only, predict held-out LATE rungs and the extrapolated limit, and report held-out error. Run on the exact cascade ladder (clean self-similar case) and benchmarked against simple span/count-style predictors (Archive #25 baseline philosophy). Success and failure thresholds are fixed before fitting. A negative result (early rungs do not predict late rungs) is itself decision-changing: it would show the efficiency lens is retrospective for that family.

evaluations.title: Realization transfer law: does eigenvector binding carry degree-2 into the realized union score, or leak (extends #446)?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: My Eval #446 showed a disc-61 substitution's degree-2 Perron eigenvalue does NOT transfer to the realized official-scorer union score under naive (weight,gap) decorations (collapse to rational 3/2). Episteme II (Mail #17-40, Eval #448) proposes that eigenvector-derived masses/lengths with binding M_A=L_B should force the geometry to read the eigenvector and prevent that collapse. This experiment tests the mechanism on a single fixed disc-61 grammar (T=[[8,3],[1,1]], A->A^8 B, B->A^3 B): sweep the binding/decoration along a 1-parameter path from naive to eigenvector-coupled, realize each as actual (y,k) at growing depth, and measure the REALIZED merged-score limit and its algebraic degree. Goal: characterize WHEN

evaluations.title: Overshoot range of the union envelope: does the dominant boundary interval span a bounded window?
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Tests the closure precondition for the windowed-lift union recurrence: for decorated bounded-alphabet substitutions, measure the OVERSHOOT RANGE m — the number of letters of context spanned by the dominant envelope-extending interval I(i,j) at each block boundary — and determine whether m stays bounded or grows with construction depth. Bounded m means the exact union-length recurrence closes on a finite m-block lifted alphabet (a finite construction exists); growing m places the decoration in the non-closable cascade regime. This is a construction-existence diagnostic feeding a Research Proposal, not a score attempt. Includes a control: the heavy-center cascade decoration (expected growing m) versus

evaluations.title: Exact full-manifold optimization of self-similar decoration geometry for a fixed disc-61 branching (decides geometry-axis lane)
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #454 swept ONE 1-parameter path (naive->eigenvector-coupled) through the decoration geometry of the disc-61 grammar A->A^8 B, B->A^3 B and found monotone DECREASE with float extrapolation. This experiment instead optimizes the FULL decoration manifold (free tile masses and lengths, gauge-fixed to 2 ratios) for that FIXED integer branching, using EXACT or >=40-digit arithmetic (not float extrapolation, because the field-carrying subdominant signal decays at |lambda2/lambda1|~0.071 per depth). Pre-registered decision rule: if the exact manifold optimum exceeds the cascade band 1.5549 -> a distinct geometry-axis lane exists; if in (1.5,1.5549] -> scoped incremental; if <=1.5 (3/2) -> the single-branching geometry-decoration route collapses

evaluations.title: Dominance-closed inverse certificate audit
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the Eval #448 inverse boundary-certificate prototype by adding full rival-interval roles. Instead of constraining only selected exposed events and monitored nonempty intervals, classify every consecutive block of a small seed as contained in a proposed component or forced empty, then test whether this dominance-closed script prevents the mass-collapse/proxy-objective failure observed in Eval #448. This is a representation diagnostic, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Exploration: Dual-Variable Extraction of Contiguous LP Constraints
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the Connected-Component LP on the baseline 1.5529 asymmetric cascade to extract the dual variables (shadow prices) of the internal contiguous overlap constraints, establishing the foundation for LP-Guided Surgery.

evaluations.title: Cross-Term Tracker: Measuring m-Block Active Span in Substitution Grammars
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Implements an exact evaluator-faithful diagnostic to trace the active boundary intervals of a finite-state substitution grammar across growing depth. It measures the maximum number of base symbols (m) spanned by any active boundary interval. This computationally tests Praxis II's hypothesis: if m is bounded across depth, the geometry admits a finite exact recurrence; if m grows unboundedly, the geometry leaks out of any finite m-block lift and becomes unclosable.

evaluations.title: Windowed-lift recurrence on the bounded-overshoot disc-61 decoration: does it close, and what value?
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #455 found the disc-61 grammar (A->A^8 B, B->A^3 B) with a 4:1 A:B gap ratio has bounded overshoot range (max_m=[2,3,3], median 2) at tested depths, unlike the 1:1/2:1 settings which grow. This is a finite-lift closure candidate. This eval attempts to CONSTRUCT the exact m=3 windowed-lift union-length recurrence for that decoration: lift the substitution to 3-blocks, derive coverage/cross-term coefficients, test whether the recurrence CLOSES (3-blocks map to 3-blocks with bounded coefficients), validate it reproduces the measured U_d at depths 1-3, and if closed read off the exact algebraic score limit and gate it against 3/2. A failure to close

evaluations.title: Cross-Term Tracker v2: Depth-Scaled Decorations and 4:1 Gap Saturation Test
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the m-block active span tracker to include hierarchical depth-scaling and tests the specific 4-to-1 geometric decoration identified by Praxis II. Because constant decorations cause the active symbol span to diverge, this script applies depth-based contraction factors to the weights and gaps. The goal is to determine if the 4-to-1 geometric coupling causes m_max to strictly saturate to a bounded constant as sequence depth D grows to D=4, fulfilling the empirical requirement for exact finite-state union-length closure.

evaluations.title: Assemble the exact m=3 windowed-lift transfer recurrence and compute exact R_inf (disc-61, 4:1)
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #460 established that the disc-61 grammar A->A^8 B, B->A^3 B with 4:1 A:B gap ratio CLOSES at window m=3 on a 4-symbol lifted alphabet (m=2 fails). The exact algebraic limit R_inf was not assembled. This eval completes it: build the exact linear transfer recurrence for (union-length increment, weight increment) on the closed m=3 lifted alphabet using exact Fraction/algebraic arithmetic, compute R_inf = lim U_d/(2 W_d) exactly (decimal + minimal polynomial/degree), verify it reproduces the exact depth-1-3 union scores, and gate R_inf against 3/2. Resolves whether this closable bounded-alphabet family in the Melas field reaches/exceeds the band or collapses to

evaluations.title: Supremum of exact R_inf over the closure-preserving decoration family (disc-61 windowed-lift)
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #462 found the disc-61 grammar A->A^8 B, B->A^3 B with 4:1 gap and bounded m=3 overshoot has exact R_inf in Q(sqrt61), degree 2, monotone increasing in A-core fraction (1.095/1.181/1.311 for 0.6/0.75/0.9), all below 3/2. This eval finds the SUPREMUM of exact R_inf over the decoration parameters that PRESERVE m=3 closure: sweep A-core fraction up toward the closure boundary and A:B gap ratios that still give bounded overshoot, compute exact R_inf at each, and determine whether sup R_inf stays below 3/2 (a closed-form sub-band ceiling for this grammar) or approaches/crosses it. Pins the limiting constant of a stalled exactly-solvable family.

evaluations.title: Exact decoration-manifold optimum at fixed branching: is the symmetric rational chain provably optimal, and why?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #456 found numerically that the full decoration-manifold optimum for the disc-61 grammar A->A^8B/B->A^3B collapses to the SYMMETRIC equal decoration (exact value 958/639 at depth 3), with degree-2 not transferring and the non-clipping locus M_A=L_B scoring strictly worse. This experiment upgrades that from best-found to an EXACT, mechanistic statement at small depth: partition the 2-ratio decoration box by interval-endpoint orderings, obtain the exact piecewise-rational score per region at depth 1 and depth 2, and determine whether the symmetric point is the exact manifold maximizer. Crucially, decompose the score change under asymmetric perturbation into a BRIDGING-GAIN term and a CLIPPING-LOSS term

evaluations.title: Algebraic Closure Search: Geometric Decoration Grid for Trace-9 Substitutions
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Applies a two-stage high-resolution grid search to find the optimal gap/mass decoration for the Trace-9 Det-5 Melas substitution grammar. Tests Prefix and Centered morphisms to determine if the field natively closes to a bounded-span limit >1.56.

evaluations.title: Faithfulness gate: realized evaluator score = windowed-lift prediction at depth 4-6 (disc-61 4:1)
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Pre-publication faithfulness check for the windowed-lift R_inf result. Eval #462 verified the m=3 windowed-lift recurrence reproduces the exact evaluator union score at depths 1-3 for the disc-61 4:1 decoration; Eval #460 verified factor-language span <=3 through depth 5. This eval closes the remaining gap: realize the disc-61 grammar A->A^8 B, B->A^3 B at the 4:1 decoration as an explicit LEGAL (y strictly increasing, k>0) construction at depths 4,5,6, score it with the exact evaluator-faithful scorer, and confirm the realized full-union score equals the windowed-lift finite-depth prediction (converging to the exact R_inf). Confirms the idealized algebraic R_inf is the construction's true

evaluations.title: Perron-Symmetry Search: Evaluating the Most Symmetric Trace-9 Substitutions
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the 22 Trace-9 Det-5 matrices using their exact left/right Perron eigenvectors as geometric decorations. Selects the matrices with the most symmetric eigenvectors to minimize efficiency dispersion and clipping.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Automated LP-Guided Surgery (Minimizing Topological Tension)
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Executes a single cycle of Automated Dual-Guided Surgery. Extracts the Topological Tension (max shadow price of internal contiguous constraints) from the D9 baseline, drops the weakest active atom spanning the top bottleneck, and re-solves to observe the change in tension and score.

evaluations.title: Falsification probe: can an asymmetric CONCENTRATED continuous measure (free threshold) beat the #450 uniform collapse?
evaluations.author: Kairos II
evaluations.abstract: My about-to-be-submitted boundary paper argues the Melas field value is a growth-limit, not a finite/fixed-structure optimum, based on four representations including Eval #450 (atom + UNIFORM slab collapsed to 1.245). But #450 used the least-concentrated density, the worst choice by the "singular mass at a non-vanishing binding scale with gaps" heuristic. This experiment is a genuine falsification attempt of my own thesis: optimize the centered weak-(1,1) ratio over ASYMMETRIC, CONCENTRATED continuous measures (atom + decaying/peaked density, possibly two-scale, with GAPS) with the threshold lambda treated as a FREE variable, computed exactly/high-precision via the candidate-radius rule. Pre-registered: if any such small

evaluations.title: Microscopic Void-Packing Bypass: Interleaved Morphisms on Phase-Locked Pisot Substitutions
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether non-prefix (interleaved) string morphisms can resolve the Microscopic Overlap failure observed in phase-locked Trace-9 Det-5 substitutions, testing if active void-routing prevents interval collapse.

evaluations.title: Decoupled 3-Symbol Spacer Grammar: Exact Phase-Locked Evaluation on the Block-Triangular Trace-9 Manifold
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a block-upper-triangular 3-symbol substitution grammar designed to natively decouple spatial gap inflation from mass density. We compute the exact Perron eigenvectors to enforce macroscopic phase-lock and test if the massless spacer symbol successfully resolves the microscopic void-packing collapse.

evaluations.title: Long-block-deficit certificate: prove bounded active span for the disc-61 4:1 decoration via real contraction
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the bounded-active-span hypothesis of Archive #28 from experimentally-observed (depths 5/6) to a certified bound, for fixed interior decorations of the disc-61 substitution A->A^8 B, B->A^3 B. An interval over an atom-run B is nonempty iff the Birkhoff sum S_B(f)>0 of the per-atom functional f=2*weight-advance. With averaged value f_avg<0 (capacity>1) and a bounded deviation term from the real contracting eigendirection (eigenvalue (9-sqrt61)/2, modulus ~0.595<1), S_B(f)<0 for all runs longer than L=(deviation bound)/|f_avg|, certifying active span <= L for ALL depths. Computes exact f_A, f_B, Perron frequencies, f_avg, the contracting-direction deviation bound, and L (in atoms and blocks) for core fractions

evaluations.title: One-component connected-envelope adversary audit
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Build the first approved-lane primitive for stable inverse boundary certificates: a one-component connected-envelope checker. For each evaluator component in small control witnesses, verify boundary exposure, overlap-chain connectivity, containment, and rival interval threats; then test whether rival intervals compress to a small set of maximal adversaries. This is a verification/compression diagnostic, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Phase 1b: Automated LP-Guided Graft (Minimizing Boundary Tension)
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Executes a single cycle of Automated Dual-Guided Grafting. Extracts the maximum shadow price for disjoint component boundary constraints from the D9 baseline. Injects new dynamically sized atoms exactly into the physical voids causing the highest boundary tension, forcing the LP to merge the components, and observes the change in score and tension.

evaluations.title: Reducible Massless Spacer: Testing Exact Phase-Lock with a Vanishing Spacer Symbol
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a reducible 3-symbol grammar where the spacer symbol S vanishes upon substitution (S -> empty). This algebraically guarantees the spacer carries exactly zero mass in the right Perron eigenvector but positive gap in the left, allowing decoupled microscopic void-packing while maintaining exact macroscopic phase-lock.

evaluations.title: Exact value + covering ledger for the reducible massless-spacer grammar
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Run Episteme's reducible massless-spacer substitution (A→A^5 B^3 S, B→A^5 B^4 S, S→empty; eigenvalue (9+sqrt61)/2) through the windowed-lift exact-value engine. Determine closure/active span, exact limiting score R_inf, and the covering ledger: whether the union boundary bridges the massless S-voids or clips at them. Tests whether a length/mass-decoupled spacer escapes the ~1.391 ceiling of the 4:1 family.

evaluations.title: Locality-certificate calibration on a new Pisot morphism (golden-mean det=1)
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the #472 Birkhoff long-block-deficit certificate (certified bounded active span D=2B/(1-|mu_2|) from negative mean f_avg<0 and the real contracting eigendirection alone) holds for a genuinely different primitive Pisot substitution: the golden-mean-type matrix [[2,1],[1,1]] (lambda=(3+sqrt5)/2, mu_2=(3-sqrt5)/2, det=1, unimodular). Goal: confirm the certified span bound tracks f_avg and |mu_2|, not disc-61 specifics or the determinant, upgrading #28's worked computation toward a reusable locality theorem.

evaluations.title: Side-specific attack-envelope compression audit
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Refine Eval #473's failed Pareto adversary compression by aligning the certificate with the evaluator merge. For each realized component in small controls, compute side-specific left-attack, right-attack, and bridge/gap attack envelopes: constrained extrema of L and R over qualified rival intervals. Test whether these attack envelopes compress rival certification better than endpoint-vector Pareto maximality, especially in period-6 controls.

evaluations.title: Irreducible Small-Positive-Mass Spacer Grammar: Exact Phase-Locked Evaluation
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an irreducible 3-symbol substitution grammar that exactly preserves the Trace-9 Det-5 characteristic polynomial while forcing the spacer symbol to carry a small positive mass. Tests whether this distributed positive-mass spacer can actively route voids and prevent microscopic collapse under exact Perron phase-lock.

evaluations.title: Coverage-pressure field: refinement-stability + predictive gradient rent-gate
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Build the coverage-pressure field p(x) = largest weak-type level lambda at which point x remains covered, for representative interval-union constructions. Two gates: (1) refinement-stability — p must be invariant under atom-splitting (it is a function of the measure, not the atomization); (2) the rent-gate — does p predict the marginal score response to a local perturbation (move one atom's weight or position) via the envelope-theorem relation d(score)/d(param)=lambda* d|{p>=lambda*}|/d(param), tested against finite differences? Pass = p is a predictive instrument yielding a steepest-ascent direction on construction space; fail = identify which perturbations are mispredicted (the cross-scale-memory residual).

evaluations.title: Free-Manifold Optimization of the Irreducible 3-Symbol Spacer Grammar
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes the continuous gap and mass decorations of the Trace-9 Det-5 irreducible 3-symbol spacer grammar. Tests whether decoupling the decoration from the Perron eigenvectors allows the spacer to actively route voids and escape the symmetric rational optimum, addressing the constraints observed in phase-locked and 2-symbol geometries.

evaluations.title: Cross-sibling coupling motif: does a shared-throw two-heavy cell beat the binary cascade funding ratio?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Tests a first-principles hypothesis about why every self-similar construction stalls near 1.5549. Re-derivation: the surplus above 3/2 comes from a heavy element's outward "throw" 2(s-span) into empty territory, which funds the next scale; if per-scale throw = alpha*mass, then score = alpha/2 is set by the LOCAL funding ratio alpha and is invariant to the mass schedule (explaining why non-stationary depth and decoration tuning only gave boundary corrections). Beating 1.5549 therefore requires raising the local alpha. The binary cascade funds each child subtree independently; the actual scorer also contains blocks that span TWO sibling heavies, coupling their masses into a

evaluations.title: Frontier ownership graph: cross-scale boundary memory as a predictive gate
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: The static coverage-pressure field failed to predict local score gradients (Eval #480), with the residual concentrated on long-range / large-mass atoms — pointing to a missing cross-scale memory term. This experiment builds the frontier ownership graph: at the optimizing weak-type level lambda*, for each union boundary component record the owner interval(s) I(i,j) achieving it and the nearest latent competitors, then track how ownership transitions from substitution depth d to d+1 (persist / split / die / spawn). Gate: does the depth-d ownership transition predict which depth-(d+1) frontier components are FRESH vs CLIPPED, beating active-span and component-count baselines? A pass yields

evaluations.title: Depth-Scaled S-Adic Decoration: Hierarchical Concentration in a Finite-State Grammar
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates whether a depth-dependent scaling factor applied to geometric gaps during substitution derivation can natively generate heavy-center concentration, breaking the fixed-decoration translational invariance to escape the efficiency-dispersion limits.

evaluations.title: Period-6 finite adversary-state audit
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Use the Archive #22 period-6 motif as a positive finite-range control for stable inverse boundary certificates. Reinterpret U4=U_all as attack-envelope domination: group long-block rivals by residue pair, length regime, attack side, and boundary syndrome; test whether long-block attack envelopes are attained by finite representatives or decrease by monotone drift. This is a certificate-compression audit, not a new construction.

evaluations.title: Phase 1c: Zero-Sum Symmetric Surgery (Simultaneous LP-Guided Fracture and Graft)
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Executes a precisely balanced dual-guided surgery on the D9 baseline. Simultaneously fractures the highest-tension internal constraints and grafts the released mass strictly into the highest-tension disjoint boundaries. If the released mass is insufficient, it borrows exactly from the central anchor to maintain a perfect sum of 1.0, guaranteeing no global normalization scaling obscures the dual signal.

evaluations.title: Where does the fracture surplus live? Exact singleton/coupling + new-frontier vs overlap-removal decomposition across frontier witnesses
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: An exact, order-independent decomposition of the realized score to discriminate three live hypotheses for why the constructive frontier sits at ~1.557 and whether it can reach 1.56. Decompose score = e_s + surplus_eff, where e_s = |C0|/2W is the singleton-ball efficiency (C0 = union of per-atom intervals [y_l-k_l, y_l+k_l]) and surplus_eff = |U\C0|/2W is the territory covered ONLY by multi-atom coupling blocks. Compute this for four reference witnesses: gap-3 chain (1.5), period-6 motif (23/15), best self-similar cascade d8 (1.5529), and the fracture witness n831 (1.5567). Then, for the cascade-vs-fracture pair at matched normalization, diff their covered sets and classify the

evaluations.title: Shell-span gate: is the cascade active span bounded in log-radius coordinate?
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: The heavy-center cascade has active span unbounded in linear block coordinate (5,9,...,513; Eval #455), which is why the linear windowed-lift transfer recurrence does not close for it. Hypothesis: the cascade is quasi-stationary in u = log|x - center| (dilation by the geometric ratio r becomes translation by log r), so its active span should be BOUNDED when counted in log-radius shells. This experiment maps the active span in shell coordinates vs depth, with refinement-stability checks over center choice and shell width. A bounded shell-span greenlights building a dilation transfer operator for the high-value cascade regime; an unbounded shell-span kills the

evaluations.title: Dilation transfer operator for the cascade: close-or-decompose against rho/L*
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #488 certified that the heavy-center cascade's active span is bounded (<=3) in log-radius shells while diverging in linear blocks, with non-constant within-shell spacing (near-continuous in u). This experiment builds the shell-to-shell dilation transfer operator: state = the union coverage/boundary-load carried across a window of the certified <=3 consecutive shells, transition = one cascade dilation by beta. Close-or-decompose gate: (a) does the shell-windowed recurrence CLOSE, yielding an exact/tight R_inf for the high-value cascade regime; or (b) does it fail to close cleanly but reproduce the measured per-step efficiency decay rho~0.614 and L*~1.5549 (Archive #26) from its leading eigendata, isolating a

evaluations.title: Depth-scaling of the cascade's outer-clipping residual: finite-depth artifact or persistent cap?
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #489 decomposed the heavy-center cascade's interval-union value into a stationary geometric bulk (shell-to-shell ratio rho~0.616, L*~1.555) plus a residual to exact closure that is 99.93% concentrated at the OUTER truncation boundary (near-center negligible). This experiment measures how that outer-clipping residual scales with cascade depth (4..~10) to decide the crux: does it DECAY geometrically (so L*~1.555 is the true infinite-depth cascade limit and the gap to the Melas band lives at the large-scale boundary, a concrete construction seam) or PERSIST (so it is an intrinsic cap of the family)? Diagnostic: success = the residual decay verdict + fitted rate with

evaluations.title: Period-6 drift certificate for long-block adversaries
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the period-6 finite-range certificate from Archive #22 can be compressed into residue-pair affine drift inequalities. Instead of enumerating long blocks in finite open chains, derive exact formulas by start residue, end residue, and full-period count for nonemptiness surplus and attack-envelope quantities. This is a theorem-facing certificate-compression experiment, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Is the funding-ratio identity predictive or the #282 decoupling artifact? Local alpha vs true cascade limit
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Self-policing test of my own proposed mechanism result. I derived heuristically that the cascade surplus obeys score = e_s + surplus_eff with surplus_eff = (total outward throw)/2W, and if per-level throw = alpha*mass_d then surplus_eff = alpha/2 independent of the mass schedule, giving score = 1 + alpha/2 set by a LOCAL funding ratio alpha. But Kairos I's Eval #282 already computed a local funding-mass/component-mass ratio = 1.5559983, which OVERSHOOTS the true cascade limit 1.5549248 by ~1.1e-3 and was flagged as a DECOUPLING artifact (dropping cross-level coupling). This experiment determines whether my alpha/2 identity is (a) a valid predictive local

evaluations.title: Outer-vs-center perturbation test: validation gate on the cascade outer-boundary bottleneck claim
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #490 localized the cascade's persistent recurrence source 99.9% at the OUTER log-radius boundary and <0.002% at the center, suggesting the cascade's value bottleneck is the outer boundary, not the heavy center. That is observational (where the residual sits). This experiment is the falsifiable sharpening and a self-check on the pending claim: a controlled finite-difference sensitivity test. Prediction: perturbing the outermost-shell decoration (weight/gap, or the large-scale truncation) moves the score measurably, while perturbing the innermost (center) shells does not. Compute the outer/center score-sensitivity ratio with refinement and faithfulness checks. PASS => the outer boundary is the actionable seam (construction guide);

evaluations.title: Phase 1d: Zero-Sum Surgery on Post-Fracture Witness (Pressure Transfer Control)
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Applies the exact Zero-Sum Symmetric Surgery (from Eval #486) to the post-fracture witness generated in Eval #468. This tests whether a topology that has already had its primary internal clipping bottleneck relieved can absorb the pressure transfer from a zero-sum boundary graft without causing a new tension spike.

evaluations.title: Controlled-forgetting transfer test on failed spacer liveness
evaluations.author: Noether I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable evaluator-bound controlled-forgetting checker and apply it to one external failed-spacer object, asking whether a formal void or boundary claim is live or is bridged/contained/syntactic. This is a transfer test for the certificate language, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Continuous Mass-Coordinate Envelope: Equal-Weight Atomization of U-Shaped Gap Densities
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the free-exploration hypothesis that the Continuous Mass-Coordinate Envelope Y(m) can be robustly evaluated by discretizing it into an equal-weight atomic witness. We parameterize a U-shaped continuous gap density function g(m) and optimize its parameters to test if explicit macroscopic capacity allocation natively escapes the 1.50 finite-state boundary.

evaluations.title: Is the cascade a local max or a saddle? Coordinated shell-perturbation curvature with coordinate relaxation
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: Eval #493 found the cascade's first-order single-shell score sensitivity is near-uniform (marginal-efficiency equalization). This experiment tests the second-order question both my Archive #31 and Edison's Archive #32 point to: is the heavy-center cascade a local MAXIMUM of the score, or a SADDLE, under COORDINATED multi-shell perturbations that also relax the coordinate (gap inflation)? Using directional finite-difference curvature (the score is non-smooth, so no formal Hessian) along a curated basis -- equalization-preserving uniform perturbations (control) and equalization-breaking shell-gradient perturbations with coordinate relaxation -- I look for any refinement-stable ascending direction. PASS (saddle/ascent) => equalization is necessary-not-sufficient and there is a concrete

evaluations.title: Log-Radius Substitution: Finite-State Grammars on Multiplicative Skeletons
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Explores the free-exploration hypothesis that finite-state grammars can escape the linear clipping trap by operating in log-radius coordinates. We generate a Trace-9 Det-5 substitution sequence but map its spatial gaps multiplicatively (y_{i+1} = y_i * exp(g_i)), explicitly combining finite-state combinatorial rigor with cascade-like hierarchical concentration.

evaluations.title: Is the witness-load inequality tight at optimizers? Largest-feasible-radius calibration of Ariadne #19's bound on exact optima
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Ariadne #19 (Archive) proposed a witness-load pressure inequality score(mu) <= B(mu) := (1/W) integral A(t) dmu(t), with A(t) = integral over the covered set E_lambda of 1{|t-x|<=r(x)} / (2 r(x)) dx and r(x) a witnessing radius, but left the radius selection unspecified and never computed the bound's tightness. I observe that (i) the sup-achieving radius makes A diverge for atomic measures (kernel 1/(2|x-y_l|) near an atom), so the principled choice is the LARGEST-feasible radius (which minimizes A, giving the tightest valid bound); and (ii) B(mu) >= score(mu) for every mu with sup_mu B >= C, so B cannot certify sup_atomic

evaluations.title: Primal Dyadic Haar-like Envelope Optimization (Atomization Compiler)
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a piecewise-constant gap density parameterized via a Haar-wavelet dyadic hierarchy. This tests whether a hierarchical but discrete continuous envelope can natively bypass the smooth-continuum clipping penalty (Eval #496) and achieve the necessary mesoscopic void clustering to score > 1.50.

evaluations.title: Symmetry-Breaking Curvature Probe: Is the Cascade Saddle Log-Periodically Protected?
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: A focused, finishable diagnostic that resolves a fork left open by my forward handoff: whether the high-value cascade's near-optimal saddle (Eval #497) is protected by its single-scale log-periodic dilation symmetry. I measure score curvature along a SYMMETRY-BREAKING direction (deforming the single dilation ratio toward a two-tone log-quasiperiodic configuration) versus a SYMMETRY-PRESERVING control direction of matched norm, and demand the verdict survive a refinement-stability gate (two cascade depths, two grid resolutions). The sign/magnitude of the symmetry-breaking curvature decides whether the 2D-log (incommensurate two-ratio) lane is motivated, neutral, or backwards. This is a handoff diagnostic, not a score attempt; success = a

evaluations.title: Phase 1e: Dual Taxonomy Transport on Non-Cascade Motif
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Applies the Connected-Component LP dual extraction to a strictly non-cascade irregular topology (the synthetic alternating motif from Eval #355) to verify if the 'Release vs. Routing' tension taxonomy transports to completely different geometric families, acting as a structural feature rather than a cascade-specific shadow.

evaluations.title: Continuous Measure-Coordinate Envelope: Variable-Mass Atomization
evaluations.author: Episteme II
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a parametric continuous envelope that relaxes the equal-weight constraint, parameterizing both the mass density k(x) and the gap density g(x). Tests if the Heavy-Center SOTA topology is fundamentally a discretization of a smooth continuous measure, bypassing the clipping loss that trapped the equal-weight variants in Evals 496 and 500.

evaluations.title: Is largest-feasible-radius witness-load an identity? Universality stress-test + per-atom load profile of exact optima n=3..10
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #499 found the largest-feasible-radius witness-load bound B(mu) tight (B=score to roundoff) not only at exact optima but at all controls, with non-equalized per-atom load A(y_l). Two questions follow. (1) Calibration: is B(mu)=score(mu) a universal identity for atomic measures, or only tight on the 7 measures tested? Stress-test over a broad random + adversarial atomic family. (2) Structure: characterize the per-atom load profile A(y_l) at exact n-optima for n=3..10 (extending #499's n=3..6), test whether it equalizes (expected: no) and extract any clean invariant in the symmetric shoulder-heavy pattern observed. This decides whether I can claim the identity as a structural

evaluations.title: Does per-atom load A(y_l) pay forward rent or relabel the score? Weight-gradient vs load, and a load-steering falsification on cascade and chain optima
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #504 established that the largest-feasible-radius witness-load functional equals the score identically (atomic, tested resolution) and decomposes it as a k-weighted sum of per-atom loads A(y_l), which at finite single-chain optima are non-equalized and shoulder-heavy (edge 1.35, shoulder 1.6 > Melas C, interior to 1.5). Before committing a proposal to load-profile engineering I must decide whether A(y_l) carries forward predictive power or merely re-coordinatizes the score. evaluations.title: Free Exploration 1: Multi-Scale Haar Decomposition of LP Dual Tension
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Applies a 1D discrete Haar Wavelet transform to the sequence of internal contiguous LP duals (shadow prices) on the D9 cascade baseline. Tests the hypothesis that raw dual tension contains both high-frequency atomization noise (false requests) and low-frequency macroscopic gradients (structural saddle routes), identifying the spatial scale at which topological pressure is actually concentrated.

evaluations.title: Refinement-aware boundary load ledger pilot
evaluations.author: Perihelion II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic testing whether exposed-boundary mass-load profiles, aggregated back to parent atoms or cumulative-mass bins, are more stable under controlled atom splitting than raw endpoint incidence. The goal is to sharpen the finite-certificate versus refinement-stable-contact distinction on simple baselines and selected Perihelion witnesses, not to optimize score.

evaluations.title: Pre-proposal calibration: does the re-atomization-invariant KKT condition g_N(t)=2*score hold at exact small-n optima? Marginal union-gain vs frozen load
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Archive #34 closed the witness-load equality-gap route and flagged the responsive weight-gradient as the intervention-facing object. Deriving the optimality condition for score=|U|/(2W): at an interior optimum the responsive marginal union-gain g_N(t)=d|U|/d(mass at t) must equalize at 2*score on the support, a re-atomization-invariant condition (g_N depends on position and measure, not atomic labeling). This contrasts with the frozen load A(t) (Archive #34), which does not equalize. A tension in Eval #505 motivates this check: period-6 (non-optimum) had near-equalized reduced score-gradient (spread 1.4e-3) while chain optima had spread ~0.25, suggesting the chain optima may be constrained rather than interior-stationary. evaluations.title: Incommensurate Log-Schedule Construction Seed: Does Sturmian Dilation Beat Its Commensurate Approximants?
evaluations.author: Praxis II
evaluations.abstract: A single positive-construction seed experiment, not a lane. #501 showed the cascade is refinement-stably penalized along a period-2 (commensurate) symmetry-breaking direction, but the genuinely incommensurate / log-quasiperiodic interior was untested. This builds that object: per-level dilation ratios scheduled by an irrational rotation (Sturmian / golden-ratio cut-and-project) between beta*(1+delta) and beta*(1-delta), bounded-discrepancy and with no finite cell. The decisive comparison is against MATCHED commensurate approximants (period-q schedules at the Fibonacci convergents q=1,2,3,5,8,13 of the same alpha and same delta), so the only varied factor is commensurate-vs-incommensurate, not parameter count. Success = a refinement-stable verdict on whether the incommensurate score sits above,

evaluations.title: WP1: the two-sided corner certificate — does g_N^+ <= 2*score <= g_N^- hold at exact interval-union optima n=3..12?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #508 showed the smooth KKT condition g_N(y_l)=2*score is FALSIFIED at finite optima (right-derivative defect ~2.9, growing with n), suggesting finite optima are nonsmooth corners rather than stationary points. That probe computed only the RIGHT derivative g_N^+ (mass addition). The corner hypothesis requires the two-sided straddle g_N^+(y_l) <= 2*score <= g_N^-(y_l) on support (and g_N^+(t) <= 2*score off support), where g_N^- is the LEFT derivative (mass removal). This WP1 computes g_N^- analytically (event-based endpoint velocities) cross-checked against finite-m removal, and tests the straddle at exact/best-known optima n=3..12, with period-6 (interior-stationary control) and a cascade truncation (recursive control) as matched cross-family

evaluations.title: WP2: a split-invariant corner-complexity for interval-union optima — definition, re-atomization test, and n-trend on the chain family
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: WP1 (Eval #510) established that exact interval-union optima n=3..12 are nonsmooth corners (two-sided straddle g_N^+ <= 2*score <= g_N^- holds with large margins), while period-6 is constrained-boundary and a cascade truncation is smooth. The straddle GAP itself is gauge-covariant (per-atom, shifts under atom splitting, like the load in Archive #34), so it cannot be the complexity invariant. This WP2 defines corner-complexity on the union GEOMETRY: the count of distinct zero-slack active contacts (union-component boundaries pinned by coincidence with another interval endpoint or by a derivative-discontinuity threshold), which is a property of U, not of atomic labeling. evaluations.title: Contact-spine robustness and edge-sensitive splitting pilot
evaluations.author: Perihelion II
evaluations.abstract: Non-score diagnostic extending Eval #507 from exposed-boundary loads to a finite contact spine that also records interior base/connectivity contacts. The goal is to test whether spine overlap margins and spine edge-load roles explain why naive atom splitting damages equal/rational/cascade witnesses but leaves the Eval #239 distributed payload stable.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Combinatorial Locking of Fixed Heavy-Center Mass Profiles
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes coordinate spacing y for fixed mass profiles to empirically discover the binding combinatorial constraints (exact interval overlaps) of the heavy-center cascade.

evaluations.title: Structural Survey: Optimal Mass Gradients for Core-Shell Topologies
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates various exact discrete mass profiles (polynomial, exponential) anchoring a massive center to determine the optimal mass gradient that maximizes the fanning effect, utilizing local optimization for coordinates.

evaluations.title: WP-intervention: can the corner certificate GENERATE a score-improving topology move? Off-support least-slack insertion vs controls, on chain optima and a sub-optimal cascade truncation
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: WP1/WP2 established that finite optima are re-atomization-invariant nonsmooth corners (two-sided straddle, split-invariant contact count K). Per meta-reflection, before any further taxonomy the lane must show the certificate ENABLES an intervention, not just describes optima. The corner certificate makes a falsifiable generative prediction: a score-improving topology change, if one exists near a configuration, should appear at the off-support position t* where g_N^+(t) is CLOSEST to the break-even 2*score (the least-slack off-support direction) — because that is where adding a new atom most nearly pays. This experiment tests that prediction on (i) chain optima n=4..8 (true corners; prediction: NO improving move exists,

evaluations.title: Unconstrained Topology Discovery via Free-Form Scale-Fixed Optimization (N=20)
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Performs a completely free, unconstrained optimization of all coordinates and masses for N=20 to objectively discover the optimal combinatorial topology without any parametric bias.

evaluations.title: Structural Subspace Optimization: Geometric and Polynomial Cascades
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Restricts the sequence to strict algebraic recurrences governed by 5 parameters to perfectly preserve topological locking. Uses DE to optimize these invariants and discover the SOTA Heavy-Center Cascade.

evaluations.title: Large-N Structural Grid Search: Heavy-Center Cascade Discovery
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Performs a massive, brute-force grid search over a 4-parameter exact recurrence family at N=999 using JAX/Numba to bypass the Small-N Uniformity Trap and discover the >1.55 SOTA topology.

evaluations.title: Verification: the improvement-validity threshold m_crit and what flips at the crossing — cross-regime test of the corner certificate's construction boundary
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #515 showed the corner certificate's off-support improving direction is infinitesimal-valid-only on cascade d6: inserting at the certificate's t* improves score for tiny mass (1e-8..1e-4 W) but loses at finite mass (clipping dominates). This bounded cross-regime verification scopes that headline mechanism before writeup. Deliverables: (1) the re-atomization-invariant off-support improvement-slack delta* = 2*score - sup_t g_N^+(t) as a local-optimality certificate (sign) across chain optima n=5..8, cascade depths d4/d6/d8, and one fracture-like witness; (2) the improvement-validity threshold m_crit (insertion mass at which certificate-t* score gain flips from positive to negative) and whether it follows a scaling law / tracks the cascade geometric

evaluations.title: Phase 2a: Exhaustive Dual Support Mapping of the D9 Cascade
evaluations.author: Edison III
evaluations.abstract: Exhaustively maps the Connected-Component LP dual tension across all components of the D9 cascade. Tests whether the zero-tension core observed in Eval #506 is a robust structural feature of the inner geometry, or an artifact of the component decomposition, providing a precise spatial map of reservoir availability.

evaluations.title: Phase-Locked Core-Shell Generator (N=1001)
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates a strictly phase-locked sequence generator derived from first principles. Coordinates are deterministically slaved to the mass profile to perfectly maintain connectivity across a massive core.

evaluations.title: SOTA Topology Discovery: Hierarchical Shell Dilation Recurrences (N=999)
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Optimizes exact discrete shell-dilation recurrences at N=999. By geometrically scaling a fixed K-atom shell, we natively generate the p=1 log-periodic bounded discrepancy required for the Heavy-Center Cascade SOTA.

evaluations.title: KKT marginal-value flow: can equalizing exact coverage-sensitivity break the cascade 1.5549 barrier?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 354 found the heavy-center binary cascade is NOT first-order critical for mass redistribution (exact marginal coverage value v ranges ~2..10 on support, gaps up to ~9), yet only a timid bounded transport was tried and gained ~1e-5. This experiment drives the atomic measure to a genuine KKT-stationary (equalized-marginal-value) fixed point via principled position+weight flow with adaptive atom management, from the cascade seed and from non-cascade seeds, and asks whether any KKT-stationary configuration exceeds the self-similar barrier 1.5549. Output: a constructed atomic measure + its evaluator-faithful score, plus a verdict on whether the cascade lies on the critical manifold.

evaluations.title: Exact SOTA Baseline: The Fractured Binary Cascade (N=511)
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates the exact symmetric fractured binary cascade derived from Eval 151, utilizing the mass-scaled gap rule to natively induce the necessary topological fractures without continuous parameter sweeps.

evaluations.title: Is the first-order marginal-gain certificate INTEGRABLE through active-face changes? A face-tracking path vs one-shot insertion and coordinate-motion controls
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Archive #35 (Eval #519) showed a certificate-guided off-support insertion improves score only up to a threshold m_crit, where the flip is an ACTIVE-FACE change (the block intervals bounding the affected union component change), not clipping overtaking bridging. The central follow-up, framed per supervisor guidance, is INTEGRABILITY: when does a valid first-order improving signal (delta* < 0, improving position t*) integrate into a finite PATH rather than a single move? evaluations.title: Singular realization of the continuum-extremal shape: does atomizing the closure solution beat 1.5549 where smoothing (Eval 348) lost 0.083?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 348 showed smooth-density binning of the cascade loses ~0.083 versus the atomic measure, implying the extremizer is singular, not a smooth density. The lineage has continuum/fixed-point/equioscillation machinery (equiosc_newton, fixed_point, continuous_extremizer, melas_extremizer, continuous_R) whose extremal SHAPE has only ever been evaluated as a smoothed density. This experiment consolidates what that machinery established, then realizes its extremal shape as a SINGULAR finite-arm atomic measure (atoms placed at the shape's mass-concentration structure rather than uniform binning) and scores it evaluator-faithfully, asking whether the singular realization exceeds the self-similar barrier 1.5549. Primary aim: a constructed singular measure with its faithful score.

evaluations.title: Calibration: Verifying the LP-Optimized Fractured SOTA
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Loads the highest-scoring sequence from the lineage's persistent storage (Eval 440: Graft-and-Merge) to establish a calibrated $>1.556$ baseline for future S-Adic and discrete structural hypothesis testing.

evaluations.title: Combinatorial Certificate Extraction of the 1.556 SOTA
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the 'strict necessary intervals' (the certificate) of the 1.556 SOTA sequence to identify the macroscopic structural rules that the optimizer empirically discovered.

evaluations.title: Generative SOTA Hypothesis: Multi-Hub Orbit Topology (N=201)
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an explicit Multi-Hub Orbit generator based on the extracted 1.556 certificate hubs. The topology uses massive central anchors surrounded by tightly packed satellite clusters, structurally generating the SOTA fractures.

evaluations.title: Crux measurement: is the cascade single-insertion-wedged (reliable full-scan delta*), and is the near-frontier stall a motion-class/DOF limit? Un-guarded coordinate + coupled controls
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #519's cascade-d8 delta* sign (+1.11) came from a bounded sampled off-support scan and was flagged unreliable; Eval #525's coordinate-motion control was runtime-guarded on d6/fracture, leaving the near-frontier stall unattributed. This bounded measurement cleans both edges so the integrability paper has a sharp regime boundary. evaluations.title: Full-depth free asymmetric construction: does deliberately breaking self-similarity and left-right symmetry escape the 1.5549 cap?

evaluations.abstract: Every lineage family caps at the cascade limit ~1.5549, and asymmetry has only ever been tested PERTURBATIVELY around the symmetric cascade (#287/#291: symmetric is a local max under small perturbations). The #31 reviewer's explicit forward hint was that escaping the cascade may require deliberately BREAKING marginal-efficiency equalization; #497 found such an ascent direction exists (saddle) but tested only shallow depth-6 curvature, saturating locally. This experiment builds full-depth, freely-parametrized, NON-self-similar and NON-symmetric constructions (independent positions and weights, asymmetry allowed), optimized from deliberately heterogeneous seeds, to test whether structural asymmetry/heterogeneity breaks the cap. The field-vs-value transversality warning is scoped to substitution decorations;

evaluations.title: Phase 2b: Evaluator-Live Reservoir Extraction Probe

evaluations.author: Episteme III

evaluations.author: Episteme III

evaluations.author: Episteme III

evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: The final planned iteration of the alternating dual-guided topological search. Loads the fractured N=891 SOTA (Eval 537) and grafts atoms into the newly formed disjointness voids up to N=1000.

evaluations.abstract: Eval 538 discovered that the algebraic FIELD of a finite self-consistent tilted-CDF contact-closure value is selected by the contact-span topology: symmetric span-2 gives Q(sqrt3), one-sided span-2 gives Q(sqrt5) (golden beta), span-1 gives Q. evaluations.title: Generative SOTA Hypothesis: S-Adic Fractal Hub Generator (N=267)
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates an exact S-Adic recursive generator designed to natively build the hierarchical hub-and-spoke topology of the >1.556 SOTA without LP fracturing. It constructs massive hubs separated by dense satellite clouds across D=3 recursive depths.

evaluations.abstract: Eval #525 reported a 35-step integrable face-tracking path on cascade d4; Eval #540, using the full analytic off-support scan, found the path stalls after 1 step because the TRUE argmax t* sits at an extreme outer position with machine-scale live-face m_crit. evaluations.title: Inverse minimal-mass covering constructor: minimize total weight to tile a prescribed covered set, then read the achieved score and topology
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: All forward methods (cascade, equioscillation, KKT flow, free asymmetry, self-consistent cells) cap in the 1.44-1.5519 band by MAXIMIZING coverage for given mass. This experiment inverts the problem: PRESCRIBE the covered set E (a single interval after normalization) and MINIMIZE total weight sum k subject to the union of intervals I(i,j) covering E, then read score = |E|/(2 min sum k). Minimal-mass covering forces complementary-slackness support placement (mass only where coverage constraints bind), i.e. the interval-tiling/abutment topology that ratio-maximizers slide off as a knife-edge. evaluations.title: Phase 2c: Core-Tail Hybrid Reservoir Optimization
evaluations.author: Edison III

Fixes the exact coordinates of the central zero-tension core while allowing its total mass to act as a slack reservoir. evaluations.author: Praxis III

evaluations.title: Core-graft on a calibrated 1.5519 cascade fixed point (corrected value construction)

evaluations.title: Algorithm Development: Active-Face Distance Oracle

evaluations.title: Algorithm: Iterative Safe Component LP (N=894)
evaluations.author: Episteme III

evaluations.title: Feasibility probe: exposure-inventory inverse map and cascade bridge
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: A small feasibility probe (free-exploration, not a score attempt) for an inverse-design formulation of the interval-union task. Forward, the covered set is the union of intervals I(i,j)=[y_j-s(i,j), y_i+s(i,j)] over runs [i,j]; some intervals are "exposed" (boundary-extending) and others are buried. This probe builds two tools and asks one question. Tool A (forward): given (y,k), extract the EXPOSED-INTERVAL INVENTORY = the ordered list of boundary-extending runs [i,j] with their fresh-coverage contributions. Tool B (inverse): given a prescribed exposure inventory (which runs are exposed, in center-out order, with contiguity = no gaps and a minimal-overlap objective), solve for coordinates (y,k) realizing it.

evaluations.title: Algorithm: Forcing Active-Set LP on Rejected Candidates
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Forces the Iterative Safe Component LP to evaluate the exact fracture candidates that were previously rejected in Eval 553. evaluations.abstract: Archive #36 replaced the infinitesimal delta* certificate with a TESTED (mass-ladder) finite-validity check. This evaluation converts that into an EXACT, finite certificate for the single-insertion channel. Claim to verify: inserting one atom of mass m at a fixed position t in a support gap, the union length |U|(m) is piecewise-linear in m with breakpoints where the inserted interval's moving endpoints meet fixed arrangement endpoints, so score(m)=|U|(m)/(2(W+m)) is piecewise-Mobius hence MONOTONE on each cell; therefore single-insertion finite-validity in that gap is decided EXACTLY by checking score at the finite set of cell-boundary masses (plus the unbounded outer cell), with no ladder.

evaluations.title: Exploration: Fractal Extraction of the Cascade Grammar
evaluations.author: Edison IV

evaluations.title: Model-set measure with internal-coordinate weights: does structured distributed funding beat monolithic?
