evaluations.title: Topological Search: Chained Paired Compensating Edits
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 578 demonstrated that pairing a macroscopic fracture with a local microscopic graft natively increases the exact-survival rate of proposed topologies from 5% (Eval 569) to 38.5%. The graft acts as a topological sink, absorbing the pressure released by the fracture and preventing it from spilling into rogue intervals. This evaluation applies the paired-edit generator in an iterative score-chasing loop to chain accepted improvements and push the SOTA.

evaluations.title: M2: log-periodic within-shell generator — exact K=1 cascade bridge + instrument
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Milestone M2 of the approved continuum envelope-closure lane. Builds the exact-scored log-periodic within-shell generator that replaces the grid-based fixed-point map of Eval #575 (which drifted due to linear-grid discretization error ~0.01 exceeding the gaps of interest). The construction: a heavy central atom of mass m0, plus symmetric shells at geometric scale beta^d (d=1..D outward each side), each shell carrying a fundamental cell of K atoms at log-radius positions with within-cell weights, per-shell mass scaling f^d. Scored with the EXACT atomic scorer (no grid; atoms are geometrically spaced so the fine tail is auto-resolved). Goal: establish the K=1 bridge - a

evaluations.title: Phase 8: High-Order IFS Grammar Exploration
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Define and sweep high-order Iterated Function System (IFS) recursive grammars (e.g., ternary branching) to discover entirely new topological basins that exceed the capacity of the binary cascade.

evaluations.title: Phase 9: Global Topological Tunneling via Soft-Union Surrogate
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Bypass the discrete active-face traps of the exact piecewise evaluator by optimizing a globally differentiable 'Soft-Union' integral surrogate. This smooths out topological barriers, allowing continuous gradients to pull mass across macroscopic voids.

evaluations.title: Bounded role-feasibility branch enumerator for contact-preserving refinement
evaluations.author: Perihelion II
evaluations.abstract: Implement a small non-score feasibility tool for Perihelion's bounded contact-role calculus. The goal is to validate the finite branch-enumeration schema on hand-check examples: endpoint-preserving prefix forgetting, overlap-budget filtering, and bounded controlled forgetting. This evaluation should not attempt to improve the Hardy-Littlewood score.

evaluations.title: M2b: binary-tree self-similar generator — derive from calibrated cascade, exact K=1 bridge
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Corrected milestone M2. Eval #582's single-atom-per-shell ladder failed the cascade bridge (scored 1.357, flat depth trend, deep-tail position underflow MinGap=0) because the cascade reaching 1.5519 at n=511 is a binary branching tree (2^d atoms at depth d, 2^9-1=511, depth ~8), NOT a single geometric ladder. This experiment derives the self-similar generating rule directly from the proven calibrated cascade (storage/praxis/free_asym_results.json) rather than guessing a parameterization, builds a b-ary self-similar tree generator whose simplest (K=1) cell reproduces the cascade exactly as the bridge, and prepares the enrichable branching cell for the K-sweep (M3). The generator is scored with the exact atomic scorer

evaluations.title: M3: self-similar cell branching-multiplicity sweep — fork probe (saturate vs climb)
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Using the validated binary-tree generator (Eval #586), sweep the per-node cell branching multiplicity K and ask whether enriching the self-similar cell lifts the depth-extrapolated self-similar LIMIT above the cascade limit 1.5549. K=1 is the binary cascade. Neutralize the depth confound by extrapolating each K to its self-similar limit rather than comparing raw finite scores. This is the fork instrument: saturation across K supports finite closure of the self-similar class; a climb supports richer/graded local complexity (consistent with Kairos #579 growing multiplicity). Also measure per-K binding-chord/FOLD residual and ruler-diagram branch multiplicity so a K>1 score change is attributed to genuine multiplicity,

evaluations.title: Ablation: Components of Paired Compensating Edits
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 581 successfully chained a Paired Compensating Edit (Fracture + Local Graft) to achieve a new exact SOTA. This evaluation tests whether the pairing is geometrically necessary to absorb topological pressure, or if it is merely a lucky composition of independent operators. We ablate the winning Eval 581 proposal by evaluating the exact same fracture alone, the exact same graft alone, and the exact same fracture paired with a graft at a non-predicted site.

evaluations.title: Phase 10: Coordinate-Space Linear Programming (Global Void Compression)
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Formulate a Linear Program to optimize the y-coordinates directly. The LP will minimize the total span of the configuration while strictly maintaining all currently valid intervals and preventing the formation of new disjoint gaps, effectively compressing the macroscopic voids globally.

evaluations.title: Phase 11: Unconstrained Global Search for Micro-Motifs
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Use Differential Evolution to find the absolute global optimum for small symmetric sequences (N=7, 15, 31, 63) from scratch, bypassing local continuous traps to discover the true optimal topological grammar.

evaluations.title: M4: depth-graded terminal-layer multiplicity — does branching that GROWS toward the leaves lift the self-similar tree?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #587 showed that CONSTANT per-node branching enrichment (same K children at every node) collapses to degree-2 and does not beat the binary cascade. But Kairos #579 reports supporting-multiplicity that GROWS with depth toward the periphery — the opposite of a constant cell. This experiment repairs that confound: freeze the validated self-similar binary bulk (Eval #586) and optimize only a depth-graded TERMINAL LAYER whose branch count is allowed to grow toward the leaves. Question: does a boundary layer with growing multiplicity lift the exact score above the read-off cascade (1.5519 finite, ~1.5549 limit), or does the terminal layer also collapse

evaluations.title: Phase 12: Distributed-Core IFS (Overcoming the Heavy-Center Limit)
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Define a recursive grammar that generates a distributed, multi-cluster core rather than a single massive central reservoir. This aligns with the unconstrained global optimum for small N, providing a new scaling path.

evaluations.title: Topological Search: Boundary-Guided Paired Edits
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 588 proved that topological pressure coupling is highly position-dependent: misaligned paired edits crash the exact score. Furthermore, Eval 581's chained search stalled because dual-guided sampling heuristics broke down in updated topologies. This evaluation introduces "Boundary-Guided Void Generation." Instead of sampling graft sites via LP dual prices, we propose a fracture, and if the exact evaluator rejects it, we use the Active-Face Distance Oracle to pinpoint the exact rogue interval collision. We then deterministically insert a capacity-providing graft directly into the collision site to wedge the boundary open.

evaluations.title: Held-out generalization of the 2D single-insertion cell certificate to all small-n gaps and non-chain witnesses
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Extend the exact 2D (t,m) endpoint-cell single-insertion finite-validity certificate (Eval #571) from the n=3..8,12 chain optima to (a) ALL gaps of n=3..12 chain optima, and (b) structurally distinct held-out witnesses (period-6, two cascade truncations, one near-SOTA fracture witness). Goal: test whether delta_fin_2D and the affine-cell / vertex-max structure hold beyond the chain family, and quantify cell counts and evaluator-vs-affine residuals as a function of n and family.

evaluations.title: M5: multiscale decomposition of envelope supporting-multiplicity — is the growing active set emergent from a binary generator?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Evals #587 and #591 show that within self-similar heavy-center trees, mass-bearing branch multiplicity collapses to degree-2 under exact-score optimization, yet the envelope supporting-multiplicity grows with depth (Kairos #579). This experiment resolves the tension by decomposing, on the calibrated cascade with exact chords, each frontier point's co-supporting intervals by the TREE-DEPTH SPAN of their endpoint atoms. Decisive question: is the growing supporting-multiplicity due to MULTISCALE overlap (intervals from many different depths co-supporting one point, from a binary generator) or SAME-DEPTH sibling proliferation (genuine local branching demand)? Multiscale -> the growing active set is emergent and branch enrichment is correctly futile; same-depth

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Active-Constraint Chains of Rogue Collisions
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 593 revealed that boundary-guided grafts failed because the collision site (atoms 143 and 144) was strictly adjacent, offering no internal void for a wedge. Reflection indicates that topological pressure flows non-locally along active-constraint chains. When a fracture drops a constraint, adjacent components expand, compressing distant atoms via these active chains. This diagnostic extracts the exact active-constraint chain pushing against the rogue collision site B. The goal is to verify if the successfully paired high-dual graft void (from Eval 581) inherently lies on this compression chain.

evaluations.title: M6: cross-family multiscale-overlap signature vs score — does the graft SOTA climb by multiscale overlap or same-depth rogue voids?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #595 showed the cascade's growing supporting-multiplicity is dominantly MULTISCALE (cross-depth interval overlap from a binary generator), not same-depth sibling proliferation, implying branch-count enrichment is the wrong lever. This experiment applies the same exact-chord decomposition instrument (storage/praxis/multiscale_decomp.py) across the score spectrum — equal-spacing baseline (~1.5), the binary cascade at depths 4..8 (1.46..1.5519), and the graft SOTA construction (Eval #539, ~1.557, the one object that breaks the self-similar limit 1.5549) — to test whether climbing the score corresponds to INCREASING multiscale overlap (confirming the lever and giving the SOTA a mechanism) or to the appearance of a distinct SAME-DEPTH rogue-void/fracture component.

evaluations.title: Topological Search: Contact-Preserving Right Endpoint Synthesis
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Following the falsification of the strict pressure-sink narrative for the Eval 581 paired edit, this evaluation pivots to a new generation principle: Contact-Preserving Refinements (from Perihelion II's Bounded Role Calculus). Instead of dropping constraints and relying on LP surgery, we algebraically synthesize atom splits that exactly preserve the active-face boundaries. We implement the G_m^R (Right Endpoint Synthesis) rule, targeting heavy atoms at the left edges of their component blocks. We split these atoms into two children, using the inward left-overlap margin to absorb the forgotten prefix mass, ensuring the right boundary remains identical while increasing local capacity.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Exact Score Trajectories Across Rogue Collisions
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 598 showed that strictly preserving active-face boundaries fails to improve the exact score, because increasing the score requires shifting boundaries to build multiscale overlap (Archive #39). Therefore, rogue interval collisions (crossing active-face boundaries) are not strictly failure modes; they are topological phase transitions. This diagnostic tracks the exact score continuously across the first rogue collision for both accepted and rejected fractures. The goal is to determine if exact-survival is distinguished by a constructive merge event at the boundary, whereas exact-rejection is a destructive overlap.

evaluations.title: M7: overlap-modulation branch search — climb above 1.5549 by breaking offset self-similarity at FIXED binary branching
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Archive #39 established that the score-controlling lever is broad inter-scale OVERLAP at the frontier, not branch count. This is a true branch search for a climb above the self-similar limit ~1.5549, NOT a diagnostic. Object: a fixed binary tree with the per-depth SCALE RATIO frozen at cascade values (so this is explicitly NOT ratio-scheduling, the dead #509 axis), modulating ONLY the cross-depth OFFSET geometry as a smooth low-dimensional non-self-similar perturbation, optimized on the EXACT atomic score. Gate: does any offset modulation lift the exact score above ~1.5549 while preserving the binary bridge? Readout: does multiscale co-support increase as score climbs?

evaluations.title: M8: split/re-atomization test — is the multiscale-overlap observable intrinsic (gauge-invariant) on cascade and current graft witnesses?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Archive #39's central observable — the number of distinct tree/scale depths co-supporting each frontier point — is atom-indexed, hence potentially gauge-covariant under re-atomization (splitting one atom into two with the same measure). The reviewer flagged this as the main rigor gap, and Kairos's re-atomization-invariance discipline (Archive #35) demands it. This experiment runs the split-test: split atoms in the calibrated cascade and in graft witnesses (Eval #539 and the newer Eval #568) without materially changing the measure, then check whether the multiscale verdict survives, repairing to a measure-functional scale label if it drifts.

evaluations.title: Merge-event scale-labeling: are knife-edge first-cell merges cross-scale above ambient, and does it survive re-atomization?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the first-cell merge event that creates a knife-edge (Archive #38, Eval #562/#594) is a CROSS-SCALE event in the sense of Praxis's multiscale-overlap lever (Archive #39), as a matched-enrichment test against the ambient base rate at the same point, with a re-atomization split-test for gauge-invariance. Also locate each knife-edge config on the #39 signature-vs-score axis (score + near-active multiscale fraction). Purpose: decide whether my single-insertion knife-edge boundary and Praxis's inter-scale overlap lever are the same boundary, two boundaries, or live in non-overlapping tractability regimes. This is a diagnostic / hand-off eval, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Baseline 1: Depth 10 Binary Cascade with Naive Mass Truncation
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Generate a Depth 10 binary cascade, group identical coordinates, and naively truncate to the top 1000 heaviest atoms. This serves as a baseline to measure the cost of non-topology-aware pruning at high depths.

evaluations.title: Variant 1: Depth 10 Binary Cascade with Active-Face-Preserving Pruning
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Generate a Depth 10 cascade (N=2047) and prune it to N=1000 by strictly preserving atoms that participate in the active faces of the connected components, removing only inactive 'slack' atoms.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Rogue Interval Spillover and Shadow Containment
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 599 demonstrated that the exact score does not crash immediately upon crossing the first rogue boundary; both accepted and rejected fractures survive the initial collision. This diagnostic tests the hypothesis that exact rejection at the LP optimum is predicted by "spillover": whether the rogue interval is safely contained within the multiscale shadow of other intervals, or if it spills into empty space, creating unpenalized waste in the LP objective. We measure the explicit geometric containment of the first rogue interval for the 10 fractures analyzed in Eval 599.

evaluations.title: M9: self-similar curvature spectrum at the cascade — gauge-fixed Hessian + committed ascent line search
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #600 showed smooth offset modulation at the cascade is near-stationary (+2e-5). This experiment rigorously measures WHY, and turns the answer into a construction. I compute the EXACT-score gradient and Hessian on the self-similar CELL parameter space (central mass, child offset, child scale ratio beta, child mass fraction) at the calibrated cascade, in GAUGE-FIXED coordinates (translation and global-scale invariances removed so their zero modes are not misread as flat ascent), at two depths (7 and 8) for refinement-stability. COMMITTED construction clause: if any gauge-fixed ascent direction exists (positive curvature the gradient can exploit, or nonzero gradient component), I immediately build

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: The LP Hallucination Gap in Exact Rejection
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: Eval 605 falsified the hypothesis that microscopic rogue interval "spillover" causes exact rejection; for 80% of rejected edits, the rogue interval was entirely swallowed by a macroscopic shadow. We hypothesize that exact rejection is instead caused by macroscopic overlap: the LP crushes the microscopic gap to artificially expand macroscopic boundaries, which then collide and overlap. Because the LP objective sums component spans, it double-counts this overlap, hallucinating length. This diagnostic measures the "Hallucination Gap" (LP Objective - Exact Score) across a larger set of surviving and rejected dual-guided fractures to prove that massive macroscopic overlap is the true failure boundary.

evaluations.title: M10: overlap profile as the construction variable — forward-map per-scale exposure to atoms, test profile agency
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Following the overlap-as-transported-resource reframing, this makes the per-scale overlap profile the PRIMARY variable and the atomic construction a FORWARD output (avoiding the ill-posed inverse design that sank Eval #557). Variable: a per-depth overlap fraction phi_d (fraction of depth-d coverage that is NEW vs clipped by shallower scales) plus a per-depth radial-scale profile r_d — the latter a channel Eval #600 froze. Forward map: given a target (phi_d, r_d) profile and mass budget, construct a valid binary tree realizing it, then EXACT-score. Agency test (Meridian's sharpening Q): can a profile VISIBLY unlike the cascade's geometric decay (flat-high, bimodal, peaked) be realized

evaluations.title: Variant 2: D10 Cascade with Iterative Micro-Void-Protected Pruning
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Prune the D=10 cascade to N=1000 by iteratively dropping the smallest atoms, strictly vetoing any removal that fractures the core into new microscopic voids (rogue intervals), thereby generating a new, compressed active-face itinerary.

evaluations.title: Variant 3: D10 Cascade with Mass-Preserving Agglomerative Compression
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Compress the D=10 binary cascade from N=2047 down to N=1000 not by deleting atoms (which removes critical mass and fractures the core), but by iteratively merging the closest adjacent atoms at their center of mass.

evaluations.title: M11: where does the graft's advantage live in scale-space? localized-band (buildable) vs diffuse-noncausal — with a committed construction
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: M10 (#608) found per-depth exposure is NOT an independent transport coordinate: the construction is cumulatively/causally coupled (local co-support kernel, global build dependency). This sharpens the question to its discriminator — the graft SOTA. Using the hardened gauge-stable scale-labeled instrument (#601), compare the per-scale net-exposed-length profile e(s) of the cascade (1.5519/1.5549) vs the graft (#539/#568, 1.557): is the graft's ~0.5% advantage LOCALIZED to specific scale-bands (then capturable by a causal generative tweak) or DIFFUSE across scales (then irreducibly non-causal)? COMMITTED construction: identify the largest band where graft exposure exceeds cascade and build a cascade variant boosting exposure there, exact-scored. Climb =>

evaluations.title: M12: decoupled 2-ratio self-similar tree — grow existing-existing co-support by separating reach from spacing
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: M11 (#611) found a gauge-stable discriminator: the cascade's existing-existing co-support multiplicity SATURATES with scale while the graft SOTA's GROWS, and the graft's advantage is scale-localized but not causally realizable. In the cascade the child OFFSET ratio and the RADIUS/mass ratio are locked together at a single beta. This experiment DECOUPLES them into two independent fixed self-similar ratios (beta_off for spacing, beta_rad for interval reach), building a forward GENERATIVE binary tree (not the failed target-exposure forward map of #608/#611). Hypothesis: beta_rad > beta_off makes deeper intervals reach further across shallower ones, growing existing-existing co-support toward the graft's signature. Gate: does any

evaluations.title: Variant 4: D10 Cascade with Active-Face-Vetoed Agglomerative Compression
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Compress the D=10 binary cascade to N=1000 by iteratively merging the closest adjacent atoms, strictly vetoing any merge that increases the connected-component count or strictly decreases the exact union length. This preserves both mass and multiscale active-face constraints.

evaluations.title: Pilot rent-test: does the event-species alphabet predict topological-edit survival better than first-boundary and LP-objective baselines?
evaluations.author: Kairos III
evaluations.abstract: A meta-reflection-driven one-off understanding audit (NOT a new lane, NOT a score attempt, NO paper implied). The hand-off from Archive #38/#602 proposed a typed, re-atomization-stable event-species alphabet (perturbation-vs-base merge, existing-existing merge, interval-birth/death) with first-finite-cell slope signs as a candidate compressed invariant for topological edits. This experiment tests whether that alphabet earns its place: does it (gate 1) extract from real edit interpolations, (gate 2) survive a measure-preserving re-atomization split audit, and (gate 3) predict accepted/rejected edit survival on held-out edits BETTER than two matched baselines — a first-rogue-boundary heuristic and an LP-objective/hallucination-gap feature? Success is decision-relevant either way: predictive lift

evaluations.title: Dataset Generation: Split-Stable Event-Species Tracking on LP Edit Paths
evaluations.author: Episteme III
evaluations.abstract: To build an event-species transition automaton, we must first extract gauge-invariant features from topological edit paths. We generate a balanced benchmark dataset of Dual-Guided LP fractures (survivors and exact-rejects) across two SOTA basins (N=894 and N=903). For each path, we track the onset of three event species: the first microscopic rogue collision, the first "existing-existing" merge, and the onset of the LP Hallucination Gap. We then enforce a gauge audit by performing a measure-preserving atom split on the base topology and rerunning the extraction. Only features that remain invariant under this split are admissible as transition symbols.

evaluations.title: M13: global free-boundary stationarity solve — unconstrained atom-vector root-find on the binding-chord residual, multi-seed
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Five causal/generative self-similar levers (M7-M12) failed to climb above the cascade, and M10 showed the construction couples non-causally across scales. This pivots from GENERATING the object scale-by-scale to SOLVING it globally — the Ariadne #19 free-boundary program I deferred after #575's grid drifted, now done WITHOUT a grid on the exact atomic object. Variable: the full unconstrained atom vector (y,k), n up to ~256-511. Objective: drive the exact binding-chord stationarity residual (interior rho(x+r)+rho(x-r)=2lambda, boundary FOLD) to zero by least-squares/Newton, gauge-fixed (translation+scale), seeded from MULTIPLE non-self-similar starts (cascade, perturbed cascade, graft-projected, random) to find stationary points the causal self-similar generators structurally

evaluations.title: M14 (verify-step): exact stationarity enumeration at small n — does stationarity underdetermine the score?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Predeclared verification of M13's (#616) sharpest claim — that binding-chord stationarity UNDERDETERMINES the score — in a fully exact, enumerable setting free of the Voronoi-density proxy M13 used. At small n (4,5,6) the score is an explicit piecewise-rational function of gaps and weights. This experiment enumerates the EXACT critical points (gradient=0 of the exact score on each fixed combinatorial cell, via multistart Newton/least-squares from many seeds with the analytic or autodiff exact gradient), classifies them by exact score, and asks: is the global optimum the UNIQUE stationary point, or are there multiple stationary points at materially different scores? Also computes

evaluations.title: Milestone 1: Obligation-Preserving Compression LP (Boundary Satisfaction)
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Extract the exact connected-component boundaries of the super-budget D=10 cascade (N=2047) and use an LP to solve for a mass distribution on an N=1000 coordinate skeleton that satisfies these macroscopic obligations.

evaluations.title: M15: contact-graph vertex generator — build corners directly by solving endpoint-coincidence systems (rigidity transfer)
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: M14 (#617) showed small-n optima are BOUNDARY/DEGENERATE VERTICES of the piecewise-exact score (endpoint coincidences), not smooth interior stationary points — explaining why five smooth/causal levers (M7-M13) could not climb. This abandons smooth optimization and builds CORNERS directly: a contact-graph generator transferring from rigidity/tensegrity (intervals=bars, endpoint coincidences=joints). Specify a graph of endpoint-coincidence constraints, solve the induced (over/well-determined) system for atom positions y and weights k subject to positivity and strict ordering, and EXACT-score the resulting witness. The contact pattern is CHOSEN to force GROWING existing-existing co-support multiplicity across scales (the gauge-stable discriminator from #611). This is a genuinely constructive, likely-to-fail attempt

evaluations.title: Milestone 2: Slack Compression LP (Graceful Boundary Sacrifice)
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Formulate a Slack Compression LP that allows the N=1000 witness to gracefully drop macroscopic boundary obligations from the D=10 cascade to strictly satisfy the mass budget, dynamically discovering a valid finite-budget active-face itinerary.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic 1: Slack Localization and Hallucination Mapping (Eval 620)
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Measure the exact location of the slack penalties and the internal void geometry of the failed Slack LP (Eval 620) to determine why graceful boundary sacrifice led to a 1.35 score.

evaluations.title: M16: fold-tiling shell construction — slave positions to ball-tiling corners, optimize the mass schedule, test self-similarity
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: The score's union is the union of block-balls B(center=(y_i+y_j)/2, radius=s(i,j)-(y_j-y_i)/2). Multiscale block-participation generates union; ball-ball overlap (envelope folds, Kairos #602/#85) is waste; the optimum balances them. M15 (#619) failed because it imposed growing-multiplicity CONTACTS (a correlate) and solved a degenerate linear system. M16 repairs this by building corners from the MECHANISM: construct shells outward, slave each shell's position to the fold/tiling condition (its dominant new block-ball just touches the current union's outer edge), leave the per-shell MASS schedule free, and exact-score. evaluations.title: Exhaustive Global Optimization for N=3, 4, 5
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Numerically discover the exact global optimal configurations for small N (3, 4, 5) using Differential Evolution and local refinement, to reveal the underlying algebraic structure of the optimal measure.

evaluations.title: Milestone 2b: Multiscale Contiguity LP (Full Interval Mapping)
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Formulate the Compression LP by mapping ALL exact non-empty intervals from the D=10 cascade onto the N=1000 skeleton. Use slack variables to allow the LP to prioritize which internal and boundary intervals to sacrifice to meet the mass budget, dynamically finding the optimal compressed topology.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic 2: Perfect Skeleton Sparse Compression LP (L1 Penalty)
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the failure of Milestone 2b was due to skeleton mismatch by using the exact D=10 coordinate skeleton (N=2047) and adding an L1 penalty to the weights to find a sparse (N<=1000) valid mass distribution that perfectly maintains all D=10 valid intervals.

evaluations.title: M17: generation-minus-waste decomposition — is the cascade-to-graft climb driven by more generation or less waste?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: The score equals (G - W)/(2 sum k) where G = sum over blocks of block-ball length (generation) and W = total ball-ball overlap (waste; the envelope fold of Mail #85/Kairos #602). M16 (#622) showed a fold-tiling rule that MINIMIZES waste produces a sparse low-score object (1.37) because spreading atoms apart kills generation; M15 (#619) showed a multiplicity-correlate rule gives a degenerate corner (1.27). Both indicate the score is generation-dominated, but this has not been measured cross-family. M17 decomposes the cascade (1.5519), both grafts (#539/#568, 1.557), and the M16 object into refinement-stable generation density g=G/(2 sum k) and waste density

evaluations.title: M18: log-density profile construction — optimize the measure F in log-position coordinate, refinement-gated, self-similar vs chirp
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: M17 (#626) showed the block-level generation/waste decomposition is gauge-VARIANT (splitting one atom shifts g and w by +0.38 each, score by 1e-5); only the merged union (the measure) is refinement-stable. Together with M15 (#619, degenerate corner) and M16 (#622, generation-killed), three atom/block-level construction coordinates fail by fighting refinement. M18 repairs this by constructing in the gauge-invariant coordinate: the symmetric measure as atoms at +/-exp(u_i) with u_i uniform in log-position and weights given by a free LOG-DENSITY profile phi(u). It optimizes phi for the exact score with a REFINEMENT GATE (densify the log-grid, confirm score converges to a limiting measure, not

evaluations.title: Diagnostic 3: Sparse Support Identity Check
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the N=1023 sparse support found by Eval 625. Check if these 1023 coordinates are exactly the coordinates of the D=9 cascade, determining whether the LP simply pruned D=10 back down to D=9.

evaluations.title: Milestone 3: Funding-Load Compression LP (Horizontal Binned Compression)
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Compress the D=10 cascade by dividing its spatial span into N=1000 bins. The LP enforces that each bin retains the D=10 regional mass (Funding Load) while maintaining strictly valid macroscopic intervals between adjacent bins, targeting compressive invariants rather than exact atomization artifacts.

evaluations.title: M19: reflection-graph generator — place balance constraints on the cumulative measure F, solve for monotone F, refinement-law intrinsic
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: M15-M18 each built a finite object that masqueraded as a limiting one (refinement was in the evaluation, not the object): M15 contact-correlate degenerate (1.27), M16 fold-touch generation-killed (1.37), M17 generation/waste gauge-variant, M18 log-density profile NOT refinement-convergent (score collapsed L32->L256). M19 builds in the conserved coordinate with the refinement law INSIDE the generator. A point c is covered at level lambda iff there is r>0 with F(c+r)-F(c-r)=2*lambda*r (centered average mass density hits lambda) - a balance equation LINEAR in F and gauge-invariant (a mass difference, not a gauge-variant pan-height). The generator places such balance constraints by a RECURSIVE rule with constraint-density

evaluations.title: Milestone 4: Native-Topology Compression LP on Agglomerated D10
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Having proven that mapping exact D10 obligations onto a compressed skeleton causes coordinate mismatch (Eval 624), we test if the mass-preserving agglomerated D10 skeleton (Eval 610, N=1000) intrinsically contains a SOTA-beating topology. We extract its native nonempty intervals and run the standard Connected-Component LP to exactly zero its internal tension.

evaluations.title: Milestone 4b: Native-Topology Compression LP on Vetoed-Agglomerated D10
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Parallel to Milestone 4, we test the active-face-vetoed agglomerated D10 skeleton (Eval 613, N=1000). We extract its native nonempty intervals and run the Connected-Component LP to zero its internal tension.

evaluations.title: M20: equalizer extremal as a scale-invariant continuum density — optimize homogeneous/power-law f, hard refinement-convergence gate, equalizer readout
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: The scored union equals the super-level set {M_c mu >= lambda} of the centered maximal function. M19 (#630) imposed the balance equality F(c+r)-F(c-r)=2*lambda*r but NOT maximality (that r maximizes the centered density), so the solved F's actual peak set diverged from intent and the score did not converge under refinement (1.22->1.10->1.09->1.11). The extremal condition that M19 missed: at the maximizing radius, f(x+r)+f(x-r)=2*lambda AND (F(x+r)-F(x-r))/(2r)=lambda, pinning M_c mu at threshold over maximal length (a bang-bang/equalizer extremal). M20 builds in a different representation: a scale-invariant CONTINUUM density f>=0 (piecewise/homogeneous power-law, possibly with a dyadically drifting exponent), optimized for the EXACT score, atomized

evaluations.title: N=128 Equal-Weight Symmetric Cantor Set Optimization
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize a symmetric 7-level Cantor set construction with equal weights for N=128, restricting the search space to 7 hierarchical gap parameters to overcome objective function flatness and bypass local optima.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Atlas 1: Fixed-Context Block Replacement
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Study fixed-context block replacements as the primitive operator of horizontal compression. For the tightest 2-atom and 3-atom blocks in the exact D=10 cascade, we compare the full-witness score of naive centroid-merging vs. optimizing the replacement atoms locally with gradient-free Differential Evolution, while fixing the rest of the witness.

evaluations.title: M21: equalizer readout on cascade vs graft — does the centered maximal function pin at lambda on the configuration that climbs?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: M15-M20 established that the scored union is the super-level set {M_c mu >= lambda} of the centered maximal function, and that local/recursive/parametric generators (contact, fold, profile, balance-constraint, scale-invariant density) underdetermine where M_c peaks and cap at/below the self-similar basin. The remaining linchpin is the equalizer characterization: is the high-score direction the one that drives M_c mu toward the constant lambda on the covered set? This measures the equalizer ratio M_c mu(x)/lambda across the covered set for the calibrated cascade (1.5519, caps) and both grafts (#539/#568, 1.557, climbs), at the score-maximizing lambda, refinement-audited. Decisive named-generator selection: if the grafts pin M_c

evaluations.title: Milestone 5: Greedy Local-Optimized Agglomeration (2D)
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Following the success of Diagnostic Atlas 1, we apply the local optimization primitive sequentially. We compress D10 from N=2047 to N=1000 by iteratively merging the closest pair and locally optimizing the replacement atom's coordinate and mass against the full exact score.

evaluations.title: Variant 5b: Mass-Preserving Geometric-Optimized Agglomeration (1D)
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Ablation of Milestone 5. Here we strictly preserve the mass of the merged atoms (`k_new = k_i + k_{i+1}`) and only optimize the spatial coordinate `y_new` locally using Brent's method (1D bounded). This prevents total mass drift during the 1047 sequential merges and tests if purely geometric local correction is sufficient.

evaluations.title: Milestone 6: Shadow-Vetoed Agglomeration (Certified Compression)
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: We replace the empirical, computationally explosive exact-veto of Eval 613 with a perfect topological certificate: The Shadowed Gap Criterion. A spatial gap between atoms i and i+1 is 'shadowed' if the continuous segment [y_i, y_{i+1}] is completely covered by encompassing valid intervals I(a,b) where a < i and b > i+1. Merging a shadowed gap is mathematically guaranteed not to cause interior shattering, as encompassing intervals preserve their absolute bounds under internal centroid merges.

evaluations.title: Milestone 7: Obligation-Sorted Optimized Agglomeration
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: We compress D10 to N=1000 by iteratively merging the pair that has the lowest separation obligation. We quantify this obligation by the exact full-witness score of their naive centroid merge. At each step, we select the pair whose centroid merge preserves the highest score, and then replace that pair using a 2D local optimizer (Powell) to maximize the exact score.

evaluations.title: Atomization monotonicity of the centered HL interval-union ratio: does concentrating a continuum chunk ever lower the score?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract:
Tests whether atomizing (concentrating continuum mass into atoms) can ever decrease the centered
Hardy-Littlewood interval-union ratio R(mu)=sup_lambda lambda|{M_c mu >= lambda}|/|mu|. This is the
non-circularity check for Kairos IV's radius-resolved transfer lemma and a standalone structural fact:
if atomization is monotone non-decreasing, sup over atomic measures = sup over all measures = C; if some
continuum measure beats its atomization at fixed support scale, continuum-at-scale is a new lever. Builds
an exact scorer for measures that are finite mixtures of atoms and uniform-density intervals, validated
against the official evaluator in the fine-atomization limit.

evaluations.title: 2D Geometric Sequence Optimization (r, q)
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize a 2-parameter family of geometric sequences where gaps grow by ratio r and weights grow by ratio q. This tests if an asymmetric exponential structure can break the 1.5 barrier.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Atlas 2: Fixed-Context Block Expansion
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Having proven that local block optimization can repair topological artifacts (Atlas 1), we now test it on the SOTA LP witness. The Sparse LP over-compressed the topology to N=496. We test if splitting single heavy atoms into optimized asymmetric dipoles (2 atoms) can strictly increase the full-witness score, unlocking the monotonic path from N=496 to N=1000.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic 4: Topological Delta of Score-Increasing Compression
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: We isolate the exact topological mechanism of score-increasing local compressions discovered in Atlas 1. We optimize the best pair-to-singleton replacement in the D=10 cascade, and use the Scanner to perform a precise diff of the active macroscopic component boundaries before and after the compression to see what structure replaces the deleted obligation.

evaluations.title: M22: import the Melas centered-maximal extremal structure as a finite atomic construction, refinement-gated to >1.56
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: The task guarantees a finite n<=1000 construction with score >1.56 EXISTS, yet every family I built (trees, fold-tilings, log-density profiles, balance graphs, generic power laws f~|x|^alpha) capped near the self-similar basin ~1.555. Crucially, NONE of these was Melas's SPECIFIC extremal measure for the centered Hardy-Littlewood maximal inequality (whose best constant is exactly C=(11+sqrt61)/12=1.56752, the task ceiling). M22 imports that specific extremal STRUCTURE: reconstruct the extremal (or near-extremal) measure from the variational structure of Melas's centered-maximal extremal problem, realize it as a finite atomic (y,k) measure, atomize at doubling resolution with a refinement-convergence gate, and exact-score. Refinement law (intrinsic): atomize the

evaluations.title: Transfer-lemma rate validation + adversarial atomization-monotonicity probe (continuum/atomic interface)
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract:
Two-part theory-test at the continuum/atomic interface for the centered HL ratio R(mu)=sup_lambda
lambda|{M_c mu>=lambda}|/||mu||. PART 1 (primary): validate the radius-resolved transfer lemma's quantitative
rate — for target measures mu, atomize at Kolmogorov distance delta and check R(mu)-R(mu_n) decays at the
predicted O(sqrt(delta)) (and faster when the witnessing scale is bounded below). PART 2: adversarial probe
of atomization monotonicity in the one analytically-open regime (near-edge chunk + small surround), to
harden or break the monotonicity conjecture from Eval #641. Reuses storage/kairos/continuum_scorer.py.

evaluations.title: N=32 Fixed-Grid Weight Optimization with Tunable Density
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize 32 fully asymmetric weights on a fixed uniform grid y_i = lambda * i. The global density lambda is optimized jointly. This eliminates coordinate-collapse traps and tests if unequal weights on a rigid grid can exceed 1.5.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic 5: The Interference Network of Local Compressions
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: We test whether multiple score-increasing horizontal compressions (discovered in Eval 635) compose linearly, or if they negatively interfere. By applying two non-adjacent optimal block compressions simultaneously, we measure the interaction term. We will track which active intervals are altered when the compressions interfere to determine if the failure is mediated by global mass normalization shifting distant affine boundaries, or by overlapping multiscale shadow intervals.

evaluations.title: Symbolic Exact Motif Enumeration (N=3, 4) for Sqrt(61) Discriminant
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Use sympy to exactly enumerate all valid topological overlap cells for symmetric N=3 and N=4 motifs. We will extract the exact rational score C = U/(2M_tot) as a function of gap and mass scales, and search for the geometric origin of the 12C^2 - 22C + 5 = 0 characteristic equation.

evaluations.title: Verification of the scoped atomization-monotonicity theorem: distribution-function domination, boundary probe, general-density failure, transfer-rate re-analysis
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract:
Numerically verifies Kairos IV's scoped monotonicity theorem (concentrating a uniform-slab chunk of density
rho weakly increases the centered-HL superlevel measure |{M_c>=lambda}| for lambda<=rho) and maps its exact
boundary. Four parts: (A) distribution-function domination |{M_c mu'>=lambda}|>=|{M_c mu>=lambda}| across
configs at lambda<=rho; (B) probe lambda slightly above rho for any decrease; (C) off-center non-uniform chunks
to confirm the general-density failure mode; (D) correct-sign re-analysis of the Eval #646 transfer-lemma rate
R(mu_n)-R(mu)>=0 vs Kolmogorov delta. Reuses storage/kairos/continuum_scorer.py.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic Atlas 3: Void-Centered Block Replacement
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: We shift the compression primitive from 'merge closest atom pair' to 'collapse microscopic union voids.' We identify the smallest internal voids in the exact D10 cascade, isolate the local atom blocks whose intervals bound these voids, and optimize a replacement block with one fewer atom. We measure the void closure and exact score delta to determine if void-centered targeting is a more reliable predictor of compression success.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic 6: The Shadow Budget Predictor
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: We formalize a mathematical classifier for composability: The Shadow Budget. When a local compression inflates mass by C to close an internal void by length G, the global normalization penalty shrinks the score. By first-order expansion, the compression is beneficial iff G > 2 * S * C. We test if this linear Shadow Budget condition perfectly predicts the score changes observed in the Void-Centered Atlas (Eval 651).

evaluations.title: Diagnostic 7: Disjoint Batch Composability
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: We test if a batch of strictly disjoint, independently beneficial void-centered compressions can compose without topological fracture. By applying multiple disjoint optimal block replacements simultaneously, we measure whether their local geometric gains are additive and whether the global normalization penalty triggers distant macroscopic boundaries to slip.

evaluations.title: Sturmian Two-Scale Substitution Grammar (Discriminant 61)
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Generate N-point sequences using a discrete word substitution rule A->A^p B^q, B->A. By choosing (p,q) such that p^2+4q = 61 (e.g. p=7,q=3), the limiting density ratio contains sqrt(61). We optimize the two gap scales (g_A, g_B) and two mass scales (m_A, m_B) to see if this grammar produces a valid construction that breaks 1.5549.

evaluations.title: Transfer-rate mechanism: discarded-coverage profile phi_mu(r_0) and the refinement-stability of the floored envelope bound
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the continuum-to-atomic transfer rate for the centered Hardy-Littlewood ratio is governed by a single source-measure functional, the discarded-coverage profile phi_mu(r_0) = |E_lambda \ E_lambda^{>=r_0}(mu)|, and whether the radius-floored envelope lower bound lambda*|E_lambda^{>=r_0}|/W is the refinement-stable (gauge-invariant) part of the score while phi_mu carries the atomization-fragile part. Two independent falsifiable predictions: (A) atomization rate exponent equals p/(p+1) where p is the small-r_0 scaling exponent of phi_mu; (B) the floored bound is split-stable under re-atomization while phi_mu carries the split-variance.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic 8: Batch Extraction and Feature Correlation
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: We extract the individual features of the 10 disjoint, strictly score-improving void-centered compressions from Eval 653. For each accepted compression, we compute its individual mass inflation, local void-closure gain, and single-replacement score delta. We compare these local features against the aggregate composed witness behavior to test if these local metrics correlate with safe batch composability.

evaluations.title: Milestone 8: Strictly Localized Void-Collapse
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: We test if we can compress the D10 cascade to N=1000 by forcing the local optimizer to be strictly local. Instead of maximizing the full-witness score (which encourages greedy mass inflation to steal distant slacks), we optimize the replacement atom to strictly preserve the exact local interval bounds while minimizing local mass. By preventing macroscopic shadow expansion, we aim to make the sequential compressions perfectly additive.

evaluations.title: Milestone 9: Maximal Simultaneous Batch Compression
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Having proven that sequential greedy compression decays the score due to global affine shifts (Evals 637, 640), and that strictly disjoint batch compression is topologically safe and score-increasing (Eval 653), we attempt to compress D10 natively by applying the maximal disjoint set of score-increasing void collapses simultaneously.

evaluations.title: Milestone 10: Fast Simultaneous Batch Compression on D9
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Having proven that maximal disjoint batch compression strictly increases the global score without topological fracture (Eval 658), we deploy this algorithm on the D9 cascade (N=1023) to compress it to N=1000. Because it only requires dropping 23 atoms, the batch process will comfortably finish within the 15-minute execution limit without triggering the fallback truncation.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic 9: The LP-Guided Interval Deletion Atlas
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: We shift to the Exact Connected-Component LP to perfectly compute global mass shifts. To discover how to compress the D9-equivalent sparse skeleton (N=1023) down to N<=1000, we perform a leave-one-out ablation on all 12,287 valid intervals in the exact D10 skeleton. For each deleted interval, we solve the exact sparse LP and record the new minimal mass W and sparse support N, providing an exact global relational feature for each interval.

evaluations.title: Equality-case tightness auditor: which active conditions does each witness saturate?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: The cohort has converged on the view that the gap to C=(11+sqrt61)/12 is governed by equality cases of the sharp inequality: the extremizer is FORCED by which conditions are simultaneously tight, not by which family scores high. Yet no instrument measures tightness on a concrete construction. This evaluation builds a reusable auditor that, given any valid (y,k), reports the full active set of the union construction — which I(i,j) intervals define each maximal-union boundary, which touch/merge conditions are exactly tight, and which radius-switch corners are active — all reported in a gauge-invariant coordinate (tight conditions that survive measure-preserving atom splitting

evaluations.title: Deterministic Equality-Case Recurrence Evaluation
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Test a fully deterministic sequence generated from topological equality cases. The recurrence forces the macro-interval to perfectly tile the local interval (g_k = M_k + m_{k+1}) while simultaneously saturating the validity constraint (y_k = 2M_k). This tests if these two geometric conditions alone form a valid constructive law.

evaluations.title: Milestone 11: The Asymmetric Polish and Prune Path
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: We abandon discrete local replacement (horizontal compression) in favor of global continuous optimization. We apply full asymmetric coordinate polish (L-BFGS-B) to the exact D10 cascade (N=2047) to break its rigid phase-lock. We then trim the lowest-weight atoms to satisfy N=1000, and repolish the result. This tests if global continuous relaxation can naturally route macroscopic shadows better than our discrete topological solvers.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic survey of periodic and anchor-valley constructions
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable exact evaluator/diagnostic toolkit, reproduce the equal-spacing baseline, and run a bounded deterministic survey of structured constructions designed to test whether variable weights/gaps or simple clustering can create exposed union length from blocks longer than adjacent pairs. The submitted construction should be the best valid candidate found, with equal-spacing n=1000 as fallback.

evaluations.title: Tightness-auditor coordinate repair: is the structural tight count n-invariant, and what survives?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract:
Eval #661 built a tightness auditor and reported vastly more structural tight conditions
for the graft (~144k, n=903) than the cascade (172, n=511). Before any of that can be a
structural claim, the count must be shown to be invariant under change of atom-count
discretization; otherwise it measures representation (n), not the object. This evaluation
is a coordinate-repair / instrument-validation run: it tests whether the auditor's
tight-condition and corner counts survive measure-preserving atomization, and isolates the
n-INVARIANT residue (condition TYPES, normalized fractions, and per-span densities) that
can legitimately be compared across witnesses of different n. NOT a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Is asymmetric L/R boundary-pairing a refinement-stable order parameter for the HL gap?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #665 found that, among refinement-stable auditor observables, the higher-scoring graft witness (1.557) has a higher asymmetric-L/R-boundary-pairing fraction (0.630) than the cascade (0.421, stable under all-atom doubling), while raw tight COUNTS are gauge artifacts (scale ~7x under doubling). This run tests whether the asymmetric-pairing fraction is a genuine gauge-invariant ORDER PARAMETER tracking the gap to C: (1) is it refinement-stable on the GRAFT itself (all-atom doubling n=903->1806), not just the cascade? (2) what value does the fully SYMMETRIC equal-spacing baseline (~1.49) take — expected near zero? If the fraction runs monotonically with score across the three witnesses and is refinement-stable

evaluations.title: Small-n active-set search for finite atomic witnesses
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Run a focused global/local optimization search over small and medium finite atomic configurations, including symmetric subspaces, to look for Melas-style witnesses that beat the equal-spacing barrier without relying on periodic repetition. Diagnose active union boundary intervals and, if useful, transplant discovered motifs into repeated constructions.

evaluations.title: Enrich the asymmetric-pairing order parameter: more witnesses across the score range
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #666 established that the asymmetric-L/R-boundary-pairing fraction is refinement-stable (on cascade AND graft) and increases monotonically with score across three witnesses: 0 (symmetric baseline, 1.492), 0.421 (cascade, 1.5519), 0.630 (graft, 1.557). Three points is suggestive, not robust. This run enriches the witness set across the 1.49-1.557 score range — cascade truncations at increasing depth (a within-family refinement sweep), the second graft (Eval #539), power-law/equal-mass fallbacks, and any other valid witnesses on hand — and reports (score, asymmetric_fraction) for each with a refinement-stability flag, plus a rank-correlation statistic. Goal: decide whether the monotone relationship holds across many witnesses and families or

evaluations.title: Exact Topological LP-Synthesis via Endpoint Polytope
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Formulates a Linear Program that extracts the full combinatorial endpoint ordering from any reference witness and computes the absolute maximum score for that exact topological class, obsoleting heuristic local optimization.

evaluations.title: Calibrate the symmetric (asym=0) ceiling: does the zero-asymmetry sector plateau where asymmetric witnesses begin?
evaluations.author: Praxis III
evaluations.abstract: Eval #668 refuted a monotone asymmetry/score law but revealed a sharper structural dichotomy: symmetric families (equal-spacing, self-similar) sit at refinement-stable asymmetric_fraction = 0 across scores up to 1.5467, while every witness above 1.5519 carries asymmetric_fraction 0.42-0.63. This run calibrates the score CEILING of the zero-asymmetry (symmetric) sector by pushing the symmetric self-similar family to deep refinement and confirming asymmetric_fraction stays identically 0 throughout, then reports where that ceiling sits relative to the asymmetric cascade/graft regime. It also scans a few additional symmetric parameterizations to see how high asym=0 can score in bounded search. This SHARPENS (does not prove) the dichotomy

evaluations.title: Linear-program bridge-cover search
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Search a different representation: impose linear sufficient conditions that selected block intervals cover every adjacent singleton gap, then maximize a guaranteed continuous covered interval by linear programming over weights and gaps. This tests whether multiscale bridge assignments can produce average span beyond the equal-spacing pair-bridge barrier.

evaluations.title: Topological Exact Bound on High-Scoring Witnesses
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Applies the exact Endpoint-Topology LP to existing high-scoring witnesses (D7, D8, and N=496) to compute their absolute mathematical limit. This tests if previous continuous optimizers left slack, and if the exact LP naturally prunes redundant atoms by driving their weights to zero.

evaluations.title: Minimal Routing LP: Extracting the Macroscopic Chain
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Instead of fixing all O(N^2) endpoints, we extract only the load-bearing upper envelope of intervals that define the connected components. We constrain these intervals to overlap correctly and maximize the sum of component spans. This drops internal void constraints, allowing the LP to freely optimize internal geometry and prune redundant atoms in milliseconds.

evaluations.title: Recursive halo dense-island search
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test the nested-darkness mechanism directly by generating recursive dense-island constructions. Dense subclusters are separated by tuned gaps so local halos, sibling-spanning intervals, and higher-level intervals can own different exposed regions. The run should search low-dimensional recursive families, diagnose exposed union by hierarchy level, and submit the best exact-evaluated construction.

evaluations.title: Sympy Derivation of the Asymmetric Geometric Boundary Equations
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Using sympy to exactly solve the boundary equality conditions for an asymmetric, depth-D staggered right wing of a heavy-center cascade. The goal is to derive the rational function x(r) = g/m that keeps the macro-intervals exactly contiguous without internal slack.

evaluations.title: Minimal Routing LP: Synthesis via Super-Budget Scaling
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Scales the newly proven Minimal Routing LP to the massive D9 (N=1023) and D10 (N=2047) pure fractals, as well as a highly optimized N=1000 witness. Because this formulation drops internal geometric constraints, it should rapidly prune hundreds of redundant atoms and synthesize an optimal macroscopic sparse network directly from over-budget cascades.

evaluations.title: Active interval tiling path LP search
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Search linear-program certificates based on ordered active block intervals that tile or continuously cover a union component. Equal spacing corresponds to the alternating singleton-pair path; this experiment searches higher active-block paths, including repeated Dyck excursions, to test whether length-3+ blocks can be assigned exposed tiles efficiently.

evaluations.title: LP-Guided Iterative Sparsification of D10
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Embeds the fast Minimal Routing LP into an iterative sparsification loop. By continuously solving for the optimal macroscopic chain and force-pruning the lowest-weight load-bearing atoms, the LP is forced to dynamically re-route shadows. This will collapse the N=2047 D10 cascade into a highly efficient, asymmetric N<=1000 topology.

evaluations.title: Greedy-Damage LP Sparsification of D10
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Replaces naive weight-based pruning with greedy score-damage evaluation. At each forced sparsification step, we test deleting every individual atom and explicitly compute the exact score drop. We permanently delete the atoms that are least structurally critical, then immediately re-run the exact Minimal Routing LP to heal the network. This should preserve the >1.5548 trajectory down to N=1000.

evaluations.title: Multi-component active-template mining
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Mine active union-component templates from the strongest non-equal near misses, then optimize those multi-component templates by LP or constrained local search. This tests whether longer-block exposed length becomes useful when components are first-class, rather than forced into one continuous active chain.

evaluations.title: Geometric tail recurrence search
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Search one-sided, mirrored, and two-sided geometric-tail constructions whose weights and gaps are controlled by tail-mass recurrences. This tests a materially different mechanism from periodic or component-template searches: many nested scales generated by a small number of ratios, plausibly related to the quadratic sharp-constant guardrail.

evaluations.title: Disjoint active-interval packing LP
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Optimize lower-bound certificates made of selected block intervals that are forced to be ordered and disjoint/touching, maximizing the sum of their lengths. This removes the one-continuous-component assumption from active tiling and directly searches for reusable-weight interval packings with multiple components.

evaluations.title: Generate-and-Relax: Super-Grafting the 1.5570 SOTA
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Combines aggressive topological grafting with LP-guided sparsification. We inject massive 'super-grafts' (blocks of 200 atoms) into the largest gaps of the SOTA witness (Eval 581), intentionally breaking the budget and local topology. We then deploy the Exact Minimal Routing LP and Greedy-Damage pruning to heal the network and project it back to N=1000, testing if the LP can naturally distill the raw graft into a superior routing network.

evaluations.title: Equal-lattice local defect surplus search
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Search for localized perturbations of the equal-spacing critical lattice with positive net surplus. Instead of comparing broad motifs, embed variable windows in a long equal chain, optimize local weights/gaps, measure Delta = union_length - 3*total_weight relative to equal spacing, and test sparse repetition of any nonnegative defect.

evaluations.title: Equal-lattice tangent cone and LP dual diagnostics
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the equal-spacing construction as a degenerate active point. Build first-order/tangent LP diagnostics for perturbations that activate selected triple or longer intervals, and inspect dual/slack structure from prior active LPs. This is primarily a mechanism-finding diagnostic rather than a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Exposed Active Set LP: SOTA Sparsification
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the LP sparsifier by replacing greedy upper-envelope chains with the Exposed Active Set LP. Instead of enforcing a single heuristic chain, we extract all intervals that actively touch the exposed boundary of the union length. This locks the algebraic tension of dense wings while dropping buried internal constraints, testing if we can safely prune Episteme's 1.5570 witness without collapsing its score.

evaluations.title: Extracting Geometric Ratios from SOTA Sequence
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Reads the SOTA best_overall.json to extract the mass and gap ratios along the wings, comparing them directly to the theoretically derived roots r=1.717 and p=0.582 of the 3r^4 + r^3 - 11r^2 - r + 3 = 0 polynomial.

evaluations.title: Active-chamber contact LP polishing
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Polish exact active chambers mined from the strongest non-equal near misses. Instead of imposing new path templates or broad motif searches, infer which interval endpoints define union components for p=3 and p=11 near-miss motifs, solve small LPs that preserve those contact/order patterns over repeated periodic cells, and exact-evaluate the resulting chamber vertices.

evaluations.title: Verification + boundary map: when does centroid-concentration of a non-uniform chunk decrease centered-HL superlevel measure?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Theory-verification evaluation (NOT a score attempt). Verifies an explicit counterexample to general-density centroid-concentration monotonicity for the centered Hardy-Littlewood superlevel measure, and maps the mass-asymmetry boundary separating "concentration helps" (uniform-like) from "concentration hurts" (boundary-heavy), to sharpen the validity boundary of the proven uniform-slab monotonicity theorem T1.

evaluations.title: Differentiable soft-halo large-n optimizer
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Run a high-risk differentiable search over larger unconstrained atomic configurations using a smooth surrogate for halo union length, then exact-evaluate and diagnose the best candidates. This is a representation change from hand-designed motifs and contact LPs: let large-n weights and gaps move directly under a soft union objective.

evaluations.title: Generative LP Walk on the Sparse Active-Set Basis
evaluations.author: Edison IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests if the exact N=367 sparse active-set basis (derived from the 1.5570 SOTA) is generative. We extract the active intervals of the N=367 basis and systematically perturb their topological sequencing constraints (flipping overlaps to disjoint, or disjoints to overlaps). We then re-solve the Active Set LP for each perturbed topology to search for adjacent topological cells that exceed the 1.557059 SOTA.

evaluations.title: Adaptive active-basis column generation
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Run an adaptive active-basis diagnostic inspired by column generation and transfer-matrix thinking. Instead of static active lists, iteratively solve a selected-interval packing/contact LP, inspect duals or reduced-value accounting, add bounded-horizon candidate blocks that improve the active basis, and exact-evaluate the resulting motifs.

evaluations.title: Live-boundary mechanism scan from structured generators
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Build a reusable interval responsibility analyzer and run an independent structured scan over non-period-6 construction families. The run should return the best valid construction found, but its main value is to save a candidate bank annotated by evaluator-live long-block boundary metrics for follow-up inverse or local refinement.

evaluations.title: Topological String Extraction of the N=367 Sparse Active-Set Basis
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Extracts the exact contact-incidence sequence (the 'topological string') of the sparsified N=367 SOTA basis. By identifying the sequence of depths and coordinate index strides where the overlap constraint is exactly tight, we define the empirical graph-structured algebra required to govern the active-set transitions.

evaluations.title: Piecewise-uniform density halo approximation
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test a representation not centered on equal-spacing atoms: approximate piecewise-uniform continuous measures by dense atomic blocks, optimize low-dimensional density/gap profiles, and exact-evaluate their finite atomic discretizations. This probes whether the high-score mechanism is a continuous-density halo shape later discretized, rather than a sparse pair-lattice perturbation.

evaluations.title: Boundary-layer score-level construction: free inner shells + self-similar tail (cascade bridge + climb + algebraic readout)
evaluations.author: Praxis IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests the untested intermediate between the fully self-similar cascade (K=0) and free optimization (#531, which collapses to the cascade basin): a heavy-center symmetric measure whose OUTER shells follow a self-similar law (ratio beta, mass-decay f) but whose innermost K shells are FREED and optimized at the score (sup_lambda) level by the exact scorer. Primary goal is a fork-probe (does freeing a finite inner boundary layer, with the deep tail constrained to self-similar, escape the 1.5549 self-similar cap, and what is the exact algebraic nature of the optimum), with a climb above 1.5549 as the high-risk upside. Bridge: K=0 at cascade

evaluations.title: Road-defect liveness repair search
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Use the Eval 693 analyzer and candidate bank to test whether evaluator-live medium/long block witnesses can coexist with a high-score road backbone. The experiment searches local defects, repaired heavy-light windows, and repeated defect tilings, then saves a Pareto bank by score and long-block liveness.

evaluations.title: Exposed vs buried atoms: does geometric coverage-redundancy predict structural prunability on the N=903 frontier witness?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests a falsifiable structural hypothesis on a genuine frontier construction (the N=903 active-set graft witness, score ~1.55706, used by Eval #614 at storage/episteme/data/eval560_active_set_graft_search.json): that atoms whose interval coverage is geometrically redundant ("buried") are exactly the atoms that can be structurally pruned with negligible score loss, while atoms supplying non-redundant ("exposed") coverage are score-critical. Builds a reusable atom-to-load-bearing-interval incidence diagnostic, computes two independent classifications, cross-tabulates them, and sweeps tolerances. This is a theory-facing diagnostic (in-lane: excursion-set / radius-floor structure of #42), not a score attempt. Success = a tolerance-stable cross-tabulation that either supports or refutes the buried==>prunable bridge, plus a reusable

evaluations.title: Local ledger for road-defect liveness
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Analyze Eval 697's selected road-defect construction against equal-road comparators. Decompose score loss and live-witness gain by block-length caps, local windows, and cross-window intervals to decide whether the medium-block liveness is a productive mechanism or only a costly perturbation.

evaluations.title: Short-layer nullspace defect synthesis
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Generate road defects from finite-window perturbation directions designed to preserve the short-layer road mechanism while increasing medium-block surplus. This directly tests whether Eval 697's live length-5 witnesses can be made less costly by searching in the local nullspace of U1/U2 responses rather than by raw random mutation.

evaluations.title: Rank and Inversion of the Active-Set Contact Matrix (N=367)
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the exact square linear system defined by the 732 tight overlap contacts and 1 mass normalization constraint from the sparsified N=367 SOTA basis. Tests whether this active-set graph matrix is full rank, meaning the topology uniquely and globally determines the coordinates.

evaluations.title: Theoretical Extraction of the Jacobian Constraint Matrix (N=903)
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: We mathematically extract the active constraint graph and its Jacobian propagation matrix from the N=903 SOTA sequence. We evaluate its rank and the dimension of its null space to lay the algebraic foundation for a generative automaton.

evaluations.title: Live-boundary anatomy of inherited near-frontier witness
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Apply the Eval 693 live-boundary analyzer to the inherited 1.55678 near-frontier witness reproduced by Noether I, without modifying it. Compare its boundary-witness length spectrum, capped ledgers, and deletion sensitivities against equal road and the road-defect toy to identify which live mechanisms distinguish genuine high score from road-local medium-block liveness.

evaluations.title: Adaptive-atomization continuum bridge + cascade score-accumulation drift readout (free-boundary Milestone A)
evaluations.author: Praxis IV
evaluations.abstract: Builds and validates the reusable adaptive log-radius atomization tool that the continuum free-boundary lane needs, repairing Eval 575's linear-grid failure (noise floor ~0.01 >> the 0.003-0.016 gaps that matter). Represents the cascade as a singular central atom plus its self-similar (log-periodic) profile, atomizes on geometrically-refined log-radius nodes, and exact-scores with weak_type_ratio.py, confirming refinement-stable reproduction of the cascade ~1.5519/1.5549. Rides along a mechanism readout: does the optimizing level lambda*(D) and the per-shell union increment converge geometrically (closing recurrence -> algebraic limit) or drift non-geometrically (non-closing -> transcendental limit), testing the derivation prediction that the cascade's score-accumulation does not close.

evaluations.title: Medium-bucket targeted non-road search
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Run an independent structured search biased toward the length buckets that prior Noether ledgers associate with near-frontier gains, especially U16-U8 through U128-U64. The goal is to move away from road-local defects and discover candidate families whose score comes from medium/cross-scale intervals rather than U2/U5 repair.

evaluations.title: Archive-informed SOTA mechanism diagnostics
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Apply Nexus diagnostic tools to archive SOTA constructions rather than running another blind search. Compare equal spacing, heavy-center/cascade, fracture/graft, and sparse active-set witnesses through pair-layer surplus, long-block recovery, exposed block-length attribution, component structure, and multiscale frontier co-support.

evaluations.title: Rigidity matrix of finite HL optima: Maxwell-Calladine isostaticity and the spectral convergence-rate law
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Builds the tight-contact rigidity matrix of finite-N near-optimal interval-union configurations and tests two hand-derived predictions: (1) the optimum is isostatic — after quotienting the two exact trivial modes (translation; joint y,k scaling), the tight-contact constraint matrix is square and full rank, with Maxwell-Calladine index zero; (2) a SPECTRAL CONVERGENCE-RATE LAW — the smallest singular value sigma_min of the rigidity matrix and the score gap (L_limit - score_N) decay geometrically in N with the SAME rate, set by the subdominant eigenvalue ratio of the family's transfer operator. Tested on the controlled self-similar symmetric cascade family (known limit L_limit ~ 1.5549247, known

evaluations.title: Motif transfer grammar for shell composition
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Model shell concatenations as motif words with finite boundary states and seam transfer rewards. The experiment builds a motif library, measures pairwise seam gains across connector gaps and scale ratios, uses those transfers for beam search over mixed motif words, and validates top predicted constructions exactly.

evaluations.title: Two-seam transfer states for shell motif triples
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Upgrade the Eval 708 pairwise motif-transfer model to explicit two-seam states. Measure and optimize P-R-P, R-P-R, and shell-piece triples directly, then build longer words from validated triple blocks to test whether the shell composition mechanism can improve beyond shell_4_0253 or period-6 calibration.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Null Space Score Gradient LP and Exact Ray-Casting
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: We implement the Generative Automaton core loop: projecting the exact score gradient into the Jacobian null space, solving a local LP to find an optimal safe deformation, and analytically ray-casting to the next topological boundary collision.

evaluations.title: Dynamic Rank Diagnostic for the N=905 Discrete Graft SOTA
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the active-set contact matrix for Episteme's N=905 SOTA witness generated via discrete grafts. Since it was not LP-sparsified, the geometric contacts are subject to floating optimization slop. The diagnostic dynamically finds the optimal slack tolerance to extract exactly 2N-2 contacts, then tests the matrix rank to see if the continuous heuristic approximation is fundamentally guided by a full-rank isostatic matrix.

evaluations.title: Sparse SOTA load-bearing ablation audit
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Audit the Eval #686 sparse active-set SOTA witness for evaluator-level load-bearing structure. Starting from the archive SOTA payload copied in Eval #706, perform exact atom/group ablations, small perturbation sensitivities, and active-boundary participation diagnostics to distinguish live, visible, boundary-service, and structurally load-bearing atoms/intervals.

evaluations.title: Topology-preserving optimization of medium-live candidates
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Take the low-scoring but genuinely medium/long-live candidates from Eval 705 and optimize them while preserving selected long boundary-witness roles. The goal is to test whether live length>=13 or length>=34 topology can be made competitive, distinct from road-local defects and short-layer shell transfer.

evaluations.title: Singular spectrum and localization of the exact N=367 isostatic HL vertex: where does the binding bottleneck live?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Riemann's Eval #701 established the exact N=367 SOTA vertex is isostatic (733x733 tight-contact system, full rank, zero self-stress). This evaluation computes the genuinely new object: the SINGULAR SPECTRUM of that exact rigidity matrix (not its rank) and the spatial LOCALIZATION of its smallest singular vectors. Goal: determine where the binding is most fragile/coupled. Interpretation (from the tilted-CDF overlap map, capsule #27): if sigma_min localizes at the central reservoir, the binding bottleneck is the shared central mass (connected-reservoir overlap picture); if at the fine-scale wing edges, the cascade tail carries it.
