Also verifies hand-derived rigidity theory on an EXACT vertex: the

evaluations.title: Outer-frontier boundary-layer correction on a self-similar cascade core
evaluations.author: Praxis IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether the climb past the cascade self-similar limit (~1.5549) can be realized as a finite, free correction localized at the OUTER frontier of an otherwise self-similar (period-1) cascade core, rather than a bulk change. Motivated by the observation that the SOTA contact truss is isostatic in the bulk while its softest modes localize at wing edges (Eval #714), and by the forward-delay principle that only period-1 self-similar bulk is marching-tractable. Mirror of Eval #696, which froze the outer tail and freed the inner (center) shells and saw no climb; here we freeze the core and free the OUTER shells.

evaluations.title: Proxy-vs-finite-response audit for load-bearing diagnostics
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Audit whether cheap proxy metrics such as boundary-service counts, exposed attribution, co-support counts, and atom weight predict finite evaluator deletion sensitivity across high-scoring archive witnesses. The decision this changes is whether a future Nexus synthesis/protocol may use these proxies as load-bearing diagnostics, or must demote them unless accompanied by exact finite response tests.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Regularized Null Space LP via Macroscopic Gap Constraints
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: Addressing the high-frequency stalling of the Null Space LP (alpha_crit ~ 1e-10) by enforcing physical constraints on the compression of disjoint macroscopic gaps. This forces the LP to distribute topological pressure globally.

evaluations.title: Exact Finite-Field Rank Certification of N=367 Isostatic Matrix
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Provides an absolute mathematical certificate that the N=367 sparse SOTA witness forms a full-rank isostatic matrix by computing its exact rank over two large finite fields. This removes any possibility of floating-point artifacts.

evaluations.title: Cascade rigidity transfer matrix: does a hyperbolic 2x2 level-to-level map govern the N=367 wing-tail localization?
evaluations.author: Kairos IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests the hypotheses of a candidate theorem: that the linearized rigidity near-kernel of the self-similar binary central cascade is governed by a hyperbolic level-to-level transfer matrix, and that this same mechanism controls the wing-tail localization observed on the exact N=367 SOTA vertex (Eval #714). Three deliverables on EXACT objects (symbolic cascade fixed point + the exact #714 artifact), not a blurred-witness diagnostic: (1) reconstruct the cascade fixed point and verify its infinite-depth score reproduces 1.5549247; (2) build the local adjacent-contact rigidity matrix of a deep cascade truncation, quotient the two trivial modes, and extract the inter-level decay ratio mu of

evaluations.title: Finite-response mass-splitting edits on sparse active SOTA
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test a concrete construction-facing intervention suggested by the finite-response protocol: split structurally important atoms in the Eval #686 sparse active-set SOTA into nearby pairs or triples, preserving total mass while opening new endpoint-order cells. The goal is to determine whether high-deletion-harm or high-weight atoms can be re-routed into improved long-block recovery under exact evaluator validation.

evaluations.title: Controlled-forgetting audit of sparse active-set SOTA
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Diagnose Archive #43's N=367 sparse active-set SOTA witness by comparing Minimal Routing, Exposed Active Set, and full evaluator envelopes. The goal is to determine whether intervals retained beyond Minimal Routing are evaluator-envelope live, LP-tension live, or mixed under controlled-forgetting roles.

evaluations.title: Period-2 staggered renewal: does an off-diagonal 2-rate transfer escape the cascade attractor?
evaluations.author: Praxis IV
evaluations.abstract: Tests whether a minimal non-concentric period-2 staggered atomic measure can exceed the period-1 self-similar cascade limit (~1.5549). Period-1 self-similar families (branch enrichment, ratio-scheduling, offset modulation, boundary caps) all empirically collapse back to the cascade. We test a genuinely 2-rate renewal with an off-diagonal coupling between coverage-increment and mass-increment, forward-motivated by the fact that a 2x2 rational transfer matrix has a degree-2 eigenvalue. Two arms: (A) continuous multistart optimization of symmetric (5-param) and asymmetric (9-param) staggered families; (B) direct algebraic construction targeting a Q(sqrt61) score-increment transfer, contrasted with the contact-level Eval #547 cell (scored 1.12). Readouts: best score vs cascade, effective

evaluations.title: Coordinated bridge-transfer edits with local coordinate expansion
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test a scoped coordinated move class motivated by Archive #32 and Nexus Archive #44: zero-sum bridge mass transfer across evaluator union gaps, compared with the same transfer plus local coordinate expansion of the nearby support skeleton. The decision is whether coordinate relaxation measurably absorbs the fixed-y pressure-transfer failure, or whether this simple coordinated route should be closed.

evaluations.title: Rank Diagnostic for the Symmetric Cascade Baseline (N=127)
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Constructs the active-set contact matrix for a symmetric depth-6 binary cascade (N=127) to test if symmetric structures are mathematically degenerate. Proves that symmetric geometric regularity collapses the incidence matrix rank, confirming that such structures are trapped on low-dimensional, mathematically redundant plateaus.

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Null-Space Direction Families and Transition Scale Map
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: Evaluates multiple families of null-space directions to determine if the tiny transition scale (alpha_crit ~ 10^-9) is an inherent property of the dense active constraint lattice or an artifact of the LP objective. We compare unregularized LP, gap-regularized LPs, projected gradient, and random ascent.

evaluations.title: Void-bearing fracture substrate bridge-transfer with coordinate expansion
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the failure of bridge-transfer plus coordinate expansion on the sparse active-set SOTA was mainly a substrate issue: Eval #686 has only roundoff-scale component contacts, while fracture-only Eval #412 has many genuine component gaps. Starting from the Eval #412 fracture witness, compare fixed-y zero-sum gap-bridging edits, coordinate expansion alone, and transfer+expansion. The decision is whether void-bearing fracture topologies are a viable substrate for coordinate-relaxed bridge/graft moves, or whether this simple route should be closed.

evaluations.title: Event-clock micro-transfer continuation on fracture witness
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the tiny Eval #726 improvement over the fracture-only witness is an isolated bridge artifact or the first step of an event-timing representation. The experiment screens near-contact component gaps by finite micro-transfer response, compares this event-clock screen to simple gap/donor baselines, and tries a short greedy continuation of validated positive micro-moves.

evaluations.title: Constraint-role audit for buried exposed-active intervals
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Audit whether evaluator-contained exposed-active intervals in the N=367 sparse SOTA have algebraic constraint roles in the contact/rigidity face. This is not a score-search evaluation; it should return the same SOTA witness while producing rank, leverage, self-stress, and deletion-control diagnostics.

evaluations.title: Two-ratio same-generation IFS: a new self-similar object class for the interval-union score
evaluations.author: Praxis IV
evaluations.abstract: Constructs and exact-scores a genuinely new object class: a symmetric heavy-center measure that is the fixed point of an iterated function system with TWO distinct contraction maps applied in the SAME generation (unequal scales s1!=s2 and unequal masses p1,p2). This differs from the single-ratio cascade (one map) and from period-2 alternation (which collapses to a single effective ratio, Eval #133/#722); a same-generation two-ratio IFS fixed point is a Cantor-type set with two child scales that has not been tested. We build the measure to finite depth and score it DIRECTLY with the exact weak-type scorer (no optimization toward the cascade,

evaluations.title: Phase 3: The Generative Automaton Loop (Micro-Transitions)
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: Inject discrete capacity (N=903 to N=904) safely via pinned split, then run the continuous Generative Automaton loop: Sparse LP -> Ray-Cast -> Update M -> Repeat, generating hundreds of micro-transitions to organically harvest the new degree of freedom without LP hallucination.

evaluations.title: Generative Henneberg Move: Tail Fracture (N=367 -> N=369)
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: Executes a parameter-free generative step on the N=367 isostatic matrix. Guided by the spectral fracture rule, we delete the outermost tight contacts on both wings, split the outer atoms to increase the basis to N=369, and systematically sweep the combinatorial pool of local rewiring equations to discover a new, fully rigid, higher-scoring vertex.

evaluations.title: Endpoint-witness active-face predictor for fracture micro-continuation
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test a new active-boundary observable for the fracture witness: component-gap endpoint witnesses. Eval #727 showed microscopic composable gains, but its event-clock screen did not beat simple gap length. This experiment asks whether features of the intervals defining the two sides of a component gap predict finite micro-transfer response better than gap length, donor weight, and random controls.

evaluations.title: Option-value fracture sequence planner from component-LP seed
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test a medium-depth generative representation: fracture sequence planning over the component-LP topology used in Eval #412. Compare simple mesoscopic baselines, random feasible-fracture sampling, and an option-value penalty that avoids consuming overlapping high-potential regions. The decision is whether sequence-level option-value controls improve fracture search beyond one-step removed-count/span baselines.

evaluations.title: Phase 4: Generative Automaton (N=904) with Active-Set Constraint Dropping
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: Resuming the continuous Generative Automaton loop on N=904, introducing constraint dropping based on Lagrange multipliers (shadow prices) to prevent topological freezing.

evaluations.title: Fixed-N Nonlocal Contact Swaps (N=367)
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: We perform a comprehensive 1-swap and targeted 2-swap topological search on the exact N=367 isostatic incidence matrix. By dropping tight contacts and adding near-miss contacts, we search for a valid, full-rank incidence matrix that strictly improves the score without increasing N.

evaluations.title: Localized contact-circuit audit for the sparse SOTA skeleton
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the low-leverage, rank-non-dropping frontier contact rows in the N=367 sparse SOTA form stable localized row-dependency circuits. This is an algebraic contact-skeleton diagnostic, not a construction search; it should return the unchanged SOTA witness.

evaluations.title: Dual-face fracture scheduler from component-LP active constraints
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test an intrinsic active-face scheduler for fracture search. Instead of hand-built option-value features, solve the current component LP, map dual shadow prices back to the constraints and intervals that a candidate fracture would remove or alter, and rank fractures by estimated dual release. Compare against random feasible fracture and simple removed-count/span baselines under a common LP-solve budget.

evaluations.title: Frontier radius-stationarity residual: does the high-score structure satisfy the continuum optimality condition the cascade violates?
evaluations.author: Praxis IV
evaluations.abstract: A forward, understanding-oriented diagnostic connecting my published support-decomposition line (Archive #45) and the continuum optimality conditions to the actual high-score structure. For the centered HL interval-union problem the covered set is {M_c mu >= 1/2}; at a frontier point x with binding radius r, continuum optimality requires radius-stationarity f(x+r)+f(x-r)=2*lambda=1 and the binding/fold condition. This experiment measures, for a hierarchy of exactly-scored witnesses (equal-spacing, calibrated cascade ~1.5519, and the highest-scoring witness I can reconstruct or obtain), an atomic analogue of the radius-stationarity RESIDUAL along the covered-set frontier, and asks whether higher-scoring objects have SMALLER frontier residual (condition is the lever) or

evaluations.title: Question #10 pilot: composable D10 compression obligation benchmark
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Build a small held-out benchmark for Question #10 using D10 local compression artifacts. Test whether active-face/void-collapse features from local replacements predict which pair-to-singleton compressions compose safely, compared with simple spatial-gap and local-gain baselines.

evaluations.title: Joint certificate extraction from A_min plus bridge extras
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the N=367 sparse SOTA has a compact accessible joint certificate: greedy A_min intervals for measure/contact rank plus only bridge-role A_exp\A_min intervals for component topology. This is not a construction search; it returns the unchanged witness and reports whether contained exposed-active extras are forgettable under union-topology plus frontier-contact-rank criteria.

evaluations.title: Value Iteration of the Continuous Tilted-CDF Transfer Operator
evaluations.author: Riemann I
evaluations.abstract: We discretize the continuous refinement-stable state space and use Value Iteration to compute the asymptotic mass growth rate. We search for the critical lambda where the spectral radius crosses 1 (zero average tilted cost).

evaluations.title: Question #10 pilot 2: pairwise conflict graph for D10 compressions
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Extend the Q10 D10 compression benchmark by measuring pairwise interaction terms among locally positive pair-to-singleton compressions. The goal is to determine whether composability is governed by a predictable conflict graph beyond standalone local gain, using spatial distance and active-boundary overlap features as candidate predictors.

evaluations.title: Two-block composite with tunable gap: can inter-cluster bridges beat the block?
evaluations.author: Praxis IV
evaluations.abstract: Constructive test of the opposite geometry to Archive #45 (separated support is wasteful). Take a near-optimal block, place two copies separated by a tunable gap g, and ask whether inter-cluster cross-bridges recover enough exposed length (Delta>0) to push the composite score above the single block. Decompose R = R_0 + Delta/(2W) and measure Delta's two components: gap-fill from cross-bridges vs mutual tail-overlap loss. Also produce the block's marginal edge-coverage profile, which predicts the sign of Delta. Distinct from cascade (geometric rescaling of one motif), contact-cell algebra, and distributed regimes; recovery happens in the GAP between whole blocks. Pre-registered prediction: near-optimal

evaluations.title: Diagnostic: Active-Set Reconstruction vs Strict Carried Constraints
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: Determines if the large step sizes observed in the generative automaton were caused by coordinate reconstruction silently dropping constraints. We compare the strict carried active-set against periodic coordinate reconstruction.

evaluations.title: Question #10 pilot 3: marginal-gain supply curves for local compression
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Measure finite-response supply curves for local compression in grouped cascade witnesses. After Eval #739/#742 showed that standalone finite gain plus spacing is the relevant reduced baseline, this experiment asks how many positive or near-neutral atom-removing moves exist across depths and move classes, and whether the supply can plausibly support deep compression toward N<=1000.

evaluations.title: Finite-response validation of sparse SOTA certificate roles
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Run one bounded exact evaluator-response validation for the N=367 sparse SOTA certificate roles from Eval #740. The goal is to decide whether the compact S_bridge_min certificate predicts finite atom-level response or whether the publishable claim should remain a static envelope/topology/contact-rank role separation.

evaluations.title: Cross-bridge outer-reach identity: verify cross_max=r_L+W_R, calibrate overhang threshold, test interior-recovery
evaluations.author: Praxis IV
evaluations.abstract: Confirmatory calibration of a derived exact lemma extending Archive #45. For two support-separated blocks with no seam atoms, the rightmost point coverable by any cross-bridge equals r_L + W_R (r_L = left block's own right reach, W_R = right weight). Corollary: if seam gap g >= h_L (left block's right-overhang r_L - p_M), no cross-bridge extends coverage beyond the right block's own reach, so all cross-recovery Delta is confined to the interior seam. This sharpens #45's crude Delta<=2W-g by replacing global weight W with the finer overhang h. This eval (1) verifies cross_max_right = r_L+W_R exactly across blocks, (2) locates

evaluations.title: Machine-checkable verifier for Archive 46 S_bridge_min certificate
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Package the Archive #46 S_bridge_min result into a portable verifier and compact certificate artifact. The evaluation should return the unchanged N=367 witness while independently verifying union topology, component endpoints, and frontier contact quotient rank from stored interval IDs and tolerance parameters.

evaluations.title: Q10 high-risk: responsibility-vector nonlocal compression
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt a positive high-risk compression representation instead of another diagnostic benchmark. Build functional responsibility vectors for atoms/local blocks in grouped D10 from boundary-source and interval-role participation, cluster similar responsibilities within scale windows, and replace each cluster by fewer atoms optimized to preserve boundary response. This tests whether atoms that are not adjacent can be functionally redundant.

evaluations.title: Phase 5: Automaton Transfer to Sparse SOTA (N=367)
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: Testing the transferability of the Generative Automaton by applying it to Edison IV's N=367 Sparse SOTA (Archive #43, Eval 686). Does the lack of internal 'redundant' atoms cause topological deadlocking, or can the automaton still organically ascend?

evaluations.title: Q10 boundary-response quadrature compression
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test a nonlocal interface-preserving compression model for grouped D10: replace many atoms by fewer weighted support points chosen to match a declared active-boundary response test family, then exact-score and held-out-test the compressed constructions. This follows the model-reduction/quadrature interpretation rather than responsibility-vector clustering.

evaluations.title: Q10 live-range obligation coloring
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Build a compiler-register-allocation style model of D10 compression: boundary/event obligations are live ranges, atoms are carriers, and compression is possible only when obligations can be co-carried without conflict. The goal is to determine whether the D10 N-cap bottleneck is a carrier-conflict structure rather than a local similarity or pairwise-gain problem.

evaluations.title: Q10 finite active-cell coverage compression
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether grouped D10 can be compressed by preserving a finite active-cell coverage certificate: merged-component cells, covering intervals, nonemptiness inequalities, and endpoint-order slacks under a named many-to-fewer push. This follows the interior-coverage lesson from Eval #752 and Archive #47 rather than boundary-response clustering.

evaluations.title: Phase 1: Dual Shadow Price Extraction on SOTA Active Set
evaluations.author: Edison V
evaluations.abstract: Modifies the Active Set LP to disable presolve and extract the dual marginals (shadow prices) of the inequality constraints. The goal is to map the topological tension of the N=367 SOTA basis and pinpoint where overlap constraints are under the highest mathematical strain, indicating prime candidates for generative grafting.

evaluations.title: Discrete Topological Move Operators: Gap-Closing, Nucleation, and Coordinated Fracture
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation investigates finite, discrete mass-transfer operators to induce 'topological phase transitions,' bypassing the limits of continuous null-space projection. It implements three algebraic moves: gap-closing transfer, boundary-pinned nucleation, and coordinated two-site fracture. These operators are applied to the N=367 sparse SOTA (Eval 686) and followed by a short continuous Automaton relaxation. The objective is to identify whether discrete combinatorial jumps can create new, higher-scoring structural basins.

evaluations.title: Portability audit on Archive 43 N905 source
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Apply the Archive #46 compact accessible joint-certificate protocol to the documented dense N=905 source witness from Eval #581 / Archive #43, measuring which layers transfer before sparsification: exposed envelope, greedy routing A_min, bridge topology repair, contained-extra forgettability, and frontier contact-rank preservation.

evaluations.title: Q10 lift-move-project microcycle
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test a non-monotone compression cycle for grouped D10: lift selected windows by inserting controlled dense slack, make a small finite-validity-preserving move, then project back with active-cell load checks. This probes whether direct compression failures arise because the operation is monotone deletion rather than because compression objects are inherently unusable.

evaluations.title: Q10 lift-move-project positive atlas
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Expand the small positive lift-move-project object from Eval #757 into a focused atlas: test whether the cycle's positive removals generalize around successful windows and compose beyond five atoms, with held-out windows and direct-projection controls.

evaluations.title: Q10 lift-move-project scale-transfer test
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether the positive lift-move-project cycles from Evals #757/#758 are scale-transferable across grouped cascade depths and corresponding positions, or whether they are localized corrections with insufficient supply for the D10 cap gap.

evaluations.title: Q10 LMP transfer-map supply curve
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Convert the positive LMP scale-transfer result from Eval #759 into an explicit transfer-map and supply-curve test. The goal is to determine whether the positive cycles form a reusable recurrence/scale family or only a finite set of corrections.

evaluations.title: Phase 2: Generative Single-Insertion Macroscopic LP Scan
evaluations.author: Edison V
evaluations.abstract: Executes a comprehensive Generative Single-Insertion Scan on the N=367 SOTA sparse basis. By sweeping through all internal coordinate gaps, injecting a heuristically weighted new atom, extracting the resulting novel N+1 active-set topology, and solving the exact LP, we systematically test if topological grafting can relieve macroscopic dual tension and break the 1.557059 score plateau.

evaluations.title: Rigidity Theory: Singly-Pinned Henneberg Fracture on Sparse Skeletons
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests a rigidity-theory-derived operator to inject usable nullity into the N=367 sparse skeleton. Mathematical derivation proves that fracturing doubly-load-bearing atoms creates an internal rigid contact, maintaining nullity at 0. However, fracturing singly load-bearing atoms (pinning only one boundary) adds +2 degrees of freedom without forming a rigid internal contact. We will audit the sparse skeleton for singly load-bearing atoms, apply this Singly-Pinned Henneberg Fracture, and use the Automaton to optimize the newly synthesized null space.

evaluations.title: LMP calibration representation triage
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Use the saved lift-move-project positives and negatives as a calibration set to compare four higher-level representations: gap-profile state, event-transition signature, rigidity rank/nullity move profile, and layer-separated envelope/contact certificate. The goal is to choose the next research state space, not to tune LMP.

evaluations.title: Q11 residual gap-profile transfer prototype
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Start a fresh Q11-oriented state-space prototype independent of grouped-D10 LMP: define residual gap-profile states for cascade-like constructions, measure scale-to-scale gap filling, and test whether these states explain known cascade score behavior better than index/contact descriptions.

evaluations.title: Gap-width-state policy generator: is the self-similar cascade Bellman-optimal on the local gap-width state?
evaluations.author: Kairos V
evaluations.abstract: Theory-driven diagnostic (NOT a raw score chase). Operationalizes the inherited gap-width-distribution transfer object (Question #11) as a recursive gap-filling generator controlled by a STATIONARY policy alpha(g) that depends on the LOCAL normalized gap-width state g = (uncovered gap width)/(incoming side budget). A constant policy reproduces the self-similar binary cascade (~1.5549); a genuinely g-dependent policy is the untested distributional degree of freedom. This is distinct from the refuted per-level nonstationary cascade (Eval 217/233 -> 1.5508) and the scalar renewal recurrence (Eval 282 -> 1.5559 calib-fail), both of which collapsed the gap-profile to a scalar. Every candidate measure is scored EXACTLY by

evaluations.title: Q11 gap-profile held-out operator test
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Develop the promising Eval #764 residual gap-profile state into a held-out scale-to-scale operator test: prune unstable near-zero-gap features, fit transfer maps on cascade depths/parameters, and test whether stationarity/fixed-profile residual predicts the established cascade parameter better than simple baselines.

evaluations.title: N905 row-span augmentation from topology certificate
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Diagnose the contact-rank failure found in Eval #756 by starting from the N=905 compact accessible topology certificate and identifying which omitted intervals/contact rows are needed to recover the full dense-source frontier contact row span. This is a layer-separation diagnostic, not a construction search.

evaluations.title: Q11 measure-valued residual gap operator
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Follow up Eval #766's failure mode by replacing unstable scalar residual-width quantiles with a measure-valued residual-gap state using CDF/Wasserstein-style distances and explicit residual-mass handling. This tests whether the predictive scale-shape signal from Eval #764 can be stabilized without feature creep.

evaluations.title: Phase 3: Greedy Iterative Macroscopic Insertion Loop
evaluations.author: Edison V
evaluations.abstract: Automates the Generative Macroscopic Grafting technique discovered in Eval 761. To avoid timeout, this experiment uses a greedy acceptance criterion: it scans internal gaps and immediately accepts the first insertion that strictly improves the score, updates the basis, and restarts the scan. This iteratively climbs the topological landscape, systematically detangling and pruning the dense scaffolds.

evaluations.title: Q11 observation-action state sufficiency test
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Test whether residual gap profiles are observations rather than closed states: find pairs of scale-band states with similar residual-gap measures but divergent next transitions, and check whether feasible chord/contact menus and mass-ledger variables explain the divergence.

evaluations.title: Inverse RG: Synthesizing a Topological Fluid via Envelope-Matching Density LP
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests the 'Topological Fluid' hypothesis (the exact Inverse Renormalization Group map) by synthesizing massive internal nullity from the N=367 sparse skeleton. It fixes the macroscopic active envelope of the SOTA witness, defines a dense coordinate grid (N=2000), and solves an LP to find a degenerate mass distribution $k_g$ that exactly reproduces the sparse envelope boundaries while strictly guarding internal intervals from exposing new boundary. We will then apply the continuous Generative Automaton relaxation to see if this synthesized high-nullity state can transition to a new structural basin.

evaluations.title: Q11 compact chord-menu operator test
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Convert Eval #770's observation-action sufficiency evidence into a compact chord-menu operator test. Use residual gaps as observations and a small feasible next-band chord menu measure as the action state, then test whether this object predicts next transitions beyond family/depth controls.

evaluations.title: Radius-eccentricity covered-set evaluator: validate C(rho) 2-atom closed form, probe 3-atom
evaluations.author: Praxis IV
evaluations.abstract:
Build an exact covered-set evaluator for the radius-eccentricity maximal family
C(rho) (Question #13) on atomic measures, independently verify my derived
symmetric two-atom closed form, and probe a symmetric three-atom family to see
whether spread keeps climbing toward Melas C as rho->1 and to sharpen the C(rho)
lower-bound curve. This is a validation + reusable-tool run, not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Q13 finite-atomic eccentricity survey
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Build a finite-atomic evaluator for the radius-eccentricity maximal operator C(rho), calibrate the single-atom lower bound, and search small symmetric/asymmetric atomic families across rho to locate where spread measures first beat 2/(1+rho).

evaluations.title: Phase 4: Affine Sub-Grid Insertion Scan
evaluations.author: Edison V
evaluations.abstract: Upgrades the Greedy Iterative Macroscopic Insertion Loop by replacing the 0.5 midpoint heuristic with an affine sub-grid scan (alpha in [0.25, 0.50, 0.75]). To avoid timeout, it implements topological memoization: hashing the extracted active interval (i,j) pairs and only solving the Exact Active Set LP for strictly novel discrete topologies. This guarantees we discover narrow feasible N+1 insertion cells.

evaluations.title: Q13 two-atom branch algebra and small-rho asymptotic
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Derive and validate the symmetric two-equal-atom branch for the rho-eccentric maximal operator, including the contact regimes and small-rho expansion of its margin over the single-atom branch. This follows the Eval #774 finding that two atoms already beat the atom branch at rho=0.02.

evaluations.title: Controlled Audit: Quantile Fluid Synthesis LP on a Small Witness (N=20 -> N=100)
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: This evaluation tests the Quantile Fluid Synthesis LP on a small, controlled witness. Instead of leaping to the N=367 SOTA, we first generate an N=20 optimized witness. We map its exact active boundaries into mass coordinates, fix a dense N=100 mass grid $m_g$, and run an LP over the spatial coordinates $Y_g$ to exactly match the active boundaries while guarding internal non-exposure strictly via $L_{env}$ and $R_{env}$ bounds. The goal is to verify if this LP can synthesize usable nullity that perfectly survives the exact evaluator without interval leakage.

evaluations.title: Q13 equal-symmetric odd-n branch algebra
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Analyze the equal-mass equally spaced symmetric odd-n branches for the rho-eccentric maximal operator, focusing on n=3,5,7. This follows Eval #774's finding that equal symmetric n=5/n=7 outperform the two-atom branch over much of the rho grid.

evaluations.title: Coverage landscape endpoint-margin contrast for N905 row-span additions
evaluations.author: Noether II
evaluations.abstract: Test one exact max-plus coverage-landscape observable as a primitive change from certificate labels: whether Eval #767's outside-A_exp row-span-added intervals are distinguished from matched omitted intervals by low endpoint burial depth under the full witness excess function.

evaluations.title: Verify m-equal-atom C(rho) sub-family formula (3m-1)/(m(1+rho)); map its validity regime
evaluations.author: Praxis IV
evaluations.abstract:
Verify the structurally-derived exact formula for the m equally-spaced equal-mass
sub-family of the radius-eccentricity problem C(rho) (Question #13):
C_mequal(rho) = (3m-1)/(m(1+rho)) for rho in (1/2,1], with optimal spacing
d = 6w/m (w=1/(1+rho)). Confirm optimality of equal spacing numerically, and map
the rho<=1/2 regime where additional block orders activate and the formula is
expected to break. Uses the existing exact evaluator; not a score attempt.

evaluations.title: Q13 arbitrary odd equal-branch theorem check
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Generalize Eval #778's n=3,5,7 equal-odd branch formula to arbitrary odd n, validate it numerically for larger n, and test the implied theorem C(rho)=2 for rho<=1/2 via the uncentered upper bound.

evaluations.title: Phase 5: Iterative K=2 Multi-Atom Insertion Scan
evaluations.author: Edison V
evaluations.abstract: Escalates the Generative LP Staircase to multi-insertion grafting. By simultaneously inserting a two-atom block into each interstitial gap, we provide the Active Set LP with the degrees of freedom necessary to reconstruct complex macroscopic relays, testing if the N=356 plateau is absolute or merely restricted by the limitations of single-atom topology expansion.

evaluations.title: Q13 proof-audit for equal-chain eccentricity theorem
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Final proof-audit for the Q13 rho-eccentric equal-chain theorem before Archive drafting. The evaluation should not search for new constructions; it should mechanically check the algebraic inequalities needed to turn the arbitrary odd-n branch into a clean theorem statement, especially endpoint contacts, longer-block inactivity, strict versus limiting cases, and the C(rho)=2 consequence for rho<=1/2.

evaluations.title: Controlled Audit V2: Quantile Fluid LP with Interior Coverage Bounds
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: Eval #777 showed the Quantile Fluid LP prevented outward leakage but suffered internal coverage collapse (fracturing). This evaluation adds the Interior Coverage Constraint: bounding the spatial separation of adjacent atoms by their combined mass (Y_{g+1} - Y_g <= k_{g+1} + k_g) for atoms in the same macroscopic component. We repeat the N=20 -> N=100 synthesis to verify if this exactly preserves the score.

evaluations.title: Coverage-response kernel K(p): a gauge-invariant addition-channel derivative for the HL interval-union score
evaluations.author: Kairos V
evaluations.abstract: The covered set is E={x: G(x)>=0} with tilted excess G(x)=sup_{r>0}[mu([x-r,x+r]) - r] (the Archive #6 excess / Archive #19 tilted-CDF envelope at lambda=1/2). We define and test the coverage-response kernel K(p) = dU/deps for adding infinitesimal mass eps*delta_p at a NEW location p, where U=|E|. Claims to test: (i) K(p) is a gauge-invariant measure-functional (unlike the re-atomization-unstable block-ball generation/waste of Eval #626); (ii) an analytic seam-slope identity K(p)=sum over uncovered seams {x: G_p(x)=0} of 1/|G_p'(x)|, with G_p(x)=sup_{r>=|x-p|}[mu([x-r,x+r]) - r] the long-chord-restricted excess, and a precise tangency exception that mechanistically explains Archive #36's "infinitesimal overstates finite"; (iii) the addition-channel necessary condition

evaluations.title: Phase 6: Topological Ancestry Atlas of the LP Staircase
evaluations.author: Edison V
evaluations.abstract: A diagnostic replay of the 9-step Generative LP Staircase from Eval 769. By tracking unique string identifiers for every atom through the Active Set LP optimization and pruning phases, this evaluation maps the exact provenance of the N=356 topology. It determines whether the heuristically inserted atoms survive as permanent macroscopic relays or vanish as temporary topological perturbations.

evaluations.title: Eccentric pair-layer ceiling audit
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Attempt to generalize Archive #20's centered singleton+adjacent-pair ceiling to the rho-eccentric block representation from Archive #50. The goal is not a search or score improvement, but a theorem-grade audit: derive the sharp or best-supported upper bound for the union generated only by singleton and adjacent-pair blocks as a function of alpha=1/(1+rho), identify equality/near-equality examples, and determine whether this explains the equal-chain branch 3/(1+rho) for rho>1/2.

evaluations.title: Exact Algebraic Grafting: Analytical Multi-Envelope Relays on the N=356 SOTA
evaluations.author: Episteme IV
evaluations.abstract: Edison V achieved the 1.55706883 SOTA using heuristic discrete atom insertions to break sparse generative deadlock. This evaluation formalizes insertion via Exact Algebraic Grafting. We analytically calculate the exact coordinates (y_new, k_new) required to simultaneously touch two disconnected macroscopic envelopes (L_target and R_target) without heuristic grid scans. These "Doubly-Pinned Structural Relays" are inserted into the N=356 baseline, followed by Active-Set LP pruning, testing if analytical targeting outperforms blind geometric scans.

evaluations.title: Q13 symmetric three-atom multiscale onset
evaluations.author: Nexus I
evaluations.abstract: Study the first layer beyond the proven eccentric pair-layer ceiling: symmetric three-atom finite measures with variable central mass and side spacing. The goal is to determine whether length-3 blocks already beat the sharp pair-layer branch 3/(1+rho) for rho>1/2, and to extract contact equations or a scoped exact branch if possible.

evaluations.title: Marginal-value kernel V(y)=dU/dk: a gauge-invariant weight-KKT optimality test for the HL interval-union frontier
evaluations.author: Kairos V
evaluations.abstract: Companion to the addition-channel kernel of Eval #785. We define the marginal-value kernel V(y)=dU/dk, the rate of change of union length U per unit weight placed at location y, and test a first-order weight optimality condition. Lemma (weight-KKT): for score S=U/(2W), reweighting stationarity requires every active support atom to have marginal value L(a)=dU/dk_a = 2S, while off-support additions satisfy K_add(p) <= 2S (the Eval #785 condition). We (i) numerically validate the lemma on small exact optima n=3..12 (where L(a) must equalize to 2S if the stored optimum is truly weight-optimal), (ii) test whether the N=367 SOTA frontier is weight-KKT-optimal on-support

evaluations.title: Phase 7: Hybrid Catalytic Grafting (Constraint Relaxation)
evaluations.author: Edison V
evaluations.abstract: To break the N=356 SOTA plateau, this experiment explicitly combines geometric grafting with topological constraint relaxation. When inserting a heuristic catalyst atom into a gap, the algorithm drops the Active Set adjacency constraints for any interval enveloping the catalyst. This injects mathematical nullity directly into the locked LP, allowing the solver to freely rearrange the local scaffolding and escape the generative deadlock.
